0.title: INDIAN ARMY AND ASSAM RIFLES RESCUE OVER 500 CIVILIANS ON FLOOD RELIEF UNDER OP JALRAHAT-2
0.description: Troops of Indian Army and Assam Rifles continued extensive flood rescue operations across Imphal East…
0.text:
Troops of Indian Army and Assam Rifles continued extensive flood rescue operations across Imphal East and West on Day Two of Operation Jalrahat-II, rescuing over 500 civilians, including children and the elderly, from severely waterlogged areas such as Wangkhei, Heingang, Lamlong, Khurai, JNIMS, and Ahallup.

Ten flood relief teams, equipped with eight BAUTs, two inflatable boats, and supported by three BAUTs from the Indian Army, were deployed for the rescue operations. Troops also undertook emergency repairs of the breached Iril River boundary wall near Arapti Lamkhai in Lilong, Thoubal District, to control further flooding. At JNIMS hospital, boats were used to ferry stranded patients to safety.

Nearly 800 bottles of drinking water and other essential supplies were distributed to displaced families across relief zones.

Indian Army and Assam Rifles continue to operate in close coordination with civil authorities to reach affected communities and provide all support.

1.title: 10th Capt (Late) N Kenguruse, Mahavir Chakra Memorial Football Tournament 2026 | Akashvani News
1.text:
In Nagaland, the 10th Edition of the Capt (Late) N Kenguruse, Mahavir Chakra Memorial Football Tournament 2026-27 will be held from November 2 to 10. The tournament will be conducted under the aegis of Spear Corps and Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (North), in collaboration with the Nagaland Football Association and supported by the Kohima District Football Association and Chümoukedima District Football Association.

A total of 20 teams are expected to participate, divided into four pools of five teams each. Matches will be played at Indira Gandhi Stadium, Kohima, and Chümoukedima Football Stadium. The tournament carries a total prize pool of 8.69 lakh rupees. Registrations will open today and close at 08:00 PM on 30 September. The tournament will culminate with the closing ceremony on November 10. The milestone edition seeks to celebrate football, inspire young talent and carry forward the values of courage, dedication and sportsmanship associated with the late Captain N. Kenguruse.

2.title: Matthew VanDyke’s family seeks US intervention over detention in Delhi’s Tihar Jail

2.text:
VanDykeâs family alleges he has been held in solitary confinement and denied basic rights, as his lawyers cite a 14-kg weight loss during custody

The family of American mercenary Matthew VanDyke has urged the US Department of State to intervene, alleging that he is being held in solitary confinement and denied basic detainee rights at Delhiâs high-security Tihar Jail.

"The family of Matthew VanDyke seeks urgent US diplomatic intervention as Matthew VanDyke is presently still denied basic detainee rights, and is being kept in solitary confinement at Tihar Jail 8/9 in Delhi, India. It is time to bring Matthew VanDyke back home," the family of the former mercenary and prisoner of war (PoW) posted from his verified X handle.

VanDyke, 47, has been lodged in Tihar Jail 8/9 since April 2026. He was arrested by Indiaâs National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March along with several foreign nationals and charged under Section 18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), which deals with conspiracy linked to terrorist activities.

Indian authorities allege that VanDyke provided tactical military and drone training to armed groups operating along the India-Myanmar border. His family and legal team have rejected the allegations.

Family raises concerns over treatment

VanDykeâs family said his physical condition has deteriorated during his time in custody and accused authorities of restricting his access to basic facilities and regular contact with his family.

The family is also seeking greater US consular involvement and intervention over his conditions in prison.

A Delhi court has since directed Tihar Jail authorities to provide him with a specialised vegetarian diet, access to a cook under supervision, an electric kettle and protection from mosquitoes.

3.title: Assam to set up Anti-Narcotics Task Force to combat drug menace: Himanta Biswa Sarma
3.description: Himanta Biswa Sarma said Assam will set up an Anti-Narcotics Task Force within the police next month. The move is aimed at tightening NDPS enforcement, tracking cartel finances and blocking regional transit routes.
3.text:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on September 3 announced that a new Anti-Narcotics Task Force will be established within the Assam Police to strengthen the fight against the state's growing drug menace.

Speaking at a press conference after the conclusion of the two-day SSP Conference in Dergaon, Sarma said the new force is expected to be constituted within the next month and will focus on stronger enforcement of the NDPS Act.

According to the Chief Minister, the task force will have specialised verticals, including legal and financial units, to address issues such as bail granted to accused persons and the financial networks supporting drug cartels.

Sarma said Assam has also made progress in its conviction rate in chargesheeted cases, which has increased from around 7 per cent in 2020 to 29.3 per cent currently. The state government is targeting a 35 per cent conviction rate by the end of this year.

He further said chargesheets are currently being filed within the stipulated period in around 80 per cent of registered cases.

The two-day SSP conference also discussed the movement of narcotics through the Northeast. Sarma said Assam Police would need to coordinate with Mizoram, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh to effectively block the transit routes used for transporting drugs.

The conference also decided to establish two new battalions within Assam Police. Sarma said promotions that had been pending in the police department would now be taken forward, creating additional posts for recruitment.

The Chief Minister announced that 5,000 personnel will be recruited into Assam Police next year. He added that around 21,000 youths have been recruited into the police force over the past five years, while the government aims to recruit another 15,000–20,000 personnel during the current term.

Maintaining law and order was identified as a key priority during the conference, with Sarma stressing that it should not be compromised.

Several other decisions were also taken to strengthen Assam Police, including measures to improve forensic science capabilities, the prosecution system and disaster-response mechanisms. One of the new battalions will also be tasked with strengthening security at Oil India Limited and ONGC installations, while another will support disaster-response operations.

The Chief Minister also reviewed infrastructure development at the Lachit Barphukan Police Academy (LBPA) in Dergaon, where the SSP conference was held.

The first phase of the Academy's development, including the academic building and police museum, has already been completed. The second phase, estimated at over Rs 200 crore, is underway and includes barracks for around 1,500 trainees, hostels for officers and residential quarters for officers, trainers and other staff.

Planning for the third phase has also begun. Sarma called for the Academy to be developed into a world-class police training institution with modern infrastructure meeting high national standards.

He also directed officials to keep the portion of the Academy campus adjoining the National Highway open to ensure greater visibility of the institution. The Chief Minister further called for the police museum to be developed with an aesthetically appealing and professionally curated design.

Sarma suggested adding another barrack with capacity for around 1,000 personnel under the third phase and directed officials to study training facilities at the Assam Regimental Centre in Shillong and other Indian Army training establishments to adopt suitable best practices.

The review meeting was attended by Chief Secretary Ravi Kota, DGP Harmeet Singh and other senior officials.

The Chief Minister also reviewed the functioning of the newly established Smart Response Unit, which has been set up within Assam Police to ensure a swift response to crisis situations.

The next SSP conference is scheduled to be held in Bongaigaon in February next year.

4.title: Arunachal: Landslide blocks Zemithang-Tawang road
4.description: A landslide has blocked the Zemithang-Tawang road near Shakti village in Arunachal Pradesh’s Tawang district, disrupting connectivity.
4.text: Tezpur: A landslide has blocked the Zemithang-Tawang road near Shakti village in Arunachal Pradesh’s Tawang district, disrupting connectivity in the remote border region. The blockage occurred on the road linking Zemithang with Tawang, near the India-China border. Details on the extent of the landslide, its impact on vehicular movement and restoration efforts were not immediately available. Shakti is a remote border village in the Zemithang circle, inhabited by local communities as well as yak-grazing communities. The area lies in the strategically sensitive frontier region. The Indian Army conducts medical and civic action camps in Shakti and neighbouring areas, providing healthcare and other assistance to residents and pastoral communities. Road connectivity in Tawang and adjoining frontier areas is important for civilian movement as well as logistical access. Heavy rainfall-triggered landslides have previously disrupted key road links in the region, with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) carrying out clearance and restoration work. 5.title: Manipur Police, Assam Rifles arrest four insurgents in Chandel
5.description: Manipur Police and Assam Rifles arrested four insurgents during a joint search operation in Chandel district. Police said the men were linked to two insurgent groups and were carrying mobile phones and cash.
5.text:
Manipur Police and Assam Rifles arrested four insurgents during a joint search operation in Chandel district on September 1, police said.

The operation was conducted near Border Pillar 59 in the general area of Aivomjang village under Molcham police station.

Those arrested were identified as Thiyam Jotiraj Singh, 19, from Moirang Thana Leikai in Bishnupur district; Oinam Benarji Singh, 18, from Charangpat Mamang Leikai in Thoubal district; Huidrom Rajesh Singh, 28, from Moirang Ngangkhalawai; and Khundongbam Lemba Singh, 31, from Heirok Part-I in Thoubal district.

According to the police, three of the arrested men are suspected members of the United National Liberation Front (K) while Oinam Benarji Singh is suspected to be associated with the People's Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (Progressive).

Police said mobile phones, 12,115 Myanmar kyat and Rs 10 in Indian currency were recovered from the four men.

6.title: 4 militants arrested from India-Myanmar border in Manipur
6.description: IMPHAL: Security forces arrested four militants belonging to various banned outfits from the India-Myanmar border area in Manipur's Chandel district, police sai
6.text:
The four were apprehended by a joint team of the Assam Rifles and the Manipur Police on Tuesday during a search operation based on continuous surveillance and credible intelligence in the vicinity of Border Pillar 59 at Aivomjang village, a senior officer said.

The four armed militants - three members of the proscribed United National Liberation Front (Koireng) and one cadre of the outlawed Prepak - entered into Indian territory, and their bid to flee back towards Myanmar was thwarted, an Assam Rifles statement said.

The four militants were subsequently handed over to the Molcham Police Station for further legal proceedings, it said.

7.title: Lt Gen Harpal Singh Reviews Critical Frontier Connectivity Projects in Northeast
7.description: Lieutenant General Harpal Singh, AVSM, VSM, Director General Border Roads (DGBR), undertook a two-day visit to Border Roads Organisation (BRO) Projects
7.text:
Lieutenant General Harpal Singh, AVSM, VSM, Director General Border Roads (DGBR), undertook a two-day visit to Border Roads Organisation (BRO) Projects Brahmank and Arunank from September 2 to 3, 2026, reviewing critical road and connectivity works being executed in the remote frontier areas of the Northeast.

The visit focused on assessing the progress and implementation of strategically important infrastructure projects in some of the most challenging and remote areas of the region. Connectivity in these frontier areas has wider implications for operational preparedness, mobility and access, particularly where difficult terrain and demanding weather conditions can complicate the movement of personnel, equipment and essential supplies.

During the visit, Lt Gen Harpal Singh interacted with BRO Karmayogis engaged in the execution of these projects and appreciated their dedication, professionalism and resilience while working under demanding conditions. The interaction highlighted the important role played by BRO personnel in developing infrastructure in remote and difficult-to-access areas, where construction activity often requires sustained effort and adaptability.

The DGBR emphasised the importance of timely execution of projects while maintaining high standards of construction quality. The twin priorities are particularly significant for infrastructure being developed in frontier regions, where delays or deficiencies can affect the broader objective of strengthening connectivity and ensuring reliable access.

The projects under Brahmank and Arunank form part of BRO’s continuing infrastructure efforts in the Northeast, an area where road connectivity remains central to both development and strategic mobility. Improved road networks can facilitate movement between remote areas while also supporting the accessibility and integration of frontier communities.

For the Armed Forces, reliable connectivity is closely linked with operational preparedness. Roads and associated infrastructure provide the physical network required for movement and sustainment, enabling personnel and resources to reach remote locations more efficiently. In areas characterised by difficult terrain, dependable connectivity can assume even greater importance during periods of adverse weather.

Lt Gen Harpal Singh’s emphasis on all-weather access therefore underlines the need for infrastructure that remains dependable throughout the year rather than functioning only during favourable conditions. Such connectivity can improve the resilience of movement networks and contribute to sustained access to remote areas.

The DGBR’s visit also placed emphasis on the human element behind the infrastructure effort. BRO Karmayogis routinely work in demanding environments, and their dedication remains central to the organisation’s ability to execute projects in challenging terrain. Recognition of their professionalism and resilience reinforces the importance of maintaining high standards of commitment alongside engineering and construction excellence.

The Northeast has emerged as an important focus of India’s infrastructure development efforts, with improved connectivity intended to support remote communities while strengthening strategic mobility. Road construction in such areas is consequently not merely an infrastructure exercise but part of a broader effort to improve accessibility, resilience and integration.

Projects Brahmank and Arunank are being executed against this backdrop, with their work contributing to the wider connectivity architecture of the region. The DGBR’s review provided an opportunity to assess ongoing efforts while reiterating the organisational priorities of timely completion, quality construction and dependable access.

The visit also reflects the BRO’s continuing role in supporting India’s infrastructure requirements along challenging frontier areas. Its personnel operate in environments where terrain, distance and weather can significantly increase the complexity of construction and maintenance. Maintaining momentum under such conditions requires technical competence, logistical planning and sustained commitment from the workforce.

By stressing timely execution and quality, Lt Gen Harpal Singh reinforced the need to balance speed with durability. Infrastructure intended to serve remote frontier areas must not only be completed within planned timelines but also deliver dependable performance over the long term.

The DGBR’s review of Projects Brahmank and Arunank ultimately highlighted the strategic importance of connectivity in the Northeast. As India continues to strengthen infrastructure in remote frontier areas, all-weather roads and resilient connectivity networks will remain important enablers of operational preparedness, regional accessibility and national development.

The visit reaffirmed BRO’s commitment to delivering quality infrastructure in demanding environments and recognised the Karmayogis whose sustained efforts make such projects possible. Through timely execution, engineering quality and improved access, these infrastructure initiatives are aimed at strengthening connectivity in some of the country’s most challenging frontier regions.

9.title: India, China Corps Commanders To Meet Soon Amid Arunachal Friction: Report
9.description: India and China are expected to hold Corps Commander-level talks in the coming days, following reports of tension in the Taksing area of Arunachal Pra
9.text:
India and China are expected to hold Corps Commander-level talks in the coming days, following reports of tension in the Taksing area of Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri district.

The Indian Express reported that Lt General Girish Kalia, who heads the Army's III Corps, will shortly meet his Chinese counterpart along with other officers. The formation, known as the Spear Corps and headquartered at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland, oversees operations in Nagaland, Manipur and the central and eastern stretches of Arunachal Pradesh along the Line of Actual Control.

Local commanders from the two sides have met several times in recent weeks in an effort to settle the issues.

Army chief General Dhiraj Seth visited the Spear Corps earlier this week to "review the operational readiness of all formations and ongoing border development initiatives," the Army said in a post on X, adding that he was briefed on capability development and steps taken to strengthen combat capability.

The military engagement follows the 25 August meeting in Beijing between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, the special representatives for the boundary question.

A day later, the two countries said they would take forward discussions on "an early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation and border management.

They also agreed on two fresh military hotlines in the eastern and middle sectors, two additional meeting points for commander-level talks, and holding the trans-border river meeting in September.

The hotlines are likely to be located at the Army command headquarters in Lucknow and Kolkata. A Border Personnel Meeting point will come up at Joshimath in Uttarakhand, adding to those at Tawang and Chushul.

Xi Jinping is expected in New Delhi for the BRICS summit on 12-13 September. Relations have been strained since the 2020 eastern Ladakh standoff. Xi last visited India in October 2019 for the Mamallapuram summit.

10.title: After Nepal flash flood, 16 glacial lakes in Sikkim identified at highest risk of outburst
10.description: The eastern Himalayan state of Sikkim has identified 40 high-hazard glacial lakes, with 16 of them classified as being at the highest risk of catastrophic outbursts that could threaten downstream settlements.
10.text:
The eastern Himalayan state of Sikkim has identified 40 high-hazard glacial lakes, with 16 of them classified as being at the highest risk of catastrophic outbursts that could threaten downstream settlements.

The data is significant as it comes against the backdrop of the recent flash flood in Nepal, triggered by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 that left a trail of destruction with hundreds of people dead and scores missing.

Advertisement

Though the catastrophe was not linked to a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF), the flash flood has highlighted a broader transformation across the Himalayas as glaciers retreat, new lakes are forming in their place, while existing ones are expanding.

Advertisement

Glacial lakes are formed by the melting of glaciers and accumulation of meltwater in depressions on or near the glacier’s surface. GLOFs occur when these lakes suddenly burst open due to factors such as excessive water accumulation or triggers like earthquakes.

These floods can cause significant destruction and pose serious risks to people and the environment downstream.

Advertisement

One such outburst in Sikkim in October 2023 resulted in at least 60 fatalities and extensive damage in the Mangan, Gangtok, Pakyong and Namchi districts. It also destroyed the Chungthang dam, a crucial part of a major hydropower project.

At a media sensitisation workshop on GLOF Risk Mitigation held here on Thursday, Principal Secretary Sandeep Tambe said remote sensing and satellite imagery were being used to monitor changes in glacial lakes.

Of the 40 high-hazard lakes, 16 are in Category A (highest risk), two in Category B (high risk) and nine in Category C (moderate to low risk), while 13 remain unclassified, he said.

The workshop focused on strengthening public understanding of GLOF risks and ensuring that verified, science-based information reaches the public.

Yougan Tamang, the press secretary to Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang, said media sensitisation was crucial to communicating the scientific measures being undertaken to mitigate GLOF risks.

Sikkim’s Department of Science and Technology was designated the nodal department for GLOF hazard assessment and mitigation studies in February 2025, with the work being carried out through an interdisciplinary approach, Tamang said.

The state is also working towards what could be the country’s first dedicated GLOF Risk Mitigation Protocol, aimed at creating a standardised scientific framework for assessing, preparing for and mitigating glacial flood risks.

It could also serve as a model for other Himalayan regions, an official release said.

Field studies cover water-level and discharge monitoring, Electrical Resistivity Tomography, geophysical and differential global positioning system surveys, bathymetry, flood modelling, hazard assessment and feasibility studies for lowering lake levels and constructing flood-retention structures.

Tambe said a uniform strategy could not be applied to all lakes, and separate proposals had therefore been prepared for the Lhonak Complex, Shako Chho Lake and Gurudongmar Complex, according to the release.

The Sikkim government has identified Shako Chho as most vulnerable to GLOF.

The Detailed Project Report (DPR) for Shako Chho has been submitted to the National Disaster Management Authority, and a preliminary project report has been sent to the Jal Shakti Ministry.

The Central Water Commission is preparing a DPR along with the Sikkim government for a flood-retention structure at Dolma Sampa near Muguthang in the Lhonak Complex.

For the Gurudongmar Complex, a moraine plug wall at the lake outlet has been proposed. The Department of Science and Technology and Brahmaputra Board are jointly working on the proposal, taking into account both GLOF risk and the lake’s cultural and religious significance.

The Science and Technology Department’s principal director-cum-secretary D G Shrestha said Sikkim’s devastating 2023 GLOF had underscored the urgency of strengthening preparedness.

At the policy level, Sikkim is pursuing a whole-of-government approach, clearer business rules, measures to bridge technical expertise gaps and a proposal for a commission on glacial hazards.

Various lake-level lowering techniques are being examined, including siphoning, pumping, improving existing channels, artificial channels, moraine cutting with safety walls and tunnelling.

Shrestha outlined a four-stage mitigation process—preliminary assessment, comprehensive assessment, designing mitigation measures and execution—and stressed the need to strengthen institutional, technical and financial capacity.

He also said additional early-warning sensors had been proposed across Sikkim following a virtual meeting with Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, who gave a positive assurance on the proposal.

On Thursday, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan reviewed the preparedness of Himalayan states and Union Territories in dealing with GLOF risks and snow avalanches.

The chief secretaries and State Disaster Management Authorities of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir, along with senior officers of the Ministry of Home Affairs, National Disaster Management Authority, Central Water Commission, India Meteorological Department and the Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment attended the meeting.

11.title: India, China Corps Commander Talks In Northeast Soon, Military Hotlines Planned - India Today
11.description: India and China are set to hold Corps Commander-level talks in the Northeast soon, amid reports of tension in Daksing. The Spear Corps Commander is likely to lead the Indian side in the discussions. The two countries are also planning new military hotlines to link the Indian Army's Eastern and Central Commands with China to prevent border escalations. This development follows boundary talks between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing, where both sides agreed to strengthen mechanisms to ensure peace along the border regions.
11.text: A massive flood disaster has struck the Nepal-Tibet border region, causing widespread destruction. China has officially released casualty figures for the first time following the catastrophe, confirming 31 recovered bodies and 531 people missing on its side. The devastation severely impacted the town of Gyarang, where an immigration building was destroyed. Around 2,500 to 3,000 individuals, including Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, business travelers, and container drivers, were present in the area during the incident. Rescue operations remain ongoing on the Chinese side, with authorities stating that further information and updates will be shared as more bodies are recovered from the disaster zone.

13.title: NorthEast United FC unveil new-season jersey in Mumbai
13.description: NorthEast United FC unveiled their new-season jersey at an event in Mumbai on Saturday.
13.text:
Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 5 (ANI): NorthEast United FC unveiled their new-season jersey at an event in Mumbai on Saturday.

Aryaman Vikram Birla, Director of the Aditya Birla Group and Non-Executive Director of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), joined NorthEast United FC Co-Owner John Abraham to unveil the jersey, marking a new phase in the partnership, according to a press release.

Aryaman Vikram Birla, Director, Aditya Birla Group, commented, “Sport is entering a defining phase in India, and sportswear is emerging as one of the most exciting opportunities within fashion and lifestyle. Reebok is uniquely positioned at the intersection of these trends, combining an authentic sporting heritage with the ability to connect with a new generation of consumers, making it one of the fastest-growing brands in our fashion portfolio. Our partnership with NorthEast United FC is a natural extension of that vision, bringing together an iconic sports brand and one of India’s most passionate football communities."

Reebok, the iconic global athletic footwear and apparel brand, is making its return to competitive football sponsorship in India. The brand unveiled NorthEast United FC’s new-season jersey, marking a renewed association with the sport and signalling a fresh chapter in its football journey in the country.

This partnership marks a new sports era for Reebok in India and mirrors Reebok’s global playbook: building credibility on the field and showing up in spaces that resonate with each region’s sporting culture.



John Abraham, co-owner of NorthEast United FC, stated, “Reebok's sporting heritage speaks for itself, and this partnership with NorthEast United FC is a special moment for us. This partnership reflects the ambition we have for the club, both on and off the pitch, and we're excited about the opportunities this creates for football in the region.”

Arjun Ramamoorthy, Brand Head, Reebok India, added, “This partnership is about building Reebok’s relevance through sport, with a clear focus on where consumers are engaging and where the brand can add value. Football gives us an authentic platform to engage with a new generation of consumers, while NorthEast United FC provides a strong cultural and sporting connection.”

Mandar Tamhane, CEO, NorthEast United FC, added, “This partnership is a reflection of where NorthEast United FC is heading. We have always believed that the Northeast has the talent, passion and culture to make a much bigger mark on Indian football. Reebok and Aditya Birla Group share that belief, and together we have an opportunity to connect that footballing identity with a new generation while continuing to raise the standards for the club and the region.”

Reebok has a long-standing association with sport in India, having outfitted athletes and teams across cricket, football and running over the decades. The two-time Durand Cup winner NorthEast United FC (NEUFC), representing all eight states of Northeast India, has played a key role in bringing the region's rich footballing culture and talent to the forefront of Indian football.

Aryaman Vikram Birla and John Abraham were joined by key members of the NorthEast United FC squad, including Mandar Tamhane, Gurmeet Singh, Buanthanglun Samte, Redeem Tlang and Lalrinzuala Lalbiaknia, as the club unveiled its new Reebok jersey. (ANI)

14.description: Reebok the iconic global athletic apparel company, is back on the pitch the brand unveiled NorthEast United FC’s new jersey today in Mumbai
14.text:
Reebok Returns to Sport with NorthEast United FC Partnership

Reebok, the iconic global athletic footwear and apparel company, is back on the pitch. This partnership marks a new sports era for Reebok in India and mirrors Reebok’s global playbook: building credibility on the field, and showing up in spaces that resonate with each region’s sporting culture.

This partnership reflects the ambition we have for the club, both on and off the pitch, and we’re excited about the opportunities this creates for football in the region.”

Football gives us an authentic platform to engage with a new generation of consumers, while NorthEast United FC provides a strong cultural and sporting connection.”

Mandar Tamhane, CEO, NorthEast United FC, added, “This partnership is a reflection of where NorthEast United FC is heading. We have always believed that the Northeast has the talent, passion and culture to make a much bigger mark on Indian football. Reebok and Aditya Birla Group shares that belief, and together we have an opportunity to connect that footballing identity with a new generation, while continuing to raise the standards for the club and the region.”

The two-time Durand Cup winner NorthEast United FC (NEUFC), representing all eight states of Northeast India, has played a key role in bringing the region’s rich footballing culture and talent to the forefront of Indian football. Together, Reebok and NEUFC aim to build on that legacy, creating greater momentum for the sport and deepening engagement with one of India’s most celebrated football communities.

Aryaman Vikram Birla and John Abraham were joined by key members of the NorthEast United FC squad, including Mandar Tamhane, Gurmeet Singh, Buanthanglun Samte, Redeem Tlang and Lalrinzuala Lalbiaknia, as the club unveiled its new Reebok jersey.

Bringing the launch to life on the pitch, NEUFC players played a fast-paced 5-a-side exhibition match, giving fans and media their first glimpse of the new Reebok kit in competitive action. 17.title: Manipur: Two UKNA cadres killed, Two injured in Joint Indian Army, Assam Rifles Operation
17.text:
In Manipur, two cadres of outlaw armed group United Kuki National Army (UKNA) were killed and two others injured in an operation jointly conducted by Indian Army and Assam Rifles team in the jungle area of Churachandpur district.

A joint team of Indian Army and Assam Rifles team launched a counter insurgency operation in the jungle area near Phaibong Village of Henglep Sub-Division in Churachandpur district, IG Assam Rifles (South) said in a statement.

The operation was based on specific intelligence regarding the presence of a United Kuki National Army (UKNA) camp where cadres were equipped with automatic weapons. It further said that on September 2, security forces came under fire and engaged the cadres who fled into dense vegetation.

The operation reportedly neutralized two UKNA cadres and injured two others. Security forces recovered two MA rifles, on AK-56, one 40 mm Lathode gun, ammunition, magazines and other military stores and further search operations are continuing in the surrounding jungle to apprehend the fleeing cadres, it added.

18.title: Stanzin, first female officer from remote Ladakh mountains, among 342 inducted into Army
18.description: CHENNAI: Twenty-four-year-old Stanzin Tsangyang travelled from the remote mountains of Zanskar to Chennai to begin a journey that none in her home district had
18.text:
CHENNAI: Twenty-four-year-old Stanzin Tsangyang travelled from the remote mountains of Zanskar to Chennai to begin a journey that none in her home district had undertaken before. On Saturday, she became the first officer from Zanskar district in Ladakh to be commissioned into the Indian Army.

Her parents, Tundup Tsering, a teacher and Rigzin Ladol, travelled from Ladakh to witness the passing-out parade at the Officers Training Academy. Dressed in traditional attire, they stood proudly alongside their daughter and relatives after the ceremony. “There was no one in our district to guide us,” Stanzin rued, pointing to the lack of an established pathway for young people in the region aspiring to become officers.

“This is our first time in Chennai, and it is all because of our daughter. I am proud she is contributing to the nation,” her father said. Stanzin left home at a young age to study at Lamdon Model School in Leh, spending nearly 14 years in a hostel. Her academic performance lead her to Tezpur University in Assam, where she studied mechanical engineering.

It was at the university that she joined the National Cadet Corps. “I came to know through the NCC that I could join the Army as an officer,” she said.

19.title: John Abraham: ISL's Club-Led Model Will Transform Indian Football
19.description: John Abraham, owner of Northeast United, believes the upcoming Indian Super League (ISL) season will mark a significant turning point for Indian football. With a new club-led domestic structure and a return to the traditional home-and-away format, Abraham envisions a 'paradigm shift' where football could rival cricket's popularity. He also highlighted NEUFC's regional impact and their ambition to win the ISL title.
19.text:
Discover how the Indian Super League is set for a monumental transformation with a new club-led structure, as Northeast United owner John Abraham predicts a "paradigm shift" that could elevate Indian football to new heights.

IMAGE: Owner of ISL club NorthEast United FC, John Abraham. Photograph: X

Key Points The upcoming ISL season (2026-27) is expected to be a turning point for Indian football, shifting to a club-led domestic structure.

John Abraham, Northeast United owner, believes this new model will lead to a "paradigm shift" and make football as popular as cricket in India.

The AIFF has handed over commercial rights of the ISL to clubs for four years, with administrative and regulatory functions remaining with the federation.

Northeast United FC, under John Abraham's ownership, aims to win the ISL title this season after consecutive Durand Cup victories.

The 2026-27 ISL season will feature a traditional home-and-away format with 13 competing teams, and a play-off for the ISL Cup.

Northeast United owner John Abraham is hoping that the upcoming Indian Super League (ISL) season beginning October 10 will be a turning point for the country's football, as it marks a shift towards a new club-led domestic structure for the first time.

The 2026-27 season of the ISL, which will run through May next year, will return to its traditional home-and-away format for a marathon 163-match eight-month league. Last season, the ISL was played in a truncated single-leg format in a short window after being delayed by administrative and commercial uncertainty. There will effectively be no relegation this season from among the 13 competing clubs, with Diamond Harbour FC to be treated automatically relegated after failing to pay their mandatory participation fee.

ISL Embraces Club-Led Model for Future Growth

Amid the buzz of franchise owners taking a more active role in shaping the league's direction, Abraham reaffirmed his belief that the ISL is entering a new era, one driven by the clubs themselves.

"Football will be the new cricket (in India) from this year, because the club owners have taken over the league. You will see a huge paradigm shift in Indian football from this season, and as one of the owners, I'm hoping to see that change," Abraham said, at the unveiling event of NEUFC's new official jersey.

"All the owners in the Indian Super League want football to do better in the country. We're all very cohesive as we want to make this work. So, we're hoping for the best," he said.

On July 8, the AIFF and ISL sides reached a landmark agreement, allowing the clubs to run a full-fledged top-tier competition of the country for at least two years. The AIFF handed over the commercial rights of the ISL to the clubs for four years. But there is an option for the clubs to exit it unilaterally after two years. The national federation accepted the club-led model of running the ISL while the administrative and regulatory functions remain with it.

Northeast United's Ambitions and Regional Impact

Further shedding light on the challenges of running an ISL club, Abraham said, "As a single owner competing with multi-billion-dollar corporations, we're punching above our weight. We're really proud of ourselves and our region. We've got Northeast into the main fold with partners like Reebok along with other public and private sector entities supporting us. That speaks about the confidence in the league and in the sport."

Abraham also reflected on his journey as the owner of NEUFC so far, while highlighting his team's ambitions for the future. With the Highlanders having clinched consecutive Durand Cup titles in 2024 and 2025, the team's owner is confident that they can clinch their elusive ISL title this season. "I really got teary-eyed because I get emotional about my club and I'm in love with my club. Not because of any vanity reasons, but it's because we worked really hard to stay afloat and to be here. We're very proud to be the club we are. We're looking forward to the ISL starting next month, and we are going to fight for the title."

The Bollywood actor also spoke about the impact his club has made beyond the football field and the role it has played in shaping the region. "I think today, Northeast United FC is not just a football team. We're a movement. The northeast has seen a lot of civil tension, but the only exception to every rule has been our football club, which has been a binding factor."

ISL 2026-27 Season Structure and Teams

Meanwhile, Churchill Brothers' participation, as Jamshedpur FC's replacement, will also remain subject to the club fulfilling the necessary regulatory requirements and securing the required approvals. The team finishing on top of the table at the end of the league stage is crowned the Shield Winners, the official champions of the ISL, besides earning a slot in Asian competition. The play-off format will also make a comeback, with the top-six teams competing for the ISL Cup.

Thirteen teams are set to compete in the league, namely Bengaluru FC, Chennaiyin FC, Churchill Brothers FC, East Bengal FC, FC Goa, Inter Kashi FC, Kerala Blasters FC, Mohun Bagan Super Giant, Mumbai City FC, NorthEast United FC, Odisha FC, Punjab FC and Sporting Club Delhi. Diamond Harbour FC, who earned promotion to the ISL after winning the 2025-26 Indian Football League title, failed to fulfil the administrative fee requirement for the 2026-27 season and did not take up their promoted slot. In keeping with the promotion-and-relegation principle, they will not be eligible to earn points this season and will be placed at the bottom of the table by default. They will also lose their ISL status for 2027-28 and compete in the IFL that season.

21.title: Manipur: 2 militants killed, 2 injured in joint operations by Army-Assam Rifles
21.description: Two UKNA militants were killed and two injured in a joint Army-Assam Rifles operation in Manipur's Churachandpur district.
21.text:
Two UKNA militants were killed and two others injured in a gunfight with a joint team of the Indian Army and Assam Rifles in Manipur's Churachandpur district, officials said.

Acting on intelligence inputs, the security forces launched an operation at Phaibong village in the Henglep subdivision on the night of August 29, they said.

The forces established surveillance over a UKNA camp and commenced tactical closing-in at 5 am on September 2, they said.

The UKNA cadres opened "indiscriminate firing" around 5.30 a.m., prompting the troops to retaliate with controlled fire, they added.

"Intel confirms 2 UKNA cadres neutralised and 2 injured," the Assam Rifles said in a social media post on Saturday (September 5, 2026) night.

The United Kuki National Army (UKNA) is not a signatory to the Suspension of Operations (SoO) pact signed between the Centre, Manipur government and several Kuki and Zomi armed outfits.

The Assam Rifles said a subsequent search of the camp led to the recovery of two MA rifles, one AK-56 rifle, one lathode gun, seven lathod grenades, 15 AK magazines, 371 AK-56 rounds, 601 MA rifle rounds, 172 SLR rounds, 15 combat uniforms and seven ammunition pouches.

The operation is continuing in the surrounding jungles, it said.

22.title: India, China Corps Commanders hold talks in Arunachal Pradesh
22.description: Meeting held at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point on Indian side of the LAC
22.text:
Lt General Girish Kalia, commander of the Army’s III Corps, also called the Spear Corps, with its headquarters at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland, was meeting his Chinese counterpart and other officers. (Wikimedia commons)

India and China were conducting Corps Commander-level talks in Arunachal Pradesh Sunday amid reports of recent tensions in the Taksing area of the Upper Subansiri district.

Lt General Girish Kalia, commander of the Army’s III Corps, also called the Spear Corps, with its headquarters at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland, was meeting his Chinese counterpart and other officers.

The talks were being held at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point on the Indian side to address ongoing issues along the LAC in the area. Wacha is India’s easternmost border personnel meeting point, located in the Kibithoo sector in Arunachal Pradesh.

The Indian Express first reported on Saturday about the holding of Corps Commander-level talks following multiple meetings between local commanders of the two sides in recent weeks to resolve issues. 23.title: India, China hold first Corps Commander meeting in Arunachal
23.description: India and China hold their first Corps Commander meeting in Arunachal Pradesh, enhancing military dialogue amid rising tensions.
23.text:
Amid concerns over conflicting territorial claims and military buildup along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Indian and Chinese armies held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Eastern Sector on Sunday (September 6, 2026), marking a significant expansion of the military dialogue mechanism beyond the Ladakh sector.

The meeting was held at the Vacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting Point in Arunachal Pradesh amid reports of tension in the Taksing area of the Upper Subansiri district.

According to Defence Ministry sources, Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, Commander of the 3 Corps (Spear Corps), led a 12-member delegation that included an Inspector General of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police.

The talks are significant as Corps Commander-level meetings between the two armies have largely been held at the Chushul-Moldo Border Meeting Point in eastern Ladakh, particularly after the June 2020 Galwan Valley clashes. The meeting comes days before India hosts the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi from September 11 to 13, where Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to participate.

The 3 Corps, headquartered at Rangapahar in Nagaland, is responsible for operational areas along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh. The Indian Army has two Corps formations responsible for the frontier in the State — the Tezpur-based 4 Corps and the Rangapahar-based 3 Corps.

Until now, the Corps Commander-level mechanism had primarily been used to address military issues and tensions along the western sector of the India-China boundary in Ladakh. The mechanism became particularly important following the Galwan clashes, in which both sides suffered casualties.

Since then, India and China have continued to use military and diplomatic channels to manage differences and maintain stability along the LAC.

The latest meeting comes amid reports of continued Chinese activity and alleged incursions in the Taksing area, despite two high-level engagements since July.

On August 6, the two countries held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs. This was followed by the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SR) on the Boundary Question in Beijing on August 26. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval represented India, while the Chinese delegation was led by Wang Yi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs.

The two sides signed an eight-point outcome document following the SR-level talks. The agreement included a decision to establish two additional Border Personnel Meeting Points and new hotlines to strengthen communication and confidence-building mechanisms along the frontier.

According to sources, one of the newly proposed meeting points will be in the Eastern Sector under the operational responsibility of the 3 Corps, while another will be in the Central Sector. The sources clarified that Joshimath is not among the newly identified meeting points.

Meanwhile, the Indian Army has been closely reviewing its operational preparedness along the frontier. Recently, Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth visited the headquarters of the 3 Corps, where formation commanders briefed him about operational readiness and measures being undertaken to strengthen combat capabilities.

24.title: Two UKNA militants killed in Manipur gunfight, two others injured
24.description: A joint Army and Assam Rifles operation in Churachandpur killed two UKNA militants after an exchange of fire. The encounter led to weapons recoveries and the search operation is continuing in nearby jungles.
24.text:
Two militants of the United Kuki National Army (UKNA) were killed and two others injured in an exchange of fire with a joint team of the Indian Army and Assam Rifles in Manipur’s Churachandpur district, officials said.

The operation was launched following intelligence inputs about the presence of UKNA cadres at a camp in Phaibong village under Henglep subdivision. Security forces began surveillance of the camp and moved in for a tactical operation early on September 2, officials said.

According to the Assam Rifles, the militants opened fire at around 5.30 am, following which the troops responded with controlled fire.

“Intel confirms 2 UKNA cadres neutralised and 2 injured,” the Assam Rifles said in a social media post on Saturday night.

A search of the camp after the exchange of fire led to the recovery of two MA rifles, an AK-56 rifle, a lathode gun, seven lathod grenades, 15 AK magazines, 371 AK-56 rounds, 601 MA rifle rounds and 172 SLR rounds, officials said.

Security forces also recovered 15 combat uniforms and seven ammunition pouches from the site.

The operation was continuing in the surrounding jungle areas, the Assam Rifles said.

The UKNA is not a signatory to the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement between the Centre, the Manipur government and several Kuki and Zomi armed groups.

Following the exchange of fire, security forces searched the camp and recovered two MA rifles, one AK-56 rifle, one lathode gun, seven lathod grenades, 15 AK magazines, 371 AK-56 rounds, 601 MA rifle rounds, 172 SLR rounds, 15 combat uniforms and seven ammunition pouches, the Assam Rifles said.

The operation was continuing in the surrounding jungle areas, it added. (with inputs from PTI)

26.title: Manipur: Security forces defuse 20 kg of IEDs in Jiribam; Two wanted mutants neutralised in Churachandpur
26.description: Security forces kept up pressure on militant and extortion networks across Manipur, with the Assam Rifles, operating under the Spear Corps
26.text:
Imphal: Security forces continue to hit militant groups in coordinated operations across Manipur. Troops from the Spear Corps of Indian Army, working alongside the Manipur Police, successfully recovered and defused three Improvised Explosive Devices (IED) weighing a combined 20 kg in a jungle stretch between Leishabithol and Ahamadabad in Jiribam district on September 5. Acting on specific intelligence, the joint team conducted massive operations and located the explosives and successfully defused it by the explosive experts of the Army. The troops carried out a controlled demolition on-site, neutralising the threat without any harm to life or property.

Officials of the Indian Army described the operation as a reflection of the close coordination and constant vigilance. They said that timely intelligence and swift action by the troops helped avert major security threats.

UKNA militants neutralised in Churachandpur

In a joint operation carried out by the Assam Rifles and the Indian Army, two cadres of the UKNA militant outfit were neutralised and two others injured following a gunfight in Churachandpur district.

The operation was launched on the intelligence input on the night of August 29, targeting a suspected UKNA hideout in Phaibong village under Henglep Sub-Division. Troops quietly moved in and kept the camp under watch before beginning their final approach at around 5 am on September 2. It was a 5 day long operation which resulted in the elimination of two wanted militants.

According to officials, militants inside the camp opened indiscriminate fire on the approaching troops at approximately 5:30 am. Security forces responded with controlled retaliatory fire, resulting in the neutralisation of two cadres and injuries to two others.

A subsequent search of the camp led to the recovery of a substantial cache of weapons and ammunition, including two MA rifles, an AK-56 rifle, a 40 mm Lathode gun, seven Lathod grenades, and over a thousand rounds of assorted ammunition. Combat gear such as uniforms, ammunition pouches, backpacks and jungle boots were also seized from the site.

Three UNLF (K) cadres held

Security forces kept up pressure on militant and extortion networks across Manipur, with the Assam Rifles, operating under the Spear Corps, and the Manipur Police carrying out a series of coordinated operations on September 3.

A search operation conducted in Imphal East led to the seizure of six firearms. In a separate follow-up action at Keishampat and Charangpat, security personnel apprehended three active cadres of the UNLF (K) outfit, who were reportedly involved in running an extortion racket in the area.

27.title: India’s border villages get Rs 11,639-crore push to develop 2,616 villages near international borders
27.description: NEW DELHI: Once known for being neglected and cut off from the rest of the country, India’s border villages are fast turning into hubs of economic activity.One
27.text:
NEW DELHI: Once known for being neglected and cut off from the rest of the country, India’s border villages are fast turning into hubs of economic activity.

One of the major drivers of the change is the Centre’s decision to turn paramilitary outposts along international borders into buyers of local produce. The move is part of a Rs 11,639 crore push to keep villages populated along sensitive frontiers under the Vibrant Village Programme (VVP).

Overall, 2,616 villages situated along the international borders are covered under VVP, in two phases. These include 455 villages in Arunachal Pradesh, 75 in HP, 51 in Uttarakhand, 46 in Sikkim, and 35 in Ladakh.

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police, which guards the Himalayan frontier with China, has been directed to procure all daily need items from these model villages. Be it procuring milk, vegetables, eggs and grains, they have to buy directly from the villages.

The government’s aim it to make border posts of army and paramilitary a local market wherein the troops deployed will buy every day essentials for local farms and reduce the economic isolation that has driven migration away from frontier areas.

The paramilitary forces have started the process, the Centre stated on Sunday. The Border Security Force has also started the process.

According to sources, the move has had a positive impact with residents returning to villages they had earlier left in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey, Dibang Valley and Shi-Yomi districts. The Centre is now planning to revamp schools in these villages and set up hospitals and colleges in these clusters, said a senior government official.

Two-phase project

The village scheme is run in two phases. The first, launched in April 2023, carries an outlay of `4,800 cr for 2022-23 to 2026-27. The second, launched in February this year, carries an outlay of `6,839 cr through 2028-29

29.title: Army averts IED threat in Manipur; recovers 10-kg explosive device
29.description: The Army averted another threat from Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) weighing approximately 10 kg in Manipur on Monday
29.text:
IMPHAL — The Army averted another threat from Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) weighing approximately 10 kg in Manipur on Monday, officials said.

The Spear Corps of the Indian Army, in a post on its X handle, said that acting on specific Intelligence inputs, a formation under the Spear Corps detected and neutralised an IED weighing approximately 10 kg in the South Thanjing forest area of Manipur’s Churachandpur district.

“The timely action averted a potential threat to the local population and security forces, ensured safe movement in the area and reaffirmed the unwavering commitment of the Indian Army to safeguarding lives and maintaining peace and security in Manipur,” the post said.

The latest development comes within 24 hours of the detection of three powerful IEDs in Manipur.

On Sunday, acting on specific Intelligence inputs, formations under the Spear Corps, in close coordination with the Manipur Police, recovered three IEDs weighing approximately 20 kg from a jungle area between Leishabithol and Ahamadabad in Jiribam, along the southern border of Assam.

The explosive devices were safely neutralised on the spot through controlled demolition, successfully averting a major threat to life and property.

The joint operation reflected the unwavering vigilance, operational readiness and seamless inter-agency synergy of the security forces dedicated to safeguarding peace in the region, a defence spokesman had said.

Meanwhile, a police official said that based on reliable Intelligence, a joint team of the Manipur Police, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and an NGO called YADAM (Youth Against Drugs and Alcohol, Manipur), jointly conducted an anti-narcotics operation in the Khergao-Naharup areas of Kakching district and arrested two drug peddlers.

The drug peddlers were identified as Md. Riyaz Khan, 48, and Dandshawa Molody, 26, residents of Chandel district.

Ten soap cases containing heroin, along with one Honda Activa and one Ford Figo, were recovered and seized from their possession, the official said.

30.title: India, China military commanders hold rare border talks in Arunachal sector | India News
30.description: The first session of the flag meeting between the senior military commanders was held on the Indian side on Sunday and the second session on the Chinese side. | India News
30.text:
The 24th round of talks between the Special Representatives – India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi – in New Delhi on August 19 had resulted in 10 points of consensus, including creating mechanisms for talks between military commanders in the eastern and middle sectors of the LAC.

The military talks focused on issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the eastern sector, including maintaining peace and tranquillity along the frontier, people familiar with the matter said. Lt Gen Girish Kalia, who heads the Dimapur-based 3 Corps, led the Indian side. The Indian army has not commented on the talks.

The first session of the flag meeting between the senior military commanders was held on the Indian side on Sunday and the second session on the Chinese side on Monday, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing. He did not go into the details of the discussions between the military officials.

Top Indian and Chinese military commanders met for the first time in the Arunachal Pradesh sector during two sessions held on both sides of the border this week as a follow-up to recent meetings of the Special Representatives and a border mechanism, the external affairs ministry said on Tuesday.

“Pursuant to the understandings reached between the Special Representatives of India and China in August 2025 and August 2026 and subsequent discussions at the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), meetings of which were held in Beijing and New Delhi in May and August 2026 respectively, the first senior highest military commander-level flag meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and in Damai on the Chinese side on September 7,” Jaiswal said at the media briefing.

He noted that a similar mechanism for talks between military commanders already exists in the western sector, which includes Ladakh.

A military face-off between India and China in the western sector, which began in April-May 2020 and dragged on for more than four years, had taken bilateral ties to their lowest point in six decades. Since the two sides reached an understanding in October 2024 on ending the standoff, they have taken a number of steps to normalise the relationship and put in place confidence-building measures along the LAC.

Also Read: India, China must first settle smaller disputes

It is not usual for Indian and Chinese military commanders to hold talks on both sides of the border, and discussions in the western sector are usually held alternatively on either side of the LAC. People familiar with the matter said the talks in the Arunachal Pradesh sector were held over two days as there were several issues to be discussed.

This week’s meeting was the first since tensions erupted between the Indian Army and the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) at Taksing, a remote area of Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Subansiri district, in July and August. The Indian side at the time that the two sides had agreed to use diplomatic and military mechanisms to “avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation” along the border.

New Delhi has also maintained that the state of the border will determine the overall course of the relationship.

held at Wacha on the Indian side on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.Jaiswal said the meeting followed agreements reached during the Special Representatives talks in August 2025 and August 2026, along with subsequent discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination."Pursuant to the understandings reached between the Special Representatives of India and China in August 2025 and August 2026, and subsequent discussions at the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination meetings held in Beijing and New Delhi in May and August 2026 32.title: Assam Rifles promotes women’s literacy and empowerment in Manipur
32.description: The Assam Rifles organised a lecture on women’s literacy and empowerment at Borobekra Higher Secondary School in Manipur on the occasion of International Literacy Day.
32.text:
The Assam Rifles organised a lecture on women’s literacy and empowerment at Borobekra Higher Secondary School in Manipur on the occasion of International Literacy Day.

The programme aimed to raise awareness among students about the importance of education, women’s empowerment and equal opportunities.

Around 50 students participated in the interactive session, which highlighted the role of literacy in helping women become educated, self-reliant and active contributors to society.

Students were also encouraged to view education as a key tool for personal growth, social development and nation building.

The Assam Rifles said the initiative was part of its efforts to engage with youth, promote education and support community empowerment while strengthening its ties with the local population.

The force said it would continue such people-centric initiatives to contribute towards an educated and empowered society and promote peace, harmony and development in the region.

33.title: Two suspected insurgents nabbed with weapons in Tripura, two more killed in Manipur ops
33.description: Kolkata, Sep 8 (SocialNews.XYZ) Continuing its drive against criminal activities in the northeastern states, the Assam Rifles under Spear Corps apprehended two persons from Agartala and recovered two firearms from them. The intelligence-based operation was... - Social News XYZ
33.text:
Kolkata, Sep 8 (SocialNews.XYZ) Continuing its drive against criminal activities in the northeastern states, the Assam Rifles under Spear Corps apprehended two persons from Agartala and recovered two firearms from them.

The intelligence-based operation was conducted in coordination with the local police.

The two individuals have been taken into custody by the Tripura Police and are being questioned about their involvement with insurgent groups.

Assam Rifles units are posted across several states in northeastern India, including Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Assam and Tripura.

While insurgency has been brought under control in most of the states, there are continuous attempts by banned outfits to regroup and build up networks through extortion and recruitment of youths.

"The Assam Rifles maintains constant vigil on activities involving insurgent groups. Insurgents operate across state boundaries to evade the police. The insurgent groups are also linked to each other and provide shelter to each other's cadres. A strong intelligence network is required to get to them," a senior official said.

The two individuals were apprehended in the Salbagan area of Agartala, the official said, and two pistols with magazines were recovered.

Recently, two overground workers of the NSCN(IM) were nabbed in Assam's Tinsukia during a joint raid involving the Assam Rifles.

Extensive intelligence-based joint operations were also carried out between August 29 and September 6 by the Army, Assam Rifles, Central Armed Police Forces and Manipur Police across the Churachandpur, Chandel, Imphal East, Jiribam, Imphal West and Thoubal districts of Manipur and the Tinsukia district of Assam.

Two insurgents were killed and nine apprehended in these operations. Four Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), weighing a total of 38 kg, were also disposed.

The operations also led to the recovery of 10 weapons, ammunition and other war-like stores. The successful actions reaffirm the operational synergy, vigilance and resolve of the forces to disrupt unlawful activities and strengthen security in the region, the Spear Corps said in a statement.

Source: IANS
