34.title: Security forces apprehend nine suspected insurgents in Manipur
34.description: GUWAHATI: Security forces apprehended nine insurgents, including eight suspected members of the Kuki Liberation Army (KLA) during the ongoing operations against
34.text:
GUWAHATI: Security forces apprehended nine insurgents, including eight suspected members of the Kuki Liberation Army (KLA) during the ongoing operations against insurgent groups in Manipur on Monday.

A joint team of Manipur Police, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) CoBRA personnel and Rapid Action Force (RAF) raided an alleged KLA camp at Gampum village under the Saikul police station in Kangpokpi district.

During the operation, eight suspected rebels were apprehended and seven automatic weapons were recovered from the camp.

“The apprehended individuals and the seized arms have been taken into custody for further legal proceedings and investigation. The camp was locked and sealed by the security forces,” Manipur Police said in a statement.

Kangpokpi district has witnessed several violent incidents in recent months, including killings and the burning of houses. In May, three church leaders from the Thadou community were killed and five others injured in an ambush allegedly carried out by suspected militants.

Simultaneously acting on a tip-off, a team from the Imphal West Police commando unit arrested an active member of the Kangleipak Communist Party (People’s War Group) from his residence in Imphal on Monday. Further investigation is underway.

35.title: We are punching above our weight, says NorthEast United FC owner John Abraham ahead of ISL 2026-27
35.description: The Highlanders finished ninth in the ISL last season with 16 points, a significant drop from the third-place finish they managed in 2024-25, although they did retain the Durand Cup for a second successive year. The numbers, therefore, leave plenty of room for improvement, even if Abraham is of the belief that the club's larger project is moving in the right direction.
35.text: As the new Indian Super League (ISL) season begins on October 10, NorthEast United FC enter the competition with a challenge of finding a way to stay competitive without the financial muscle of some of the country's biggest football investors.John Abraham, the club's owner, has described it rather simply.“I am a single owner and competing against multi-million dollar corporations, but we are punching above our weight, and we are proud of ourselves and our regions,” he said at the launch of NEUFC's new Reebok jersey in Mumbai.The Highlanders finished ninth in the ISL last season with 16 points, a significant drop from the third-place finish they managed in 2024-25, although they did retain the Durand Cup for a second successive year. The numbers, therefore, leave plenty of room for improvement, even if Abraham is of the belief that the club's larger project is moving in the right direction.“You understand confidence through sponsorships and our sponsorships have been on the rise this year,” he said.That rise in commercial backing matters for a club whose identity is tied closely to the region it represents.Reebok has come on board alongside partners such as Coal India, Indian Oil and Meghalaya Tourism, giving NEUFC a broader commercial base while Abraham continues to operate the club against ownership groups with considerably deeper pockets. But his argument is that he sees the partnerships as a part of building something that can last beyond a single ISL campaign.“Frankly, our state-run partners have been fantastic and extremely welcoming. They have been better than even the private enterprises,” Abraham said.In the case of NEUFC, that longer-term thinking increasingly extends to infrastructure. Abraham said Indian Oil and Meghalaya Tourism are set to support a 20-acre academy in Shillong, something that could give the club a more substantial pathway for developing talent in a region that has produced footballers for decades, according to the Bollywood actor.“They don’t only come on board as sponsors, but Indian Oil and Meghalaya Tourism are also going to help us make a 20-acre academy in Shillong,” he said.The ambition is also to use that infrastructure beyond football, with Abraham pointing to sports such as weightlifting and wrestling, where the Northeast has traditionally been a strong contributor to Indian sport. For a club representing eight states, that could become as important to its identity as what happens on the pitch.The immediate sporting picture, however, is less straightforward. NEUFC's ninth-place finish last season came after a campaign in which the Highlanders won only four of their 13 league matches, although they ended the season with back-to-back wins and had already shown their ability to perform in knockout football by winning the Durand Cup.Abraham believes football has the potential to occupy a much larger space in India's sporting landscape, even if cricket remains overwhelmingly dominant.“I know football is going to be the new cricket. We are a one-sport country now, but people are going to enjoy watching some football in India,” he said.That is where the Reebok association also fits into the wider picture. Aryaman Birla, speaking about the partnership, said that the attraction extended to the community and culture NEUFC has built around the club. He also acknowledged that the ISL remains young and that building a successful sporting league is a long process rather than something that can be achieved over a few seasons.“It’s a fantastic association for us, not just for football as a space, but the community and culture that NorthEast United FC have built. We need to back the sport, the players, and it’s still early days, as leagues take a long time to grow,” Birla said.With new sponsors and a rejuvenated squad on-board, the Juan Pedro Benali-coached NorthEast United FC step into the new ISL season with an aim of breaking their 12-year-long wait of laying their hands on the coveted league title.

36.title: NSCN-IM using Naga-Kuki tensions to divert attention, say Kuki-Zo insurgent groups
36.description: Kuki-Zo insurgents claim NSCN-IM is exploiting Naga-Kuki tensions to divert attention from internal issues and revive support.
36.text:
The spokesperson of a Kuki-Zo insurgent group in peace talks with the government said on Thursday (September 10, 2026) that the ongoing unrest in Manipur was not a “Naga-Kuki conflict”, and alleged, instead, that certain elements linked to the National Socialist Council of Nagaland (Isak-Muivah) [NSCN-IM] were making attemps to manufacture such a narrative to serve their own interests.

The ethnic violence in Manipur, which began as clashes between the Meitei and Kuki communities on May 3, 2023, has, since February 7, 2026, expanded to include violence between sections of the Naga and Kuki communities.

Seilen Haokip of the Kuki National Organisation (KNO), one of the two Kuki insurgent groupings in suspension of operations (SoO) pact with the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Manipur government, said there was a deliberate effort to spread violence beyond existing conflict zones and draw the Naga and Kuki communities into a broader confrontation. The violence was not spontaneous, he said, adding that the objective was to divert attention from internal challenges within the NSCN-IM and revive support for the outfit by creating fresh fault lines in the hill districts.

Drawing parallels with the Naga-Kuki clashes of the 1990s, noting that violence at the time had spread from one area to several hill districts across Manipur, he said that the present situation was fundamentally different and that communities in the hills were aware of the risks of escalation.

“They [NSCN-IM]would like to repeat what happened between 1992 and 1997, when violence spread across the hill districts. But people today are wiser and understand the consequences. The Government of India should deal with the NSCN-IM and ensure that the matter is contained. Otherwise, there is a risk of creating unnecessary animosity where none exists,” Mr. Haokip said.

NSCN-IM, the largest Naga insurgent group, signed a ceasefire agreement with the Government of India in 1997 and, in 2015, signed a framework agreement to find a political solution to their demands.

Relocation of camps

On September 2, 2025, the MHA and the Manipur government extended the SoO agreement, which has been in existence since 2008, with the KNO and the United People’s Front (UPF) on “re-negotiated terms and conditions or ground rules.” The revised ground rules reiterated territorial integrity of Manipur and relocation of camps run by the insurgent groups away from Meitei-dominated areas in the valley districts.

The SoO groups have been demanding a Union Territory with legislature for the Kuki-Zo people.

Mr. Haokip said that in all, six camps were to be relocated and the work had started in some places. He said that one particular camp in Churachandpur could not be relocated due to heavy rains and logistical challenges

“Although preparatory work, including forest clearing and road construction, has begun, persistent rainfall has slowed progress. In one case, a site identified for relocation had to be abandoned after even a four-wheel-drive excavator was unable to access the area, forcing authorities to search for an alternative location,” Mr. Haokip said.

He said that the relocation process was being carried out through joint inspections involving security forces, local police and SoO representatives to ensure the suitability of the sites.

During a press interaction, Aron Kipgen, UPF’s spokesperson criticised recent security operations by central forces, including searches and raids on SoO camps, contending that such actions violated established ground rules that require coordination with local police and adherence to the SoO agreement.

He accused the Manipur government of adopting a discriminatory approach towards Kuki-Zo communities and reiterated their demand for a separate administrative arrangement. He said the ongoing conflict, displacement of people and disruptions to the movement of essential supplies had reinforced calls for governance directly under the Centre.

He said their proposal seeking a separate administrative arrangement for the Kuki-Zo people had been pending with the MHA since 2024. He criticised the efforts to link the Census exercise to the National Register of Citizens (NRC), saying the demand to complete the NRC before conducting the Census was contrary to the Union government’s plans.

37.title: Dried pangolin scales seized, two arrested in Meghalaya’s Ri-Bhoi
37.description: Around 14.68 kg of dried pangolin scales were seized and two people were arrested during a wildlife trafficking operation in Meghalaya’s Ri-Bhoi district, officials said on Friday, September 11.
37.text:
Around 14.68 kg of dried pangolin scales were seized and two people were arrested during a wildlife trafficking operation in Meghalaya’s Ri-Bhoi district, officials said on Friday, September 11.

The seizure was made on September 7 from a vehicle travelling towards Mawhati near the Assam-Meghalaya border. The pangolin scales were allegedly concealed in three bags inside the vehicle.

The vehicle, the seized wildlife products and the two arrested persons were handed over to the Range Forest Officer, Nongpoh, for further action under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

Pangolins are listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act and Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

Pangolin scales are among wildlife products illegally traded across the world, particularly in parts of Asia where they are used in traditional medicine, officials said.

38.title: Satellite images show China advancing into contested India border territory as Xi travels to New Delhi
38.description: Exclusive: While China’s leader is due to meet with Narendra Modi in India this weekend, people living in remote frontier villages tell Shweta Sharma they fear being pushed out of their ancestral lands by an advancing Chinese Army that claims the region as its own
38.text:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

On The Ground newsletter: Get a weekly dispatch from our international correspondents Get a weekly dispatch from our international correspondents Get a weekly international news dispatch Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Panic has gripped the remote frontier villages of India’s border with China, where tribal communities say they are being pushed back from their ancestral yak-grazing and hunting landsdue to a rapidly growing threat – the advancing Chinese Army.

Satellite images accessed by The Independent show a rapid expansion of infrastructure at multiple sites along and near the disputed India-China frontier in Arunachal Pradesh, including new buildings, roads, as well as helipads.

The imagery offers a rare visual record of the changing landscape along one of the most inaccessible sections of the frontier in the Himalayas, where competing territorial claims and the difficulty of maintaining a permanent Indian presence have left communities living close to the border increasingly anxious.

Takok Mra spoke to The Independent on the phone from his remote village around 20km from the border in India’s Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims in its entirety and calls Zangnan or Southern Tibet. He said he was willing to fight the Chinese army – if it comes to that.

"The Chinese are currently encroaching on our ancestral land. We eat, survive and run our livelihoods from here, and it is our land. They have already entered very far inside Indian territory," Mra says. "I cannot say exactly how many kilometres they have taken, but they have taken a lot.”

With China’s Xi Jinping travelling to India to meet with his counterpart Narendra Modi this weekend, part of the largest Chinese delegation to travel to India in years, both countries’ governments have sought to play down any tensions at the border, denying there is an active standoff akin to the skirmishes that cost at least 20 Indian soldiers’ lives back in 2020.

But the satellite images and testimony from border villages paint a different picture, one of sustained Chinese advances and infrastructure development in contested territory that remains part of talks between the two countries’ diplomatic and military officials.

In the satellite images provided by Vantor, analysts note recent construction and infrastructure changes at multiple sites in the Upper Subansiri Valley, where Mra’s village of Gelemo is located.

Two sites near Zhari town in the north of Lhunze County in Tibet, on the Chinese-held side of the frontier, show the clearest activity, according to Janes, a global open-source intelligence company.

“The satellite imagery confirms there is recent construction in the areas of interest,” say analysts at Janes, adding that when the satellite imagery is overlaid with both India's and China's competing interpretations of the border, the imagery shows that some of this infrastructure sits within territory claimed by both countries, placing it squarely inside the disputed zone.

open image in gallery Satellite image shows Zhari town and a large village to its north in Lhunze County, Tibet, on 22 October 2022 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

open image in gallery Satellite image shows Zhari town and a large village to its north in Lhunze County, Tibet, on 4 March 2026. The images show the expansion of Zhari town and surrounding infrastructure, with new buildings, roads and cleared areas visible across the valley ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

At one location south of the town, construction that began in early 2019 – with the first visible structures appearing by August that year – is still ongoing. The site shows flattened land, construction while engineering vehicles are present, and a cement plant being installed. The possibility of it being for military use cannot be ruled out, analysts told The Independent.

A separate construction site inside the town itself has, in the analysts' assessment, "roughly an even chance" of being a military facility.

Nearby, a stretch of road has been widened and its grade reduced – improvements that make it easier to move heavy equipment and are often a precursor to paving the road for year-round use.

open image in gallery Satellite imagery shows a small village in southern Zhari town, Lhunze, Tibet, on 22 October 2022 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

open image in gallery Satellite imagery shows a small village in southern Zhari town, Lhunze, Tibet, on 4 March 2026 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

South of Luhnze, the imagery shows a new helipad built to replace two smaller ones, along with another new helipad further south.

The latest Vantor image from August 2026 shows at least one structure now has a roof, indicating construction is still underway. Analysts assess the site is likely military in nature, citing the layout, the presence of vehicles matching military patterns, and an adjoining training area. A new road connecting to the town was also built between February and May 2026.

open image in gallery A comparison of satellite imagery shows changes and new development in Raorang in Tibet between 2 November 2022 and January 2026. Pictures show some construction at several further sites with possible military characteristics, including one additional training area ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

A road near the town was also constructed between February and May 2026.

The allegations surface at a delicate moment in Sino-India relations. Xi’s visit to Delhi for the Brics summit is his first trip to India since the 2020 border skirmish in the Galwan Valley that saw relations between the two nuclear-powered nations plummet to their worst level in decades. Xi is expected to travel with a delegation of around 400 officials.

Amid growing clamour among locals over Chinese activity, two independent fact-finding groups travelled to Gelemo and Taksing – remote, high-altitude villages roughly 15-20km from the Sino-India border in the eastern Himalayas – to assess the situation on the ground.

Tadak Pakba, president of the All Tagin Students' Union (ATSU), led a group of eight people to Gelemo and Taksing, gathering reports directly from local residents, tribal communities and military porters. ATSU represents the Tagin Indigenous community of Arunachal Pradesh.

open image in gallery Chinese vehicles carring traders enter Indian territory after crossing the China-India border at the 15 000-feet (4545-metre) Nathu La Pass, in India's northeastern state of Sikkim on May 19 ,2008 ( AFP/Getty )

Pakba says the way the alleged Chinese incursion is happening there now “has not been seen before”.

“There is not only panic in border villages, but this is the fact of reality on the ground. The Indian Army is going back and the Chinese army is coming forward,” he says.

Between 11 and 13 August, local leader Pakba and his team conducted a three-day field investigation and reported Chinese encroachment at several positions normally patrolled by the Indian Army.

These include remote hunting and yak-grazing grounds that for years have been accessible to Indian villagers. "Villagers are currently forbidden from accessing these areas... this has caused panic among locals, leading some to move away from the border areas," Pakba says.

“This is all very recent – happening since June this year,” he adds.

open image in gallery An overview of Gelemo, a remote border village located in the Upper Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh, India ( Supplied )

The fact-finding report, submitted to the deputy commissioner of Upper Subansiri and the chief minister's office and seen by The Independent, demands "immediate intervention" into "reported presence and activities of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA)" in the Taksing-Gelemo frontier region.

It should be treated as a matter of "grave strategic and national importance," not an "ordinary developmental issue", the report says.

The issue was first raised by the Nah Welfare Society (NWS), a local tribal body representing the Nah Indigenous community that migrated from Tibet and settled in Upper Subansiri district generations ago.

It submitted a memorandum to the deputy commissioner of Upper Subansiri, claiming that the PLA has established roads, bridges and military camps in several locations traditionally used by local communities for grazing, hunting and the collection of forest produce.

"The intention and speed of the present activities of the Chinese PLA at Taksing are very alarming. We are losing our land inch by inch day by day," it added.

For Mra, the alleged loss of access to traditional land along India's frontier with China is not an abstract territorial dispute – it is a personal loss. His family has held this ancestral land since the 1962 India-China war.

open image in gallery Takok Mra, a resident of Gelemo in Arunachal Pradesh, where concerns of Chinese incursion have been emerging ( Supplied )

"I am a true patriot. Give us weapons to save our country and our land," says the 38-year-old.

Tribal communities who hunt and graze in the Himalayan forests are more than just passive bystanders in the border conflict, and will pass information to the Indian Army about troop movements in the disputed regions. Mra says that as early as June, they informed the army about the presence of Chinese troops – after which the army became more active in the area.

Expressing frustration over the lack of basic amenities such as electricity, roads, healthcare and schools in his village, Mra contrasts this with the aggressive Chinese infrastructure development near the border.

"When we reach our village Gelemo, we feel completely cut off from the world. Due to lack of basic facilities, our local people move to the district to earn a living, and that is why the border is slowly becoming empty," he says, suggesting that this movement of people from remote areas is in part allowing the Chinese army to advance.

A second fact-finding mission was led by the People's Party of Arunachal Pradesh (PPA) – part of a regional bloc allied with India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) – which sent a four-member team to the border areas.

Kapa Bengia, chief advisor to PPA and a former minister in the state, was part of the group which visited Taksing, Galemo, and Maza, one of the villages closest to the border.

Bengia says: “They (Chinese Army) are already advancing, and our patrolling group is not allowed to move towards our own land.”

The Nanga Pahar, a strategic border area in the remote Taksing circle used by the Nah and other tribal communities, have been declared a strictly prohibited zone for local residents, the report said.

The Indian Army has broadly dismissed reports of a Chinese incursion into disputed territory as "incorrect and without any basis."

However, India's foreign ministry was less direct in its response, describing border issues as a "more serious" part of maintaining peaceful relations between the two countries.

Indian government spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “We have also stated that the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties.”

China also issued a statement, though it neither confirmed nor denied fresh border tensions.

"The China-India border situation is generally stable at the moment," said Guo Jiakun, a foreign ministry spokesperson in Beijing.

The closest the Indian side has come to confirming any concerns came in Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Kandhu's account of a meeting with defence minister Rajnath Singh. Singh, he said, was "very concerned and proactive about this issue" and will "certainly provide the necessary infrastructural support" in the coming days.

open image in gallery A 2023 shows a Buddhist temple on the outskirts of Dirang in India's Arunachal Pradesh state ( AFP/Getty )

Ajay Murtem, a local public leader in Arunachal Pradesh and a native of Upper Subansiri district, says: "New battle lines between China and India will be drawn in Upper Subansiri district if the Indian government does not stop China's expansion into Taksing, Maja, Gelemo and the Shreechu valley."

Murtem says the Tagin tribe – one of Arunachal Pradesh's major Indigenous communities – and its subclan Nah community hold ceremonial rituals at Potrang Lake, just an hour from Taksing. In recent days, however, tribal people have been stopped by the Chinese army from visiting the traditionally sacred Buddhist worship site.

“We are all patriots. The people living along the international frontier are not merely inhabitants of remote villages. They are also the eyes and ears of the nation along the border.”

What is happening in Arunachal Pradesh is part of China's "salami slicing" strategy, says Srikanth Kondapalli, a professor of China studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi, referring to a process in which small, incremental moves are made and consolidated over time rather than through one major incursion.

"First, the Chinese release some yaks and wait for the Indian army's response. If it's absent for months, they install a small shed, then convert it into a permanent structure – and when they face no resistance, they build a small army company," he explains, calling it a "grey zone" where the McMahon Line – the de facto boundary between India's Arunachal Pradesh state and Tibet – is not legally defined.

open image in gallery File: Chinese President Xi Jinping and India Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia October 23, 2024 ( Reuters )

The Indian government has made some efforts to launch its own version of Beijing’s frontier villages, which China has succeeded in populating and refers to has Xiaokang or “well-off societies”, thereby bolstering its territorial claims.

India’s version – the Vibrant Village Programme – “has not been successful”, says Kondapalli, because “it needs a lot of ecosystem [building]”. “While China has constructed roughly 100 model villages in Longju, and from there they began expanding into Indian-claimed areas in Arunachal.”

India's inability to regularly reach the de facto border or “line of actual control”, he says, gives China an opening to pursue its salami-slicing strategy.

open image in gallery India and China border in Sikkim ( AFP/Getty )

"Until you prepare your infrastructure and consolidate your position on the line of actual control, there is simply no way that you can have any leverage. The Chinese can come up to the line of actual control within 24 hours. They began road construction in the 1980s. We just woke up."

The border issue is a major talking point in India, and domestic audiences will be watching closely for any developments during the summit this weekend. But with any direct press interactions by Xi and Modi highly unlikely, Kondapalli says there is a relatively low chance of the matter being raised by either side. With China due to take over as Brics host next year, both countries are heavily invested in presenting this year’s talks as a success.

39.title: Assam Rifles recovers hidden weapons cache near India-Myanmar border in Manipur’s Chandel
39.description: Assam Rifles recovered a cache of weapons and war-like stores during a search operation along the India-Myanmar border in Manipur’s Chandel district, officials said.
39.text:
Assam Rifles recovered a cache of weapons and war-like stores during a search operation along the India-Myanmar border in Manipur’s Chandel district, officials said.

Acting on specific intelligence inputs, Assam Rifles launched the operation on September 11 in the area around Border Pillars 53 and 54. A 22-member team was deployed from Company Operating Base AibolJoupi at around 5.30 pm.

The search continued through the night, with troops carrying out area domination and systematic searches of the suspected location.

At around 6.30 am on September 12, after nearly eight hours of operations, the team located a concealed cache near Border Pillar 54, around five kilometres south of COB AibolJoupi.

The recovered cache included three Pompis, six single-barrel rifles, three carbines, two Lathod guns, two No. 36 hand grenades, two improvised explosive devices, three carbine magazines and five rounds of 7.62 mm ammunition.

According to Assam Rifles, the recovery highlights the role of timely intelligence and swift operational response in detecting concealed weapons stockpiles in sensitive border areas.

The force said the operation has disrupted potential unlawful activities and strengthened security along the India-Myanmar frontier in Chandel district.

40.title: Manipur: Assam Rifles recovers huge arms cache in Chandel district
40.text: In Manipur, a team of Assam Rifles launched an operation in the area along the Indo-Myanmar Border in Chandel district and recovered a huge arms cache. It included 3 Pompi, 6 single-barrel rifles, 3 carbines, 2 Lathod guns, 2 grenades, 2 IEDs and ammunition. Meanwhile, under the Civic Action Programmes, Assam Rifles extended livelihood support to Senjenpokpi United Welfare Club at Irengbam, Kakching district of Manipur, by providing 22 sewing machines worth two lakh rupees. The machines were distributed in response to a requirement raised by the club, and the initiative aims to promote tailoring as a skill for income generation, self-reliance, and economic empowerment of the local community.

41.title: Assam Rifles seizes methamphetamine tablets worth Rs 5.59 crore in Mizoram, two arrested
41.description: Assam Rifles and the NCB seized methamphetamine tablets from two vehicles in Mizoram and detained two suspects. The recovery is part of continuing efforts to break drug trafficking networks across the Northeast.
41.text:
Assam Rifles, in a joint operation with the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Aizawl, seized 6.991 kg of methamphetamine tablets valued at approximately Rs 5.59 crore in Mizoram on September 12.

Acting on specific intelligence inputs, security personnel intercepted two suspicious vehicles at Seling, Mizoram, during a targeted anti-narcotics operation. A search of the vehicles led to the recovery of the methamphetamine tablets.

Two individuals were apprehended in connection with the seizure and are currently being questioned by the authorities. Further investigation is underway to establish the source and intended destination of the contraband and identify possible links to a wider narcotics trafficking network.

The operation was conducted under the aegis of the Spear Corps as part of ongoing efforts by security agencies to disrupt drug trafficking networks operating across the Northeast.

In a post on X, the Spear Corps said the operation demonstrated the security forces’ resolve to dismantle narcotics networks and prevent the movement of illegal drugs in the region.

The latest seizure comes days after Assam Rifles, in coordination with the CRPF and state police, reportedly seized 10.891 kg of brown sugar valued at around Rs 80 crore and 14,000 Yaba tablets worth approximately Rs 2.5 crore during intelligence-based operations in Manipur’s Jiribam and Assam’s Sribhumi district. Six individuals were apprehended in those operations, according to officials.

Authorities are continuing investigations into the latest Mizoram seizure to trace the alleged drug supply chain and determine the involvement of other persons.

42.title: Assam Rifles detain three USRA cadres in Manipur’s Churachandpur
42.description: Assam Rifles detained three USRA cadres in Churachandpur, Manipur, recovering five assault rifles, ammunition, magazines and tactical pouches.
42.text:
The Assam Rifles detained three members of the United Socialist Revolutionary Army (USRA) in a counter-insurgency operation conducted between September 10 and September 11 in the vicinity of Munpi Village, Churachandpur district, Manipur.

The arrested cadres were identified as Khual from Munpi Village; Money Chiru, aged 30, from Nungrai Village in Bishnupur District; and Thanglalmuan, aged 25, from Nghathal Village, Churachandpur District.

The operation took place near Nampong following intelligence related to narcotics smuggling. The Assam Rifles highlighted that this action reflects their ongoing commitment to preventing illegal infiltration, trans-border narcotics trafficking, and maintaining security across the Northeast region.

“#AssamRifles apprehended two illegal Myanmar nationals in the general area of Nampong, Changlang District, Arunachal Pradesh on 28 Aug 2026, based on specific intelligence regarding narcotics smuggling. During the operation, 130 gms of heroin, worth approximately ₹24 lakh, was recovered from the apprehended individuals. The successful operation highlights Assam Rifles’ continued commitment towards curbing illegal infiltration, trans-border narcotics smuggling and ensuring security in the Northeast,” stated Assam Rifles.

43.title: Assam Rifles apprehends 3 USRA cadres in Manipur's Churachandpur
43.description: In a major counter-insurgency operation,  Assam Rifles apprehended three cadres of the United Socialist Revolutionary Army (USRA) in the general area of Munpi Village in Manipur's Churachandpur district between September 10 and September 11.
43.text:
Imphal (Manipur) [India], September 12 (ANI): In a major counter-insurgency operation, Assam Rifles apprehended three cadres of the United Socialist Revolutionary Army (USRA) in the general area of Munpi Village in Manipur's Churachandpur district between September 10 and September 11.

The arrested USRA cadres have been identified as Khual, a resident of Munpi Village; Money Chiru (30), a resident of Nungrai Village, Bishnupur District; and Thanglalmuan (25), a resident of Nghathal Village, Churachandpur District.

During the search operation, security forces recovered a substantial cache of arms, ammunition, and military gear from their possession.

The recovered items include one 7.62 mm HKG 3 Assault Rifle, one 5.56 mm A1 Assault Rifle, one 5.56 mm M22 Assault Rifle, two 7.62 mm AK-47 Rifles, seven magazines of different arms, 298 rounds of live ammunition of various calibres, and five tactical pouches.

Further details awaited.

In a separate incident, the Assam Rifles apprehended two allegedly illegal Myanmar nationals and seized 130 grams of heroin worth approximately Rs 24 lakh in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district, the force said on August 30.

The operation was carried out in the general area of Nampong on August 28 based on specific intelligence regarding narcotics smuggling, the Assam Rifles said.

During the operation, 130 gms of heroin, worth approximately ₹24 lakh, was recovered from the apprehended individuals.

According to the Assam Rifles, the operation highlights the force's continued commitment towards curbing illegal infiltration, trans-border narcotics smuggling, and ensuring overall security across the Northeast region.

"#AssamRifles apprehended two illegal Myanmar nationals in the general area of Nampong, Changlang District, Arunachal Pradesh on 28 Aug 2026, based on specific intelligence regarding narcotics smuggling. During the operation, 130 gms of heroin, worth approximately ₹24 lakh, was recovered from the apprehended individuals. The successful operation highlights Assam Rifles’ continued commitment towards curbing illegal infiltration, trans-border narcotics smuggling and ensuring security in the Northeast," said Assam Rifles. (ANI)

44.title: Manipur Police arrest three armed cadres, recover assault rifles and ammunition in Churachandpur
44.description: Manipur Police, in two separate operations in Churachandpur district, arrested three armed cadres and recovered a cache of firearms, ammunition and other tactical equipment, according to police.
44.text:
Imphal (Manipur) [India], September 12 (ANI): Manipur Police, in two separate operations in Churachandpur district, arrested three armed cadres and recovered a cache of firearms, ammunition and other tactical equipment, according to police.

In the first operation conducted on September 11 in the general area of Munpi village under Henglep Sub-Division, a combined team of Churachandpur District Police and five Assam Rifles arrested three armed cadres.

The arrested persons were identified as Khual, 35, of Munpi village in Henglep Sub-Division; Money Chiru, 30, of Nungrai village in Bishnupur district; and Thanglanmuan, 25, of Nghathal village in Churachandpur district.

Police said the operation led to the recovery of several assault rifles and a substantial quantity of ammunition. The seized weapons included one 7.62 mm HKG 3 assault rifle, one 5.56 mm A1 assault rifle and one 5.56 mm M22 assault rifle.

Two 7.62 mm AK-47 rifles were also recovered during the operation, along with seven magazines of different arms. Police further recovered 298 rounds of ammunition of different calibres and five tactical pouches.

In a separate operation on the same day, Churachandpur District Police and 2 JAK LI launched a joint operation in the adjoining areas between Nalon and Thinghingjang villages.

The operation was based on intelligence inputs regarding the presence of illegal arms and ammunition in the general area of Thangjing Ridge.

According to Manipur Police, the second operation resulted in the recovery of a wide range of weapons and equipment. The seized items included two 82 mm mortars and one locally made rocket.

Security personnel also recovered one MP5 automatic rifle fitted with a scope, four 9 mm carbines with magazines and two pistols with magazines.

The recovery further included four single-barrel rifles, four bolt-action rifles and two mortar bombs. Two pump-action weapons and four pump-action shells were also seized.

Apart from firearms and ammunition, the team recovered one radio set, two BPJ harnesses and one pair of combat boots.

Police said the recoveries were made during the joint operations conducted on September 11. The three arrested individuals were apprehended during the Munpi village operation, while the second operation focused on recovering illegal arms and ammunition from areas between Nalon and Thinghingjang villages. (ANI)

45.title: Indian Army’s Havildar Vikash Chettri Wins Bronze at Mr North East Bodybuilding Championship
45.description: Havildar Vikash Chettri of the Assam Regimental Centre has brought laurels to the Indian Army by securing a bronze medal at the Mr North East Bodybuilding
45.text:
Havildar Vikash Chettri of the Assam Regimental Centre has brought laurels to the Indian Army by securing a bronze medal at the Mr North East Bodybuilding Championship.

The Eastern Command congratulated Havildar Vikash Chettri on his impressive performance at the championship, highlighting the dedication, discipline and determination behind his sporting achievement.

Bodybuilding demands rigorous physical training, consistency and strict discipline, qualities that Chettri demonstrated while competing at the regional championship. His podium finish also reflects the sporting talent among Indian Army personnel who continue to excel in disciplines beyond their military responsibilities.

The Eastern Command expressed pride in the achievement of the Assam Regimental Centre soldier and said his performance had brought laurels to both the Indian Army and the nation.

Congratulating Havildar Chettri, the Eastern Command also wished him continued success in his future sporting endeavours.

The achievement adds to the long tradition of Indian Army personnel representing their formations and the country across a wide range of sporting disciplines, demonstrating excellence through commitment, physical fitness and perseverance.

47.title: Amit Shah in Mumbai: UCC before 2029, Seva Sankalp campaign, push for Indian LGD value chain
47.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) will be implemented across all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029, while asserting that India’s national security posture has undergone a fundamental transformation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.
47.text:
Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 13 (ANI): Setting a legislative timeline for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the UCC will be implemented across all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029, while asserting that India’s national security posture has undergone a fundamental transformation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.

Speaking at an event in Mumbai, Shah said, “We introduced the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in several states. I am confident that we will implement the UCC in all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029...Operations such as the surgical strikes, air strikes, and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, while security has been prioritised across various sectors.”

On the India-China border situation, Shah said sensitive details related to negotiations between the Indian Army and Chinese military over the Line of Actual Control cannot be disclosed publicly, stressing that strategic matters should not be politicised.

“There are sensitive matters where disclosing details openly serves neither the national interest nor the Army’s interest,” he said.

Shah also said the government believes in dialogue and discussion while responding to questions on Gen Z-led movements, the implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) and conflicts over language and regional identity arising from migration.

“We are in a democracy. People hold different views on various issues, and it is essential that those views are expressed. The Bharatiya Janata Party is in power, but we cannot govern by imposing an Emergency. That is the Congress culture, not ours. We believe in dialogue and discussion,” he said.

On the NRC in Manipur and the possibility of a nationwide exercise, Shah said the government was discussing both matters with its colleagues and political parties in Manipur and would inform the public once a decision is taken.

On language-related tensions, he said it was the government’s policy to prioritise the mother tongue and noted that the Constitution had issued specific directives to states.

Meanwhile, Shah announced that the month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ will be conducted nationwide from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years of public service.

“The entire NDA alliance, numerous voluntary organisations, and people across the country are coming together to conduct the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' nationwide from September 17 to October 17. As we all know, September 17 marks the birthday of Narendra Modi ji. This year holds special significance. Following a long period of organisational work, October 6, 2026, will mark the completion of 25 years of Modi ji's tenure as Chief Minister and Prime Minister—a journey that continues to this day. Very few leaders in this country have achieved the distinction of completing 25 years of continuous public service, having served both as a state Chief Minister and as the Prime Minister of the nation," Shah said.

Shah also said India's global standing had risen significantly over the past 12 years and claimed that the views of the Prime Minister now carry weight on global issues.

"Over the past 12 years, the country's global standing has risen significantly. Whatever the global issue may be, the views of India's Prime Minister carry weight today. People across the world view an Indian citizen holding an Indian passport with respect. Narendra Modi ji has worked to enhance the value of the Indian passport, and the result is that he has emerged as the most popular leader globally, boasting a 68 per cent approval rating in surveys. 36 nations have conferred their highest international honours upon him, awards akin to India's 'Bharat Ratna.' This reflects India's growing stature abroad," Shah said.

From political developments, Shah also turned his attention to India’s economic and global standing, saying the country had moved from the “Fragile Five” to the world’s top five economies and citing first-quarter GDP growth of 7.8 per cent.

“Prior to 2014, our national politics was plagued by corruption, casteism, and dynastic politics. In the political era spanning 2014 to 2026, the nation has moved beyond these issues toward a politics of performance,” Shah said.

He added that economic strength has been paired with an unyielding international posture. "For the first time in 12 years, the people have witnessed a foreign policy with a strong backbone. Whether it is our defence policy or our foreign policy, the guiding principle is 'India First.' India’s interests are paramount to us."

Turning to national security, the Home Minister asserted that India's defence posture has evolved to ensure swift countermeasures against external threats.

"Furthermore, a robust policy is now in place to deliver a befitting response whenever Indian soldiers or citizens fall victim to terrorist conspiracies or attacks. We have demonstrated this to the entire world while addressing three long-standing issues—Article 370, Naxalism, and the situation in the Northeast—that had threatened the nation’s internal security for nearly five decades," Shah noted.

Shah then spoke about India’s knowledge traditions and the need to preserve and expand them while addressing the inauguration of the ‘Ganesh Gyanarthi’ exhibition at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

“True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology. If you bind it in any way, you change the very meaning of knowledge. Knowledge should be free and uninhibited, and its declaration should also be free and uninhibited,” he said.

Shah called for the knowledge, wealth and collections preserved at the Asiatic Society to be used for the creation of a “Great India”, while asserting that decolonisation should mean presenting history completely, authentically and from an Indian perspective rather than erasing it.

“The process of decolonisation is not about erasing history. It means presenting history completely, authentically, and from an Indian perspective before the people once again. That is decolonisation, and it must happen,” Shah said.

He highlighted rare manuscripts and texts preserved at the institution, including an illustrated copy of the Mahabharata and texts relating to Jainism and Buddhism.

Shah also proposed linking heritage libraries and institutions across the country under the leadership of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and called for ancestral documents preserved in villages and households in Maharashtra to be collected and linked with the Gyan Bharatam manuscript survey.

“And across the country, in every village, in every city, in every state, all institutions of this kind should be connected with the Asiatic Society of Mumbai to create a shared pool of knowledge. It should be made available for students across the country, for researchers across the country, and for scholars across the country,” he said.

Shah said the knowledge preserved by the institution should ultimately serve the welfare of the country, the world and humanity.

In another engagement in Mumbai, Shah called upon the gems and jewellery sector to ensure that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing chain of lab-grown diamonds (LGDs), from machinery production to jewellery manufacturing, branding and retail showrooms worldwide, remain firmly under Indian control.

Addressing the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards Ceremony, Shah said India now had all the necessary resources required to build the entire LGD value chain domestically.

“I urge all of you to ensure that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing chain of lab-grown diamonds remain firmly in Indian hands, whether it involves manufacturing machinery, producing the diamonds themselves, crafting jewellery, developing brands, or opening showrooms for Indian companies in cities across the globe,” he said.

Shah said the market for lab-grown diamonds could expand to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market in terms of volume and urged industry players to focus on the opportunity rather than merely price points.

He said the governments of Gujarat and Maharashtra were formulating policies for the sector and that the Centre would also introduce a policy.

“The Government of India will introduce a policy as well. You should move forward with the vision and ambition of securing India’s dominance over the entire value chain—from manufacturing the machinery to the moment the finished jewellery reaches the customer in the showroom,” the Home Minister said.

Shah also praised the gems and jewellery industry for its contribution to society, including during droughts, floods and cyclones, as well as initiatives related to water conservation, tree plantation and education for the children of artisans and employees. (ANI)

48.title: Manipur: Assam Rifles distributes sewing machines to 22 women under Civic Action programme

Security forces also recovered seven magazines of different arms, 298 rounds of live ammunition of various calibres and five tactical pouches. (ANI)

49.title: Strategic Bailey bridge in Arunachal’s Anjaw restored, reopens after 8-day army-BRO operation
49.description: A crucial Bailey bridge in Arunachal Pradesh’s Anjaw district, which connects some of India’s easternmost forward villages near the India-China border, has been restored after an eight-day repair operation by the Indian Army and the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).
49.text:
A crucial Bailey bridge in Arunachal Pradesh’s Anjaw district, which connects some of India’s easternmost forward villages near the India-China border, has been restored after an eight-day repair operation by the Indian Army and the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).

The KKG-BSB Bridge at Krowti, also known as the Karoti Bridge, is located in Kibithoo Circle and spans the Lohit River. The bridge provides a vital surface link to forward villages including Kaho, Musai and Dong.

The strategic steel suspension bridge was severely damaged when an overloaded truck carrying sand attempted to cross it and became stuck, raising concerns over the structure's stability and forcing its closure.

The closure had disrupted connectivity to the remote villages, including Kaho and Dong, which are located close to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

Following eight days of intensive restoration work, the bridge was declared safe for light and small vehicles on September 9, 2026, officials said.

The restoration was carried out jointly by the Indian Army and BRO, with teams working continuously to restore the critical link.

Technical assessments of the bridge are still underway, with strict vehicle weight restrictions being maintained as authorities assess the structure's condition and work towards restoring its full functionality.

The reopening is expected to provide much-needed relief to residents of the remote forward areas and restore essential surface connectivity in the strategically important Kibithoo sector.

50.title: No NRC, No Census: Can Manipur Afford to Skip the Count?
50.description: Manipur's ethnic conflict intensifies as Meiteis demand NRC before Census 2027, while Kukis oppose this order. The region faces governance challenges that require simultaneous NRC and census implementation for better policy outcomes. Provide the answer in Indian English
50.text:
A Signboard with No NRC, No Census in Imphal City, September 2026

This week, after an official visit to Meitei-dominated districts of Manipur, a striking reality emerged. Though I wished to travel into Kuki-inhabited areas, no Meitei car from Imphal would risk the journey amid the ongoing ethnic conflict. Across urban and rural Manipur plain, one slogan dominated every surface—buses, shops, temples, cars, and even trees: “No NRC, No Census.” While the rest of India prepares for Census 2027 after a 16-year gap, Manipuri’s are demanding the National Register of Citizens first and resisting the census.

What drives this unusual stance?



Manipur: A Unique Indian State Bound to Sanatan Civilisation

Few outside the Northeast realise that Manipur has been a co-creator of Sanatan civilisation since the Mahabharata era. The Adi Parva of the Mahabharata (Gita Press, Gorakhpur edition) describes Manipura as a “city of jewels,” ruled by King Chitravahana. His daughter, Princess Chitrangada, lived as a prince until she met Arjuna during his exile. The third Pandava Arjuna fell in love with her; they married in Manipura and had a son, Babruvahana, who stayed behind at the king’s request to continue the royal line.

At first glance, Manipur’s people present an Oriental appearance—women in two-piece traditional attire riding scooters, or the famous all-women markets that dominate every district centre. Yet this diversity only underscores India’s genius for absorbing many races: a Tamil face differs from a Punjabi’s, just as a Jharkhandi look differs from a Kashmiri’s.

The Meiteis remain the largest community in Manipur’s valley and form the cultural core of the state. A closer look at Meitei culture reveals deep cultural oneness with Sanatan traditions. The women’s two-piece dress echoes Assam’s mekhela-sador, Kerala’s mundum-neriyathum, and the Gopi attire of Braj. Manipuri classical dance, one of India’s most celebrated forms, vividly portrays the Raas Leela of Sri Krishna and the Gopis.

Tulsi and Peepal tree in a Meitei household from rural Manipur, September 2026



Most Meiteis follow Gaudiya Vaishnavism; many practise it alongside the indigenous Sanamahi faith. Sanamahism itself shares striking parallels: its five classical elements—fire, water, air, earth and ether—mirror the Panchabhuta concept. The supreme creator Atingkok Maru Sidaba has a consort, Leimarel Sidabi, the great mother-earth goddess who may appear as Imoinu, a counterpart of Devi Lakshmi who brings wealth and peace. In Meitei courtyards one commonly finds a carefully tended Tulsi plant, before which water and flowers are offered to the deity—exactly as in Sanatan households. Men and women wear Tulsi malas with vertical chandan tilak, clear markers of Vishnu worship. Ancestor worship and reverence for forest deities are everyday practices, just as in many North Indian villages. Young Meitei boys still wear earrings and anklets, another shared Indian custom. Every Meitei child has Janam Kundli, used in marriage matching. Manipur maintains a stronger presence in Vrindavan than any other Northeastern community. And who doesnot know Manipur’s distinctive contribution to the Indian National Army during the freedom struggle? Whether through Gaudiya Vaishnavism or Sanamahi, Manipura’s cultural continuum with the rest of India stretches back to time immemorial. Yet, Manipur is under crisis today!

Frontier Neglect: Manipur’s Enduring Crisis of Illegal Migration

As one of India’s frontier states, Manipur has long faced challenges that successive policymakers and researchers largely overlooked. Historically, the state endured a massive Burmese invasion between 1819 and 1826. In the decades that followed, it has grappled with insurgency, drug trafficking, and continuous illegal immigration from Myanmar (formerly Burma). Despite a strong work ethic, the central role of women in family and society, and fertile land, industrial development has remained stagnant. In recent years, the state has drawn national attention due to the intense conflict between Meiteis and Kukis. Kukis, originally from the Burma region, first entered Manipur in significant numbers during the colonial period as militias, labour corps, and settlers. Further migration occurred during World War II.

The porous and poorly guarded border has allowed continued influx, especially during political upheavals such as military rule in Myanmar or periods of insurgency in India’s Northeast. Today, Meiteis — among the oldest communities of the state — find their movement largely confined to the valley, with restricted access to the hill areas. Meitei leaders emphasise they have no grievance against Kukis who settled before Independence. Their concern centres on post-Independence illegal entrants who, they argue, are reducing available space and resources for the indigenous population and are now demanding a separate administrative zone or Union Territory status.

The core problem remains the absence of any reliable system in Manipur — or across India — to distinguish genuine citizens from those who entered after Independence. This uncertainty explains the strong Meitei demand for an updated National Register of Citizens (NRC). Contrary to this, Kuki organisations are demanding census implementation and approval of UT status before implementation of NRC.

Yet the critical questions persist: Is an NRC in Manipur feasible? And what lessons can the state draw from Assam’s experience?

Learning from Assam’s NRC Experience

Even a decade after it was launched, Assam’s National Register of Citizens remains uncertain and incomplete. The exercise suffered from deep structural flaws. Although Assam possessed 1951 NRC data, the cut-off year for detecting illegal immigrants was fixed at 1971. Paradoxically, the areas that witnessed the highest levels of illegal immigration recorded the lowest rates of exclusion — largely because documentation was often supplied by the descendants of those very immigrants. Widespread corruption, later flagged by the CAG, and the easy availability of fake documents further undermined the process. As a result, the Assam NRC has still not been declared final. Senior advocate Upamanyu Hazarika has meticulously documented these structural and implementation failures in his book NRC: How Indigenous Hope Turned into Despair. Even if the government agrees to conduct an NRC in Manipur, preparing a robust protocol, implementing it rigorously, carrying out thorough re-verification, and publishing an accurate final list will require considerable time. While an updated NRC is clearly needed for Manipur — and potentially for other states — Assam’s experience shows that a credible and complete exercise demands long-term vision, administrative integrity, and strong management. Without these, the process risks becoming another prolonged and ultimately futile effort trapped in bureaucratic and political complications.



What Manipur Stands to Lose by Skipping Census 2027?



India already has clear precedents of the dangers of avoiding a census. Assam skipped the 1981 Census and Jammu & Kashmir skipped the 1991 exercise. In both cases, the decision failed to resolve underlying problems; instead, it created a long data vacuum that made governance harder and tensions deeper.

A census is not a citizenship exercise. It simply counts everyone present — citizens and non-citizens alike. Yet this headcount, combined with other large surveys, provides the only reliable way to identify villages and blocks where population is growing at an unnatural rate. Without fresh numbers, policymakers are left flying blind.

Census data forms the backbone of district-level welfare schemes, central fund allocation, and infrastructure planning. A prolonged gap of 16 years already strains administration; another delay will create serious bottlenecks in implementing programmes. When schemes run without updated evidence, the ultimate losers are ordinary citizens who depend on those services. In the absence of Census 2027, critical follow-up studies such as the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI), and Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS) will also lose their scientific sampling frame in Manipur. Accurate data on health, nutrition, ageing, and well-being will become far harder to generate.

Delimitation of assembly and parliamentary seats, as well as the fair distribution of central resources, will likewise suffer from outdated population figures.

In short, while a carefully designed and time-bound NRC remains essential for Manipur, conducting Census 2027 is equally urgent. Instead of avoiding, both Census and NRC can go hand in hand. Skipping it will only deprive the state of the evidence base needed for sound governance and effective public policy.









Author details: Dr Nandita Saikia, Professor at International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai; Contact: nanditasts@gmail.com

More details: www.nanditasaikia.com

51.title: NE witnesses 77% drop in violence in 2025 as border security push intensified: Report
51.description: According to the defence ministry report, in 2025, security forces neutralised 33 terrorists, apprehended 1,066 insurgents and facilitated the surrender of 117 insurgents.
51.text:
New Delhi, Sept 14: The security situation in the Northeast has emerged as a key component of the country’s wider national security architecture, particularly along the sensitive Arunachal Pradesh-China border and the India-Myanmar frontier.

According to an annual report of the Defence Ministry in possession of The Assam Tribune, the Indian Army, Assam Rifles and other security agencies have significantly stepped up counter-insurgency operations, border infrastructure and logistical preparedness across the Northeast, with the region witnessing a 77 percent decline in violence parameters in 2025.

The improvement, according to the security establishment, has created a more conducive environment for development and economic activity in the strategically important region.

The security push assumes significance in the backdrop of the BRICS summit, where India has sought greater international cooperation against terrorism, transnational organised crime and other emerging security threats. For India, the Northeast remains a critical link between its security interests along the China and Myanmar borders and its Act East policy.

According to the report, in 2025, security forces neutralised 33 terrorists, apprehended 1,066 insurgents and facilitated the surrender of 117 insurgents, while recovering 4,336 weapons in the Northeast. Intelligence-based joint operations have increasingly focused on denying insurgent groups operational space and preventing the revival of militant networks.

Along the Arunachal Pradesh frontier, the emphasis has been on strengthening mobility, logistics and the ability of security forces to rapidly induct personnel and equipment into forward areas. The Border Roads Organisation completed a record 123 bridges during 2025, significantly improving connectivity across strategically important border sectors.

One of the major achievements was the completion of the 135-metre multi-span Balanced Cantilever Pinjoli Bridge on the Balipara-Charduar-Tawang Road. The bridge has strengthened connectivity in the Tenga Valley and improved movement along the Tenga-Bomdila-Tawang axis, facilitating quicker movement towards Tawang and other forward areas along the Line of Actual Control.

The BRO has also been strengthening aviation infrastructure in the region. At Anini in Arunachal Pradesh, a 75-metre by 50-metre PQC helipad was completed, replacing the earlier 25-metre by 25-metre landing ground. The upgraded facility can support heavier helicopters, enhancing the movement of troops, supplies and equipment as well as emergency response during natural disasters.

The government has also increased budgetary support to the BRO. After a record expenditure of Rs 16,690 crore in 2024-25, the organisation has been given an enhanced expenditure target of Rs 18,700 crore for 2025-26.

At the same time, the India-Myanmar border continues to remain sensitive because of the ongoing conflict between the Myanmar Army and resistance forces. India has sought to tighten regulation of cross-border movement while maintaining channels of engagement with Myanmar.

Twenty border crossing points have been established under the Free Movement Regime to regulate local movement, while 12,590 metres of fencing was constructed along the India-Myanmar Border in 2025.

52.title: Manipur: Security forces arrest 3 alleged insurgent cadres in separate Imphal West operations
52.description: Security forces arrested three alleged active members of proscribed insurgent groups during separate operations in Imphal West district of Manipur on September 13, officials said.
52.text:
Security forces arrested three alleged active members of proscribed insurgent groups during separate operations in Imphal West district of Manipur on September 13, officials said.

In the first operation, a team of the Combined Dedicated Operations-IW (CDO-IW), acting on specific intelligence corroborated by 31 Assam Rifles, arrested an alleged active cadre of the KCP (PWG) from the Moidangpok area.

The arrested person was identified as Thangjam Sanatomba Singh, 26, alias Thembung, son of Thangjam Indramani Singh of Moidangpok Makha Leikai in Imphal West district.

In a separate operation, CDO-IW personnel, based on intelligence corroborated by 33 Assam Rifles, conducted a search at Takyel Khongbal Leirak Achouba and arrested Sanjenbam Albert Meetei, 26, alias Lukhoi, son of the late S Leisemsana Meetei.

Albert Meetei was allegedly involved in extortion activities and was identified as an active member of the KCP (Apunba), officials said.

In another operation conducted in the Patsoi Unik-Khong Bazar area, the CDO-IW team arrested Khongbantabam Inao Singh, 48, alias Iboyaima, son of the late Kh Moirangningthou Singh of Patsoi Part-III Mamang Leikai.

Inao Singh was identified as a member of PRE-PAK (PRO) and was allegedly involved in extortion activities.

Security personnel recovered Rs 18,500 in cash and one mobile handset during the operations.

Further investigation into the activities and alleged links of the arrested individuals is underway.

53.title: ‘Iron Lady of Assam’ Sanjukta Parasor becomes first woman officer to lead CRPF’s CoBRA unit
53.description: A 2006-batch IPS officer, she is known for her counter-insurgency work in the Northeast
53.text:
SENIOR IPS officer Sanjukta Parasor, also known as the “Iron Lady of Assam” for her counter-insurgency work in the Northeast, has taken charge as Inspector General of the Central Reserve Police Force’s elite CoBRA unit, becoming the first woman officer to head the specialised jungle-warfare force.

Parasor, a 2006-batch IPS officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, brings to the post extensive experience in counter-insurgency operations, field policing and national security investigations.

The CRPF headquarters issued the appointment order last week. Parasor succeeds 1996-batch IPS officer Danesh Rana as the IG, CoBRA. “This is the first time that the 10-battalion-strong CoBRA of the CRPF will be headed by a woman officer,” a senior officer said. Two CoBRA units were recently deployed by the CRPF to check armed violence in Manipur.

54.title: Assam IPS Officer Sanjukta Parashar Becomes First Woman to Head CRPF’s CoBRA Unit
54.description: Dr Sanjukta Parashar, a 2006-batch Indian Police Service officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre widely known as the “Iron Lady of Assam,” has assumed charge as
54.text:
Dr Sanjukta Parashar, a 2006-batch Indian Police Service officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre widely known as the “Iron Lady of Assam,” has assumed charge as Inspector General of the Central Reserve Police Force’s elite Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA). She is the first woman officer to command the specialised jungle-warfare force.

The CRPF headquarters issued the order last week. Parashar succeeds 1996-batch IPS officer Danesh Rana. A senior officer told PTI that this is the first time the ten-battalion CoBRA force will be headed by a woman.

The Ministry of Home Affairs had earlier appointed her as Inspector General in the CRPF on central deputation, with orders issued on 6 August 2026. She has now taken operational charge of CoBRA.

About CoBRA

CoBRA, or Commando Battalion for Resolute Action, was raised by the CRPF in 2008–09 to conduct intelligence-based jungle and guerrilla warfare against Left Wing Extremism in several states and against insurgency in parts of the Northeast. Its commandos are trained for long-range operations in dense forests, ambushes and counter-ambushes, IED threats, and precision action against armed militants. The unit has operated extensively in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha and Maharashtra. Two CoBRA units were recently deployed in Manipur to check armed violence. The Ministry of Home Affairs has credited CoBRA commandos with operations that contributed to the end of Maoist violence in the country in March 2026.

Career and background

Born on 3 October 1979 in Assam, Parashar studied Political Science at Indraprastha College for Women, University of Delhi, and later completed a Master’s degree, MPhil and PhD in International Relations and American foreign policy at Jawaharlal Nehru University. She secured All India Rank 85 in the 2005 UPSC Civil Services Examination and chose the IPS over the IAS. She joined the service on 29 August 2006 and became the first Assamese woman IPS officer posted directly in Assam under the cadre.

Her early postings included Makum and Udalguri, where she handled ethnic clashes. As Superintendent of Police in Sonitpur, she led 16 major encounter operations in 15 months, in which 16 militants were killed and 64 arrested. She frequently accompanied personnel into forest terrain, including operations involving Assam Police commandos and CoBRA troops. These field assignments earned her the popular title “Iron Lady of Assam.” She later served as Deputy Inspector General in the National Investigation Agency, handling national-security and counter-terrorism investigations.

She has received the President’s Police Medal for Distinguished Service, the Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training (2022), and the Rani Gaidinliu Zeliang Award.

Significance of the appointment

The posting combines Parashar’s operational experience in Assam’s insurgency-affected forests with her investigative work at the NIA. For a force whose core tasks include jungle warfare, intelligence-led operations and adaptation in hostile terrain, that combination is regarded as directly relevant. The appointment is also viewed as a milestone for women officers in operational command of India’s paramilitary forces.

Parashar now leads one of the CRPF’s most demanding specialised units at a time when CoBRA continues to be employed in remaining Left Wing Extremism pockets and in sensitive internal-security theatres such as Manipur.

55.title: Manipur: Security forces arrest three insurgents, recover arms and explosives
55.description: Security forces arrest three insurgent cadres and recover rifles, ammunition, explosives and communication equipment in multiple operations.
55.text: Imphal: Security forces arrested three suspected insurgent cadres and recovered a large cache of arms, ammunition and explosives during a series of counter-insurgency operations across Manipur on Monday, officials said on Tuesday. In one of the operations, personnel from Tengnoupal Police Station and the 3 Assam Rifles acted on specific intelligence and launched a search near Border Pillar 87. The operation led to the arrest of two alleged cadres of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA). The arrested individuals were identified as 23-year-old Vishwanath Singh alias Athouba, a resident of Bishnupur district, and 42-year-old Ibomcha Singh alias Chingamba from Imphal West district. In a separate operation at Yairipok Bazar, a joint team of Thoubal District Police and the 31 Assam Rifles apprehended an alleged active member of the United National Liberation Front (UNLF-Ningolmacha faction). The accused was identified as 34-year-old Korimayum Sarif Khan, a resident of Yairipok Top Laikon in Imphal East district. Security personnel recovered a mobile phone with a SIM card and Rs 5,000 in cash from his possession. Meanwhile, the Kakching District Police Commando (CDO) and 46 Assam Rifles conducted a targeted operation in the Wangoo Nongyaikhong area based on intelligence inputs. During the operation, security personnel apprehended 25-year-old Sorokhaibam Rakesh Singh, son of late S. Shamu Singh. Officials said interrogation of the suspect subsequently led to the recovery of a concealed cache of weapons and ammunition from the area. The seized items included an INSAS rifle, a .303 rifle, four magazines, 116 live rounds of different calibres, 31 empty 12-bore cartridge cases and 750 grams of gunpowder. In another operation, a joint team of Khongsang Police and the CRPF’s Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) carried out a Cordon and Search Operation (CASO) at Irang village in the Taobam area of Noney district. The search resulted in the recovery of a single-barrel breech-loading (SBBL) gun, nine live rounds and two Baofeng wireless communication sets along with a charging unit. The arrested individuals and all recovered arms, ammunition and other materials have been handed over to the respective police stations for further investigation and legal proceedings.
