56.title: The First Lady Boss Of India's Elite Commando Force
56.description: Sanjukta Parashar, an IPS officer with a formidable background in counter-insurgency, has made history by becoming the first woman inspector general of the CRPF's elite CoBRA force.
56.text:
Sanjukta Parashar, an IPS officer with a formidable background in counter-insurgency, has made history by becoming the first woman inspector general of the CRPF's elite CoBRA force.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar, the first woman inspector general of CoBRA. Photograph: Kind courtesy @xanjuta/Instagram

Key Points Sanjukta Parashar, a 2006-batch IPS officer, has been appointed as the inspector general of CoBRA, making her the first woman to lead the elite force.

Known as the 'Iron Lady of Assam', Parashar has extensive experience in counter-insurgency operations in the Northeast.

CoBRA commandos specialise in jungle warfare, long-range operations, ambush tactics, and countering IED threats in difficult terrain.

Parashar's career graph covers field policing and national-security investigations with the National Investigation Agency.

Sanjukta Parashar, the 2006-batch Assam-Meghalaya cadre IPS officer known for her frontline role in counter-insurgency operations in Assam, has become the first woman to head the Central Reserve Police Force's elite CoBRA unit.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar. Photograph: Kind courtesy @xanjuta/Instagram

Parashar has been appointed inspector general of the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action, or CoBRA, the CRPF's specialised force trained for jungle warfare and counter-insurgency operations.

Her appointment marks a significant milestone for women officers in India's Central Armed Police Forces and brings her career back to the kind of jungle and counter-insurgency operations that first made her nationally known.

From the insurgency-hit forests of Assam to the command of the CRPF's elite jungle-warfare force, Parashar's career has been shaped by some of the country's most demanding security assignments.

Assam's Forests To CoBRA

Parashar, a 2006-batch IPS officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, has spent much of her career in the field, leading and participating in counter-insurgency operations in the North East.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar. Photograph: Kind courtesy @xanjuta/Instagram

She shot to national prominence during her tenure as superintendent of police in Sonitpur, where she led operations against insurgents in difficult forest terrain.

Her field operations brought her face-to-face with militants as well as the hazards of the terrain, including torrential rain, fast-flowing rivers and elephants.

In 2015, she was reported to have led the Assam police and CRPF personnel during operations against militants in the forests of Sonitpur.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar. Photograph: Kind courtesy Sanjukta Parashar/Facebook

CoBRA was created as the CRPF's specialised force for guerrilla and jungle warfare and operates in some of India's most challenging insurgency-affected areas.

CoBRA commandos are trained to operate in some of the most difficult terrains in the country.

Their specialised role includes long-range operations in dense forests, ambush and counter-ambush operations, dealing with IED threats and intelligence-based action against armed insurgents.

A return to the central force

The ministry of home affairs appointed Parashar as an inspector general in the CRPF on central deputation in August 2026.

Before moving to the CRPF, she was serving as inspector general of police, CID-I, in Assam.

She had earlier spent several years on central deputation with the National Investigation Agency, where she served as superintendent of police and later deputy inspector general.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar. Photograph: Kind courtesy @xanjuta/Instagram

A career built in difficult terrain

For Parashar, the new assignment brings her back to an operational environment familiar from her years in Assam -- one where knowledge of terrain, intelligence and quick decision-making are critical.

During her tenure as Sonitpur SP, she personally led patrols deep into forests and worked alongside Assam police commandos and CoBRA personnel during operations against insurgents.

Those experiences helped establish her reputation as a field officer willing to operate alongside her personnel in some of the state's most difficult areas.

More than a decade later, she will now be at the helm of the very force whose personnel once operated alongside her in Assam's forests.

IMAGE: Sanjukta Parashar. Photograph: Kind courtesy Sanjukta Parashar/Facebook

Parashar studied political science at Indraprastha College, University of Delhi, and later pursued higher studies in international relations at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

In 2006, she secured All India Rank 85 in the UPSC civil services examination and chose the Indian Police Service.

During her tenure with the National Investigation Agency, Parashar worked on national security investigations involving terrorism and extremist networks and coordinated with multiple investigative and security agencies.

Now, at the head of CoBRA, her career brings together the two strands of her experience -- the realities of counter-insurgency on the ground and the wider demands of national security investigations.

Photographs curated by Manisha Kotian/Rediff

57.title: Assam NCC cadets Rajasree Roy, Bishal Roy summit 6,546-Metre Mt. Chalung
57.description: LCpl Rajasree Roy and LCpl Bishal Roy of 4 Assam BN NCC summited the 6,546-metre Mt Chalung as part of a 14-member expedition. Their feat, as the only participants from Northeast India, drew praise from the NCC and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.
57.text:
LCpl Rajasree Roy and LCpl Bishal Roy of 4 Assam BN NCC have successfully summited Mt. Chalung, standing at an altitude of 6,546 metres, bringing recognition to Assam’s Barak Valley and the Northeast.

The duo were the only participants from Northeast India among the 14-member expedition team that successfully undertook the challenging mountaineering expedition.

Their achievement has been welcomed by the NCC community, including NCC Group Silchar and the NCC Directorate NER, Shillong, with the feat being hailed as a moment of pride for the region.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma congratulated both cadets on their remarkable achievement and lauded their courage, endurance, discipline and determination.

The successful summit marks a notable accomplishment for the two NCC cadets and highlights their commitment to mountaineering and challenging outdoor expeditions.

58.title: Rakhine traders clash With Mara volunteers in Mizoram, duty post set ablaze
58.description: A dispute over the movement of goods across the Salalui river escalated into a clash between Rakhine traders and Mara volunteers in Mizoram’s Siaha district
58.text:
Aizawl, Sept 16: Traders and transporters of Rakhine state in Myanmar clashed with volunteers of the Mara Thyutlia Py near Khaikhy village in south Mizoram’s Siaha district on Monday, setting a duty post of the volunteers on fire. The dispute reportedly arose over the movement of goods across the Salalui river.

The incident took place on the riverbank near Khaikhy, a key point for the movement of goods between south Mizoram and Rakhine. The confrontation allegedly occurred after the Rakhine traders complained that they were unable to ferry adequate goods in boats from the Indian side to Myanmar.

According to reports, the traders and boat operators approached the Mara volunteers manning the duty post, which oversees the transportation of goods in the area. A heated argument reportedly followed after the traders demanded that commodities be made available for transportation across the river.

When the volunteers left the post to avoid a physical confrontation, the traders and transporters allegedly vandalised the post and set it ablaze.

The Mara Thyutlia Py members alleged that pages of registers carrying names of boat operators transporting commodities, and account books were also ripped out. They further alleged that a sum of about Rs 10,000 in cash was also missing after the incident.

News of the confrontation prompted young people from nearby Lopu village to rush to Khaikhy. Assam Rifles personnel stationed at Lopu also moved to the area, following which the Rakhine traders and transporters withdrew from the village.

Meanwhile Mara Thyutlia Py leaders of Siaha said that a team from the organisation’s Phura sub-headquarters was sent to Khaikhy on Tuesday to make an on-the-spot assessment. The team is expected to submit its report to the Mara Thyutlia Py headquarters, which will take a final decision on the matter.

Khaikhy has emerged as a hub of unregulated cross-border trade between south Mizoram and Rakhine state. Commodities from India are transported across the Salalui river to Salachhuah village in Rakhine, with some goods also reportedly reaching the Chin state.

Local sources said more than 100 trucks bring commodities to Khaikhy each day, while over 100 boats are engaged in carrying the goods across the river.

Residents alleged that the Arakan Army which operates in Rakhine, Paletwa and adjoining areas of southern Chin, is also involved in the lucrative cross-border trade.

59.title: Manipur Police arrest four insurgent cadres in separate operations
59.description: Manipur Police and security forces arrested four insurgent cadres in separate operations across districts on September 14 and 15. The action also included a theft arrest, with police saying the stolen Honda Activa had already been recovered.
59.text:
Manipur Police and security forces arrested four insurgent cadres, including members of PRE-PAK, KYKL and RPF/PLA, in separate operations across the state on September 14 and 15.

A cadre of the PRE-PAK was arrested near Border Pillar 86 in Tengnoupal district on September 14. The operation was launched by the Assam Rifles and Tengnoupal Police based on inputs from 3 Assam Rifles, which were corroborated by district police. The arrested man was identified as 30-year-old Nongthongbam Manithoi alias Ningjaba, a resident of Awangpoksang Khullen in Imphal West district.

On September 15, a joint team of the CDO Kakching, 43 Assam Rifles and 46 Assam Rifles arrested an active KYKL cadre from his locality in Hiyanglam under Hiyanglam Police Station. The accused was identified as 27-year-old Elangbam Langam Singh of Hiyanglam Warakhong Manung in Kakching district.

In a separate operation the same day, a combined team of CDO-Imphal West and CDO-Thoubal arrested a suspected RPF/PLA member from a rented house near Langjing CRPF Gate No. 1. The operation was conducted in the Langjing area under Patsoi Police Station based on information corroborated with 33 Assam Rifles. 61.title: BRO moots strategies for infrastructure in North East
61.description:
Jitendra Prasad, VSM, Additional Director General, Border Roads Organisation (Additional DGBR), addressed a special session on Wednesday at the Infra Build Northeast Conference organised by Indian Infrastructure at Guwahati on 16 September 2026.

Speaking on building roads in remote and difficult
61.text:
Jitendra Prasad, VSM, Additional Director General, Border Roads Organisation (Additional DGBR), addressed a special session on Wednesday at the Infra Build Northeast Conference organised by Indian Infrastructure at Guwahati on 16 September 2026.

Speaking on building roads in remote and difficult terrain, Prasad shared field insights from his 36 years of BRO’s experience in the most challenging sectors, including the Northeast region.

He further stressed four key themes: Firstly, key challenges during the planning and execution stage: Quality of DPRs, quality assurance, and maintenance post-construction were the challenges highlighted by him, secondly, new techniques & technology: use of LiDAR & drone surveys, AI and digital twins for project management, use of mechanised and automated machines/equipments, new generation pavement material, precast modular construction technology and specialised tech like Rejupave (Bio fuel) for cold climate and high altitude area were highlighted, thirdly bottlenecks and strategies: delays in utility shifting, extreme monsoon and short working season causes hindrances and frequent disruptions. He emphasised that all stakeholders should work in a synchronised manner to overcome them and, fourthly, priorities and upcoming opportunities: prioritising strategic frontier connectivity, development of alternate axes to create redundancy, by-passes to towns & cities, connecting tourism centres. He apprised regarding huge upcoming opportunities like high-speed economic corridors, road connectivity with ASEAN countries, Bridges over the Brahmaputra & other major rivers.

In his closing remarks, he said, “Let us build the Infrastructure — that connects the remote villages —connects the border to meet the National Security — Connects the economic hubs to ensure economic growth & more importantly that connects aspiration with opportunities, North East with Nation, India with the World & for the India of 2047.”

63.title: 3rd DGAR Hockey Tournament kicks off at Khuman Lampak Hockey Stadium in Manipur
63.description: The third edition of the DGAR Hockey Tournament for men and women commenced at the Khuman Lampak Hockey Stadium in Imphal on September 18.
63.text:
The third edition of the DGAR Hockey Tournament for men and women commenced at the Khuman Lampak Hockey Stadium in Imphal on September 18.

The tournament, jointly organised by the Assam Rifles and Manipur Hockey, will continue till September 28. The event aims to promote unity, discipline and sportsmanship among the youth of Manipur through sporting activities.

Addressing the inaugural function as the chief guest, retired Lieutenant General Konsam Himalay Singh appreciated the organisers for conducting the tournament amid the prevailing instability in the state. He said sporting events such as the hockey tournament can help nurture sporting spirit while also contributing to peace and unity.

Singh highlighted Manipur’s rich hockey legacy and its historical association with the sport. He noted that the indigenous game of Kangjei, or Sagol Kangjei, bears similarities to modern hockey and said several players from Manipur have gone on to represent the country at international sporting platforms, including the Olympic Games.

He encouraged all participating teams and players to give their best throughout the tournament.

A total of 10 teams are expected to compete in the men’s category, while five teams will participate in the women’s category.

The tournament carries a cash prize of ₹1 lakh for the winners and ₹75,000 for the runners-up. Organisers have also introduced a running trophy for the tournament from this edition.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by senior officials of the Assam Rifles and Manipur Police, along with eminent personalities and other guests.

64.title: Army Mountaineering Expedition summits Mt Khangchengyao in North Sikkim
64.description: Kolkata, Sep 18 (SocialNews.XYZ) The Indian Army’s mountaineering expedition from the Eastern Command’s Spear Corps successfully summited Mt Khangchengyao in North Sikkim on Friday, September 18, 2026. The expedition had been flagged off on August... - Social News XYZ
64.text:
Kolkata, Sep 18 (SocialNews.XYZ) The Indian Army’s mountaineering expedition from the Eastern Command’s Spear Corps successfully summited Mt Khangchengyao in North Sikkim on Friday, September 18, 2026.

The expedition had been flagged off on August 18, 2026, from Rayang Military Station in Arunachal Pradesh. Mt Khangchengyao, at 6,889 metres, is considered an extremely challenging mountain to climb. It has steep ice walls and unpredictable weather conditions.

Mt Khangchengyao is the fourth-highest peak in Sikkim and the tenth-highest in India. In this part of the Himalayan region, locals identify most of the mountains, especially the high peaks, as deities. Peaks are also differentiated by gender. Locals deeply revere Mt Khangchengyao, identifying it as a male mountain. Local legend holds that it gets angry when a woman sets foot near it, and folklore suggests the weather worsens whenever a woman climber approaches the base camp.

The mountain has a unique dome-shaped structure without a pointed peak. Its nearly rounded top tapers down its sides at 75–80 degree angles, making climbing extremely difficult.

Officials said such expeditions help build teamwork and camaraderie among troops while also training them to handle challenges in extreme conditions.

“Under the aegis of Eastern Command, the Indian Army Mountaineering Expedition team under Spear Corps displayed exceptional courage and successfully summited Mt Khangchengyao (6,889 m), achieving a historic milestone. Defying sub-zero temperatures, treacherous terrain and punishing high altitudes, the team triumphed through sheer physical endurance and flawless camaraderie. This monumental ascent stands as a soaring testament to the indomitable spirit of the Indian Army, proving once again that no height is insurmountable when met with relentless resolve,” the Eastern Command posted on X.

The Spear Corps, also known as III Corps, is a Mountain (Holding) Corps with troops trained in high-altitude operations. It is headquartered in Dimapur, Nagaland, and is involved in counter-insurgency operations in the northeastern states. It also plays a major role in managing the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. The Corps also participated in the famous Battle of Walong during the Indo-China War of 1962.

Source: IANS

65.title: Suspected ULFA cadre surrenders before Assam Rifles at Pangsau
65.description: A suspected ULFA cadre surrendered before the Assam Rifles at Pangsau. The move marks a development in ongoing efforts to address insurgency-related activity in the region.
65.text:
In a significant development, a 23-year-old suspected ULFA cadre surrendered before the Assam Rifles at Pangsau, according to available information.

The surrendered individual has been identified as Dilip Axom, alias Kamal Sarania, aged 23, son of Prasanna Sarania, a resident of Simla village under Simla Police Station in Baksa district of Assam.

The surrender comes as a development in the security forces’ efforts to address insurgency-related activities in the region. The individual’s identity and residential details were confirmed in connection with the surrender.

Following the surrender, further details regarding his alleged association with the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA), his activities and the circumstances that led him to surrender are expected to emerge.

Authorities are likely to carry out the necessary questioning and verification procedures as part of the process following the surrender. No further details regarding weapons, ammunition or other items surrendered along with him were available in the information provided.

66.title: Assam Rifles showcases operational preparedness, capabilities in Agartala
66.description: Agartala, Sep 18 (SocialNews.XYZ) The Assam Rifles on Friday organised a display of weapons and equipment in Agartala to showcase its capabilities, operational preparedness and role in safeguarding the nation and maintaining security in the... - Social News XYZ
66.text:
Agartala, Sep 18 (SocialNews.XYZ) The Assam Rifles on Friday organised a display of weapons and equipment in Agartala to showcase its capabilities, operational preparedness and role in safeguarding the nation and maintaining security in the Northeast.

A defence spokesman said that the Assam Rifles organised a weapons and equipment display at Saheed Bhagat Singh Youth Hostel in Agartala on Friday for NCC (National Cadet Corps) cadets as part of its continued efforts to enhance awareness about the role, capabilities and operational preparedness of the force. The event witnessed enthusiastic participation by cadets and provided them the opportunity to gain first-hand knowledge of various weapons, equipment and specialised systems employed by Assam Rifles, he said.

The cadets actively interacted with Assam Rifles personnel and inquired about the capabilities, employment and operational significance of the weapons.

According to the defence spokesman, the initiative also served as an important platform to motivate and inspire the youth towards a career in the Armed Forces and Assam Rifles. The interaction provided the participants with insight into the professional ethos, commitment and role of Assam Rifles.

The event reaffirmed Assam Rifles’ commitment towards youth engagement, nation-building and fostering a spirit of patriotism and service among the younger generation. Such outreach initiatives continue to strengthen the bond between Assam Rifles and the people of the Northeast, the official noted.

Assam Rifles units are posted across several states in Northeastern India, including Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Assam and Tripura. While insurgency has been brought under control in most of the states, there are continuous attempts by banned outfits to regroup and build up networks through extortion and recruitment of youths. The paramilitary force has been playing a vital role in curbing organised drug trafficking networks in the Northeast, especially in Mizoram, Manipur, Assam and Tripura.

"The Assam Rifles maintains constant vigil on activities involving insurgent groups. Insurgents operate across state boundaries to evade the police. The insurgent groups are also linked to each other and provide shelter to each other's cadres. A strong intelligence network is required to get to them," a senior official said.

Source: IANS

68.title: Hyundai Exter Collides with Mahindra Armado Army Truck in Gangtok Head-On Accident
68.description: Hyundai Exter SUV involved in head-on collision with Indian Army's Mahindra Armado truck in Gangtok,Sikkim. No injuries reported despite severe front-end damage to the micro SUV.
68.text:
We have come across multiple videos on the internet where we see exceptional road discipline, lane discipline, and civic sense among drivers from Eastern Indian states like Sikkim. It looks like even some of the most disciplined drivers on the road are not immune to accidents. A new video has surfaced online where we see a Hyundai Exter that has crashed into an Army truck. The video has already gone viral on multiple social media platforms.

In the video, we see a Hyundai Exter and an Indian Army truck involved in a head-on collision. The accident was reported from Sikkim’s Gangtok. Based on the reports surfacing online, the accident happened near Manipal Gate at 5th Mile in the Tadong region. In the video, we do not get an actual idea of how the accident happened. It does not share details on who was at fault here.

We see the Army truck, which is a Mahindra Armado, that has crashed into a Hyundai Exter SUV. There is not much damage to the Indian Army’s truck, but that is not the case with the Hyundai Exter. The micro SUV’s front end is completely damaged. It looks like a high-speed crash because we can see one of the wheels of the Exter lying on the road as well. The front of the SUV, including the bonnet, bumper, grille, headlamps, and fender, is completely damaged.

The airbags have deployed on time, and we can see the same in the video. While the front is completely damaged, the cabin and the pillars of the vehicle look intact. It looks like the Exter absorbed the impact pretty well and kept the occupants safe. The reports suggest that the occupants in the car and the Army truck did not suffer any injuries.

Mahindra Armado

The Army truck seen here is the Mahindra Armado, which is an Armoured Light Specialist Vehicle (ALSV). It is an indigenous 4x4 tactical combat vehicle designed and manufactured by Mahindra Defence Systems for the Indian Armed Forces. Mahindra Defence Systems is a subsidiary of the Mahindra Group, and the LSV has been designed specifically for the armed forces.

The Armado is a modular-type vehicle based on the Mahindra Axe and is built to be maintenance-friendly. It can be upgraded and configured for a wide range of roles. It can be modified into a weapons carrier, a reconnaissance vehicle, or a border security vehicle. The Armado offers STANAG Level 2 and B7-level ballistic protection and comes with a payload capacity of 1,000 kg.

The SUV, or Army truck, uses a 3.2-litre turbocharged, direct-injection diesel engine that generates 215 bhp and 500 Nm of torque. It has a top speed of 120 kmph and comes with a proper 4WD setup. It also gets differential locks and a self-recovery winch in case it gets stuck in a tricky situation. The engine on this truck is mated to a 4-speed automatic transmission, and the SUV comes with 17-inch wheels with rough-terrain tyres and independent suspension.

69.title: NCC Northeast ADG meets Tripura CM, discusses expansion of cadet activities
69.description: Major General Anurag Vij, Additional Director General of the NCC Directorate, North Eastern Region, met Tripura Chief Minister Prof Dr Manik Saha in Agartala on September 19 to discuss measures to strengthen and expand National Cadet Corps activities across the state.
69.text:
Major General Anurag Vij, Additional Director General of the NCC Directorate, North Eastern Region, met Tripura Chief Minister Prof Dr Manik Saha in Agartala on September 19 to discuss measures to strengthen and expand National Cadet Corps activities across the state.

The meeting was attended by Brigadier Anand Raj Singh, Group Commander, Silchar, and Colonel N S Baath, Commanding Officer of the 13 Tripura Battalion NCC.

According to the NCC Directorate, North Eastern Region, the discussions focused on increasing the reach of NCC among Tripura’s youth, particularly those living in remote and rural areas.

The meeting explored measures to expand NCC coverage, increase the number of participating educational institutions and cadets, and strengthen infrastructure to provide greater access to NCC training and youth-development programmes.

The possibility of organising national-level integration camps in Agartala was also discussed. Such camps provide cadets from different parts of the country an opportunity to interact while promoting national integration and cultural exchange.

The NCC leadership and state government representatives also discussed expanding opportunities for cadets in military training, adventure activities, trekking, camps and leadership programmes.

Greater emphasis was placed on career guidance and creating awareness among young people about opportunities in the Armed Forces and other career avenues.

The NCC leadership also sought continued cooperation and support from the Tripura government for training activities, camps and other youth-development initiatives.

The discussions are expected to support efforts to broaden the NCC network in Tripura and provide more young people, particularly those from underserved areas, with access to its training and development programmes.

71.title: 1,800 Manipur residents mark Nambol ambush anniversary, honour Assam Rifles personnel
71.description: Nearly 1,800 people gathered at Nambol Sabal Leikai in Manipur’s Bishnupur district on Saturday to commemorate the first anniversary of the Nambol ambush. The gathering paid tribute to two Assam Rifles personnel who lost their lives in the attack while returning from flood-relief duties.
71.text:
New Delhi: Residents of Manipur came together in large numbers on September 19 to mark the first anniversary of the Nambol ambush and honour the sacrifice of two Assam Rifles personnel.

Around 1,800 people, including local residents, community representatives and youths, participated in the solidarity and remembrance event at Nambol Sabal Leikai in Bishnupur district.

The gathering paid tribute to Naib Subedar Shyam Gurung and Rifleman Ranjeet Singh Kashyap of 33 Assam Rifles. Both personnel lost their lives in an armed ambush on September 19, 2025.

Returning From Relief Duty

A column of 33 Assam Rifles was returning after carrying out flood-relief operations in the Imphal Valley when it came under attack at Nambol Sabal Leikai.

Naib Subedar Gurung and Rifleman Kashyap lost their lives in the ambush, while five other Assam Rifles personnel sustained injuries.

The anniversary gathering recalled that the two personnel were returning from humanitarian duties undertaken to assist people affected by floods when they were attacked.

Residents Pay Homage

Participants paid homage to the fallen personnel and remembered their courage, dedication and commitment to serving the people.

The large turnout reflected the solidarity and mutual respect shared between the local community and the Assam Rifles. Residents also acknowledged the force’s role in supporting people during emergencies and natural disasters.

Call For Peace

The remembrance event reaffirmed the community’s commitment to peace, harmony and peaceful coexistence in Manipur.

The gathering also highlighted the importance of collectively honouring security personnel who make the ultimate sacrifice while serving the country and its people.

A year after the ambush, residents of Nambol remembered the fallen personnel and honoured their service. The event sought to ensure that their courage and sacrifice continue to inspire future generations.

72.title: Thousands gather in Manipur’s Nambol to honour Assam Rifles personnel killed in 2025 ambush
72.description: Residents, community leaders and youth in Nambol gathered to honour two Assam Rifles personnel killed in the 2025 ambush. The first-anniversary tribute also renewed calls for peace, harmony and coexistence in Manipur.
72.text:
Around 1,800 residents gathered at Nambol in Manipur on September 19 to mark the first anniversary of the Nambol ambush and pay tribute to two Assam Rifles personnel who lost their lives in the attack on September 19, 2025.

The remembrance event saw participation from local residents, community representatives and youth, who paid homage to Naib Subedar Shyam Gurung and Rifleman Ranjeet Singh Kashyap of 33 Assam Rifles and expressed solidarity with the force.

On September 19, 2025, a column of 33 Assam Rifles personnel returning from flood-relief duties in the Imphal Valley came under an armed ambush at Nambol Sabal Leikai in Bishnupur district, according to the press release. The attack resulted in the deaths of the two personnel, while five others were injured.

The gathering recalled that the personnel were returning from humanitarian duties carried out in support of people affected by floods when they came under attack. Participants paid tribute to the two fallen personnel and acknowledged their courage, dedication and service.

The event also highlighted the participation of local communities in remembering the fallen personnel and reaffirmed calls for peace, harmony and peaceful coexistence in the state.

The first-anniversary programme concluded with a collective tribute to the two Assam Rifles personnel, with participants remembering their sacrifice and service to the people.

73.title: Serving Manipur Rifles havildar arrested in extortion case, pistol seized
73.description: The arrests come months after another state police personnel faced allegations of links to banned militants
73.text:
Imphal, Sept 19: Manipur Police have arrested three persons, including a serving Manipur Rifles havildar, for their alleged involvement in extortion.

A team of Imphal West district police commandos, acting on reliable information, arrested the three from their respective residences in and around the Singjamei Wangma area on Thursday, police said.

The arrested persons have been identified as Okram Priyokumar Singh, 40, alias Priyo, son of late Okram Nillamani Singh, and Thongram Sunson Singh, 34, alias Uttam, son of Thongram Bimol Singh, both residents of Singjamei Waikhom Leikai in Imphal West district.

The third accused is Waikhom Amarjit Singh, 44, son of W Nilachandra Singh, a resident of Singjamei Wangma Pebiya Pandit Leikai in Imphal East district.

Police said Amarjit Singh is a serving havildar of the 1st Manipur Rifles Battalion. A 9 mm pistol, along with a magazine containing four rounds, was recovered from his possession, they added.

Manipur Police shared details and photographs of the arrested persons on social media, identifying the three and confirming the recovery of the firearm from the serving Manipur Rifles personnel.

In a separate incident, a hand grenade was found near the residential gate of Shri Shri Gouragovind Girls College principal Lairenlakpam Jabotsakhi at Bashikhong Wangkhei Loumanbi in Imphal East district on Thursday morning.

The grenade was found around 6 am and was subsequently picked up by police, officials said.

The latest arrests come against the backdrop of previous instances of state security personnel being accused of links with banned armed groups.

In February this year, security forces arrested a 43-year-old Manipur Police constable driver for his alleged involvement in the recruitment of cadres for the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (MFL).

The constable driver was arrested from his locality at Utlou Chanura under Nambol police station in Bishnupur district.

74.title: #FactCheck: False Claim Says Indian Army Shot Two Women, Burnt Houses in Manipur
74.description: #FactCheck: False Claim Says Indian Army Shot Two Women, Burnt Houses in Manipur
74.text:
Introduction

Online Gaming has gained popularity over the past few years, attracting young players worldwide and global concerns. In response to the growing fame of this industry, the Indian government has recently announced introducing a set of regulations to address various concerns and ensure a safer and more regulated online gaming environment. In this blog post, we will explore the critical aspects of these regulations and their impact on the gaming industry.

Why are Regulations needed?

Recently some games faced a ban in India – games that involve betting, games that can be harmful to the user, and games that involve a factor of addiction. Furthermore, with rising popularity, With the exponential rise of online gaming platforms in India, extensive laws to safeguard players and ensure fair gameplay needs to be implemented. Players’ protection is one of the critical factors addressing the issues which involve online addiction, underage involvement, fraud, and data privacy has become critical for the well-being of Indian gamers.

Regulatory Ambiguity: The previous legislative structure, such as the outmoded Public Gambling Act of 1867, required an update to fit the digital gambling age fully.

Outline of the New Regulations

Implementing new regulations for online gaming in India represents the government’s commitment to addressing different issues and ensuring a safer and more regulated gaming sector. Let’s have a look at these rules in detail:

National-Level Standards: The Indian government is currently working on creating national-level standards to standardise online gaming practices across all states. These rules attempt to create a uniform platform for both operators and participants. The government has also made an announcement to set SRO within 90 days to regulate online gaming.

Licencing and Compliance: To legally operate in the Indian market, online gaming firms must secure licences. The operator’s financial soundness, security measures, and adherence to responsible gaming practices will be scrutinised throughout the licencing process. Operators will need to comply with the regulations in order to maintain operations.

Measures to Promote Ethical Gaming: The new regulations emphasise player protection and ethical gaming practices. This includes steps like age verification to prevent underage involvement, self-exclusion choices for gamers who want to limit their gaming activities, and adopting tools like session limits and reality checks to promote responsible gaming.

Data Privacy: Recognising the importance of data privacy, the laws are intended to contain protections for protecting user data. To safeguard sensitive player information from unauthorised access or exploitation, online gambling operators must comply with data protection regulations and deploy strong security measures.

Restrictions on Advertising and Marketing: The legislation may limit the advertising and marketing of online gaming platforms. The emphasis will be on eliminating aggressive marketing tactics that target vulnerable people, such as kids. Stricter standards for ad content and placement may be implemented.

Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money Laundering Measures: To combat criminal activity within the gaming ecosystem, the new legislation will almost certainly force online gambling companies to employ anti-fraud and anti-money laundering measures. Operators may need to set up mechanisms to detect fraud, report suspicious activity, and work with law enforcement.

Consumer Grievance Redressal: The legislation may emphasise the construction of efficient channels for resolving consumer complaints. Players should be able to report difficulties, seek resolution, and offer feedback on their play experiences through channels. The objective is to create a transparent and accountable conflict resolution mechanism.

Impact on Online Gaming Ecosystem

Adopting new laws for online gambling in India will likely have several consequences for the gaming industry. Let us look at some of these consequences:

Increased Player Trust: Implementing restrictions will increase player confidence in online gaming platforms. Establishing clear rules and procedures and steps to safeguard participants’ interests will develop a sense of trust and transparency. This can lead to increased participation and engagement in the gaming community.

Industry Consolidation: Stricter restrictions may result in industry consolidation. Compliance with the new legislation would need resources and investments, which might favour more prominent and more established gambling firms. Smaller and more non-compliant operators may find it challenging to fulfil regulatory standards, resulting in a more consolidated gaming sector.

Technological Progress: The requirement to comply with rules could lead to technological advancements in the online gambling sector. Operators may invest in modern identity verification systems, fraud detection methods, and responsible gaming solutions to satisfy their regulatory requirements. This can result in technological breakthroughs that improve gamers’ overall gaming experience.

Foreign Investment and Collaboration: Clear laws might entice overseas investors to enter the Indian gaming business. The regulated environment may appeal to international gambling enterprises looking to enter or extend their presence in India. Collaborations between Indian and foreign gaming firms may also expand, resulting in the sharing of experience, resources, and the production of high-quality gaming products.

Legal Clarity: Implementing particular laws would give online gambling operators and users clearer legal standards. This transparency can eliminate ambiguity and possible legal issues, allowing stakeholders to navigate the gaming ecosystem with better confidence and knowledge.

Contribution to the Indian Economy: A well-regulated online gaming business has the potential to contribute to the Indian economy. It has the potential to create jobs, attract investment, and produce tax money for the government. The economic effect of the gaming ecosystem is expected to increase as it grows under the new restrictions.

Challenges and Future Approach

One of the toughest challenges will be the efficient implementation and enforcement of the new regulations. Consistency in applying the legislation across multiple jurisdictions and guaranteeing compliance by all operators would necessitate comprehensive monitoring and regulatory measures. Developing suitable enforcement organisations and transparent standards for reporting and dealing with noncompliance will be critical. Besides this, online gaming is open to more than area-specific and many gaming platforms and operates internationally. Ensuring cross-border operations is a big challenge in addressing jurisdictional challenges will be complex. Collaborative efforts between nations can regulate cross-border online gaming. There may be increased collaboration between Indian and foreign gaming firms, resulting in the exchange of information, skills, and resources. This partnership can help the Indian gaming sector flourish while attracting foreign players and investments.

Esports Development: Esports have grown in popularity worldwide, and India is no exception. The Indian esports business has the potential to thrive with proper regulation and support, drawing both players and viewers. Esports-specific factors like player contracts, tournament integrity, and licencing requirements may be addressed in the regulations.

Conclusion

Despite obstacles, India’s new online gambling legislation can potentially establish a safer and more regulated gaming sector. the future depends on successful implementation, adjusting to a shifting landscape, finding the correct balance between regulation and innovation, and promoting ethical gaming practices. The Indian online gaming business can develop sustainably with the appropriate strategy, benefiting gamers and the broader economy.

75.title: Indian Army’s 2 JAT Battalion scales 6,889-metre Mt Khangchengyao in Sikkim
75.source: The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People
75.description: OUR CORRESPONDENTITANAGAR: A 12-member mountaineering team of the Indian Army's 2 JAT Battalion (Mooltan), led by Major Vatti Chandra Kumar, has successfully sc
75.text:
OUR CORRESPONDENT

ITANAGAR: A 12-member mountaineering team of the Indian Army's 2 JAT Battalion (Mooltan), led by Major Vatti Chandra Kumar, has successfully scaled Mt Khangchengyao (6,889 metres), in North Sikkim, further strengthening the battalion's record in high-altitude mountaineering. The team reached the summit at 10:28 am on September 15 and unfurled the National Tricolour and the JAT Regiment Colour, marking the successful completion of the expedition, an official communique informed here on Saturday.

The expedition began from Rayang in East Siang district of Arunachal Pradesh on August 17, following which the team underwent acclimatisation at Lachung, Thangu and Giagoan before beginning the challenging ascent.

The climbers negotiated rugged terrain, steep slopes and glaciers while operating in extreme cold and low-oxygen conditions. The successful ascent demonstrated the team's endurance, determination and ability to operate in demanding high-altitude environments.

The latest achievement adds to the mountaineering record of 2 JAT Battalion, which has earlier undertaken successful expeditions to Mt Jago Kangri (6,550 metres) in the Siachen Glacier region, Mt Bandarpunch (6,316 metres), Mt Satopanth (7,075 metres) and Mt Jogin-I (6,465 metres).

76.title: Manipur: Assam Rifles felicitates 29 girls selected for Marriott International jobs under Project PRANITA

76.text:
Imphal: The Assam Rifles on Saturday felicitated 29 local women who were selected for employment with Marriott International under its corporate social responsibility initiative, Project PRANITA.

The felicitation programme was attended by Brigadier S. Prashant of 27 Sector Assam Rifles, along with representatives of civil society and officials from the hospitality company.

Under the programme, the selected candidates will pursue a Marriott-sponsored Bachelor of Hospitality and Tourism programme at Indira Gandhi National Tribal University. 77.title: Fact Check: Indian Army did not shoot two women or burn houses in Manipur, claim is false
77.description: A viral post falsely claims the Indian Army killed two women and burnt houses in Manipur, the claim is completly fake and false
77.text:
A claim is circulating on social media that the Indian Army shot two women and set their houses on fire in Manipur. The post also claims that the alleged attack was carried out on the orders of Lieutenant General V. M. Bhuvana Krishnan, Commander of the Eastern Command.

However, the claim has been found to be false and misleading.

A detailed investigation shows that, the viral post has mixed up two separate incidents that took place in Manipur on September 15.

What does the viral claim say?

The viral post alleges that the Indian Army killed two women and burnt their homes in Manipur.

It also claims that the alleged action was ordered by the Eastern Command commander and that it led to a serious deterioration of the situation in the state.

🚨On the orders of Indian Army @easterncomd Commander Lieutenant General V. M. Bhuvana Krishnan, Unfortunately the Army shot two women in #Manipur and set their homes on fire. 🚨Following this incident, the situation in Manipur has deteriorated severely today.@manipur_police pic.twitter.com/Rs7o4AwipI — Anushi Tiwari Indian 🇮🇳 (@indiantiwari01) September 16, 2026

The claim was shared on social media along with visuals from the incidents.

What actually happened?

Reports cited in the fact-check show that two separate incidents took place in different districts of Manipur.

In the first incident, two Kuki women were shot dead by unidentified armed attackers at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district on September 15, 2026.

Later that night, suspected militants attacked Chawangkining Naga village in Kangpokpi district, according to reports.

Security forces deployed in the area exchanged fire with the attackers.

During the incident, two houses on the outskirts of the village were set on fire.

The two incidents were separate, but the viral post linked them together and claimed that the Indian Army was responsible.

What do reports say about the house fires?

A report published by The Times of India said suspected militants attacked Chawangkining Naga village at around 10:30 pm on September 15.

CRPF personnel in the area returned fire. The exchange of fire reportedly continued for nearly six hours, until around 4:30 am.

An official quoted in the report said the security forces prevented the attackers from entering the village. However, two wooden houses on the outskirts of the village were burnt.

A report by The Hindu also said suspected militants attacked the village and exchanged fire with security forces before at least two houses were set on fire.

What did the facts say?

Various fact-checkers also carried out a reverse image search of visuals used in the viral post.

The same visuals were found on the YouTube channel Ukhrul Times. The accompanying information linked the visuals to the September 15 incident at Chawangkining Naga village.

The investigation found no credible report confirming that the Indian Army had shot the two women or ordered the burning of the houses.

There was also no credible evidence linking the incidents to Lieutenant General V. M. Bhuvana Krishnan or the Eastern Command.

Two incidents were linked together

The main issue with the viral claim is that it combines two separate incidents.

Incident 1: Two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district.

Incident 2: Suspected militants attacked Chawangkining Naga village in Kangpokpi district. Security forces exchanged fire with the attackers, while two houses were burnt.

There is no credible evidence in the reports cited by the fact-check that these incidents were carried out by the Indian Army.

Claim: Indian Army soldiers shot two women and burnt their houses in Manipur on the orders of the Eastern Command commander.

Fact Check: False and misleading.

The viral post links two separate incidents and wrongly attributes them to the Indian Army. Available reports instead describe unidentified attackers killing two women in one incident and suspected militants attacking a village in another incident where two houses were burnt during the violence.

79.title: Assam Rifles backs Kiphire school sports meet
79.description: Assam Rifles backs Kiphire school sports meet
79.text:
Kiphire, Sep 20: The Assam Rifles supported the Annual Sports Meet of El-Beth High School in Kiphire, Nagaland, held on September 19, promoting sports, teamwork and healthy living among students.

The Commandant of Assam Rifles, Kiphire Battalion, attended the event as Chief Guest and formally inaugurated the sports meet. Addressing the students, he encouraged them to participate in sporting activities with discipline, dedication and a spirit of teamwork.

As part of the initiative, sports equipment was presented to the school to support students in pursuing various sporting activities. Candies were also distributed among the students during the event.

The School Management Committee, staff, students and parents expressed their gratitude to the Assam Rifles for supporting the event and encouraging young people to participate in sports.

The initiative reflects the Assam Rifles’ continued engagement with local communities in Nagaland through youth-oriented activities. By supporting educational and sporting programmes, the force seeks to encourage constructive avenues for youth development and strengthen community participation.

80.title: Ankhel Chayang wins Chandel women’s volleyball title
80.description: Ankhel Chayang wins Chandel women’s volleyball title
80.text:
Chandel, Sep 21: Assam Rifles, in collaboration with the United Volleyball Lovers Group, organised the first two-day Women’s Volleyball Tournament at Pine Turf, Hnatham, in Chandel district of Manipur from September 18 to 19, promoting women’s participation in sports and providing a platform for local talent.

The tournament witnessed participation from 14 teams, along with 30 civilians and 25 Assam Rifles personnel, creating an environment of sporting competition, community interaction and camaraderie.

The event was aimed at encouraging young women to take up sports and providing them with opportunities to showcase their skills in a competitive setting. Volleyball enthusiasts from different parts of the area participated with enthusiasm, adding to the sporting spirit of the tournament.

Team Ankhel Chayang emerged victorious after defeating Team Julbang in the final. The winning side displayed determination and teamwork throughout the tournament to claim the championship.

The tournament also provided an opportunity for Assam Rifles personnel and local residents to interact through sport. The participation of civilians alongside security personnel helped strengthen community engagement and foster a sense of unity.

Organisers said the event highlighted the potential of women athletes in the region and the importance of providing them with accessible platforms to compete, develop confidence and pursue sporting ambitions.

Women’s participation in sports can contribute to physical fitness, confidence, discipline and leadership while also creating opportunities for young athletes to pursue competition at higher levels. Community-level tournaments can play an important role in identifying emerging talent and encouraging greater participation.

The involvement of 14 teams also reflected the growing interest in volleyball among women in the area. Such events can help build a stronger grassroots sporting culture by giving players regular opportunities to compete and improve their skills.

The Assam Rifles has undertaken various sports and youth-oriented initiatives in the Northeast as part of its broader community engagement activities. Sporting events provide a platform for young people to connect, compete and develop teamwork while strengthening interaction with local communities.

The successful conduct of the two-day tournament at Pine Turf brought together athletes, community members and Assam Rifles personnel in a shared sporting environment.

With Team Ankhel Chayang lifting the title after its victory over Team Julbang, the tournament concluded on a positive note, celebrating women’s sporting talent, teamwork and community participation in Chandel.

81.title: Assam Rifles DG Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera visits Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal, hails Pune’s Ganeshotsav legacy
81.description: Assam Rifles Director General Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera visited Pune’s historic Shreemant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal and participated in the evening Maha Aarti.
81.text:
The historic traditions of Pune’s Ganeshotsav came into focus on Sunday as Director General Assam Rifles Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera visited the iconic Shreemant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal and joined the evening Maha Aarti. During his visit, Lt Gen Lakhera praised the Mandal’s efforts to preserve and promote the rich cultural and historical legacy associated with Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati and Pune’s traditional Ganeshotsav. He said such traditions connect present generations with the history and cultural roots of the city.

Advertisement

Lt Gen Lakhera participated in the Maha Aarti and offered prayers at the historic Ganpati. Following the Aarti, the Mandal felicitated him during the visit.

Speaking to the media, Lt Gen Lakhera described the opportunity to pray at the historic Ganpati as an overwhelming experience.

“The feeling is the same as that of a devotee. I am an ordinary human being, and for anyone who gets an opportunity to come to the house of God, it is an extraordinary occasion. I am overwhelmed. I thank God for giving me this opportunity,” he said.

Advertisement

His prayers, he added, were centred on the country’s progress, security and prosperity.

“My only feeling is that our country should progress, our country should remain safe, our country should become stronger, and all the people of our country should prosper,” Lt Gen Lakhera said.

Advertisement

The Assam Rifles chief also spoke about the historical significance of Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati and its association with Pune’s public Ganeshotsav tradition and the freedom movement.

“When this idol was made, we were slaves of the British. This was the first Ganpati; Ganpati began from here. The biggest inspiration from this is that the nation is supreme,” he said.

Advertisement

For Lt Gen Lakhera, the history of the Mandal also carries a message for the younger generation. He urged youngsters to understand their cultural heritage and remain connected with their roots while moving forward with changing times.

“Do not forget your culture. Your greatest strength is your culture. Your history will determine your future. Stay connected to your roots,” he said.

Advertisement

He also encouraged youngsters to consider a career in the armed forces. “You come, try, work hard, and join the Army. The Army of the country belongs to the people of the country,” he said.

During the visit, the Mandal also felicitated its Festival Chief Punit Balan. Lt Gen Lakhera appreciated Balan’s efforts towards preserving the cultural and historical legacy of Shreemant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati and promoting the traditional character of Ganeshotsav.

Advertisement

The visit comes during Pune’s ongoing Ganeshotsav celebrations, when the city comes alive with public celebrations, cultural programmes and religious traditions. The Shreemant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal has continued to highlight the historical significance of Pune’s Ganeshotsav while working to keep its traditional character relevant for newer generations.

The Mandal’s initiatives focus on keeping alive the legacy of Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati and presenting Ganeshotsav not merely as a festival, but as an important part of Pune’s history, culture and collective identity.

82.title: Myanmar’s Arakan army detains 7 boatmen over Mizoram trade point violence
82.description: The United League of Arakan said that it would face legal action under laws enforced by the organisation.
82.text:
Aizawl, Sept 21: Seven boatmen have been detained by the Myanmar-based Arakan Army in connection with the alleged attack and vandalism at a trading point in Khaikhy village of Siaha district, sources said.

The incident took place at the Khaikhy jetty, a key centre of the informal trade between south Mizoram and Myanmar’s Rakhine and southern Chin regions, on September 14.

U Khaing Thukha, spokesperson of the United League of Arakan – the political wing of the Arakan Army – said the group’s ‘department of law enforcement and public security’ had identified Ko Zaw Naing Linn (25) and six others as responsible for instigating the violence.

The seven boatmen have been detained by the Arakan Army and censured. Meanwhile, the United League of Arakan said that it would face legal action under laws enforced by the organisation.

According to Thukha, the confrontation began with an argument after the boatmen, who were allegedly under the influence of alcohol, objected to the way boats were being handled while waiting for their turn. They reportedly alleged that preference was being given to boats on the Indian side.

The dispute later escalated, with Zaw Naing Linn allegedly gathering about 30 people who stormed the duty post of the Mara Thyutlia Py, a youth organisation operating in Siaha district. The group allegedly vandalised the post and attempted to set it on fire.

The Mara Thyutlia Py has since suspended trading activities with Rakhine and southern Chin states indefinitely. Its general secretary, N Solomon Beihlotha, said the suspension, imposed from 7 pm on Wednesday, was in force. The decision followed a report from the organisation’s Phura sub-headquarters after an on-the-spot assessment of the September 14 incident.

Khaikhy, located along the Salalui river on the Mizoram-Myanmar border, is a major centre for cross-border trade. Over 100 pick-up trucks reportedly ferry goods to Khaikhy every day, while a similar number of boats transport the consignments along the Salalui towards Paletwa and other areas of southern Chin and Rakhine.

The suspension of trade can affect supplies to parts of Rakhine and southern Chin, which have faced severe disruption in connectivity with other parts of Myanmar since the military coup. Southern Mizoram has emerged as a key route for supply of essential commodities, including fuel, to these areas of the neighbouring country.

83.title: Assam Rifles DG Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera performs Ganpati aarti in Pune
83.description: Assam Rifles DG Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera performed Ganpati aarti at the Shrimant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal in Pune during Ganeshotsav 2026.
83.text:
Director General of Assam Rifles Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera performed the Ganpati Aarti at the Shrimant Bhausaheb Rangari Ganpati Mandal in Pune on Sunday.

Addressing reporters, Lt Gen Lakhera described visiting the Ganpati’s abode as an extraordinary experience. “I am an ordinary person, and for anyone who gets the opportunity to visit the abode of the Divine, it is an extraordinary event. I am truly overwhelmed. I thank God for this opportunity. My only wish is for our country to progress, remain safe and strong, and for all its citizens to enjoy prosperity,” he said.

ADVERTISEMENT

Referring to the history of the mandal, he noted that the idol was created during British rule in India, highlighting its significance as an inspiration for the nation. “When this idol was created, we were under British rule; this specific Ganpati tradition began right here. The greatest inspiration to be drawn from this is that nothing is greater than the nation, and one should seek inspiration here whenever the country faces a crisis. He was there for us even when we had nothing; there is no greater source of inspiration than that,” Lt Gen Lakhera added.

This visit took place amid ongoing Ganeshotsav 2026 celebrations across Maharashtra, which began on September 14 and are scheduled to conclude on September 25 with the immersion of the idol.

ADVERTISEMENT

Earlier in Pune, Ganeshotsav festivities featured a special offering: a 251-kilogram modak-shaped cake presented to the Shreemant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati idol. The Rasmalai-flavoured cake was prepared by Pune-based WS Bakers as part of its annual offering to Lord Ganesha and marks the second consecutive year the bakery has made such a special offering during the festival.

WS Bakers Director Vikas Agarwal explained that a team of approximately 40 to 50 people worked on preparing the giant cake, which was brought to the Prem Mandir-themed Ganpati pandal and placed before the idol during the morning rituals.

84.title: Eight, including woman, two minors, held over soldier’s lynching in Mizoram
84.description: The 29-year-old Zakaria Lalhriattluanga was returning home on leave from Jammu & Kashmir when youths allegedly attacked him near Bualpui
84.text:
Aizawl, Sept 21: Eight people, including a woman and two minors, were arrested in connection with the lynching of an Assam Regiment soldier in north Mizoram’s Kolasib district, on Monday.

Kolasib Superintendent of Police Lalrinpuia Vartes said six of the arrested adults, all from the Hmar Veng locality of Kawnpui town, had been remanded in judicial custody.

The police are yet to decide on the appropriate course of action concerning the two minors.

“Police were investigating the incident and more arrests could not be ruled out. The post-mortem examination of Zakaria Lalhriattluanga has been completed,” the SP said.

The 29-year-old soldier, Lalhriattluanga, was buried with full military honours on Monday.

He was allegedly attacked and killed by a group of youths near Bualpui village on Sunday evening while he was returning to his native New Builum village after availing leave from his posting in Jammu and Kashmir.

He was travelling towards New Builum from Lengpui airport near Aizawl in a truck driven by a friend when the incident occurred near the Coffee Board’s coffee plantation area at Bualpui, along National Highway 306.

The incident reportedly followed an altercation between the drivers of two trucks over the poor condition of the road. The damaged stretch had made it difficult for the trucks to pass each other, leading to a heated argument between the drivers.

A group of youths, who were allegedly under the influence of alcohol, subsequently approached Lalhriattluanga and his friend.

According to reports, there had been no exchange of words between the soldier and the youths before they approached them.

Lalhriattluanga was allegedly attacked while trying to intervene when the youths assaulted his friend, the truck driver.

The village council and the Young Mizo Association (YMA) unit of Kawnpui Hmar Veng on Monday publicly tendered an unconditional apology to the people of New Builum and Mizoram over the incident.

In a statement, the two organisations condemned the violence allegedly committed by youths from the locality and said those responsible should face the harshest punishment under the law.

The arrest of the eight accused comes as police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the soldier’s death, including the sequence of events and the roles of those arrested.

86.title: Lt Gen Mohit Seth Appointed New GOC of Indian Army’s White Knight Corps
86.description: Jammu, 22 September 2026: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth will assume charge as the General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Indian Army’s Nagrota-based White
86.text:
Jammu, 22 September 2026: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth will assume charge as the General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Indian Army’s Nagrota-based White Knight Corps, also known as XVI Corps, on 1 October 2026. He will succeed Lieutenant General P. K. Mishra, who will move to a new assignment. The formal change of command will take place at a baton-handing ceremony.

The White Knight Corps, raised on 1 June 1972 and headquartered at Nagrota in Jammu district, is one of the most operationally significant formations of the Northern Command. It is responsible for a wide area south of the Pir Panjal range, extending towards the Jammu plains and Akhnoor. The Corps is tasked with securing the International Border and the Line of Control, and with conducting counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations in Jammu, Rajouri, Poonch and the erstwhile Doda region. Delta Force and Romeo Force of the Rashtriya Rifles operate under its operational control.

Profile of the incoming Corps Commander

Lieutenant General Seth is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and the National Defence College. He was commissioned into the 3 Madras Regiment in 1991 and has more than three decades of distinguished service. He is presently Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team (IMTRAT), the Indian Army’s training establishment in Bhutan. He earlier succeeded Lieutenant General Mishra in that appointment as well, before Lieutenant General Mishra took over XVI Corps on 1 April 2025.

His operational record includes command of Counter-Insurgency Force Kilo, an elite Rashtriya Rifles formation responsible for anti-terror operations in north Kashmir. He has also served as the Indian Army Liaison Officer at the High Commission of India in the United Kingdom, and has held key command and staff appointments in Jammu and Kashmir, the Northeast and at Army Headquarters. The appointment marks his return to a principal operational role in the Jammu and Kashmir theatre.

Outgoing commander

Lieutenant General P. K. Mishra, of the Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry, assumed command of the White Knight Corps on 1 April 2025, succeeding Lieutenant General Navin Sachdeva. He was recently awarded the Uttam Yudh Seva Medal by the President of India at the Defence Investiture Ceremony 2026 (Phase II). He is also a recipient of the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal, the Yudh Seva Medal and the Sena Medal. Officials said he will proceed to a new posting after relinquishing command.

The succession places an officer with extensive counter-insurgency, staff and international experience at the head of a Corps that remains central to the security of the Jammu region and the western sector of the Line of Control.

87.title: CRPF to celebrate 40th anniversary of first all-women battalion
87.description: The CRPF will commemorate the 40th anniversary of its first all-women battalion on September 25 in New Delhi. The force, which now has six women-only battalions and over 10,000 women personnel, will felicitate serving and veteran women personnel
87.text:
Crpf To Celebrate 40th Anniversary Of First All Women Battalion

CRPF to celebrate 40th anniversary of first all-women battalion

The CRPF will commemorate the 40th anniversary of its first all-women battalion on September 25 in New Delhi. The force, which now has six women-only battalions and over 10,000 women personnel, will felicitate serving and veteran women personnel

By PTI Published Date - 22 September 2026, 12:52 PM

New Delhi: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) will mark the 40th anniversary of the raising of its first all-women battalion with a special commemorative event, officials said on Tuesday.

The first such unit was raised on February 6, 1986. The force now has six all-women battalions.

The event will be held at the campus of the 88th ‘Mahila Battalion’ here on September 25, where CRPF Director General G P Singh, along with his wife, president of the force’s family welfare association, will felicitate veteran and serving women personnel, officials said.

The force also has women personnel in its special units, including the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA), besides female personnel in its other regular units.

The CRPF has more than 10,000 women personnel across its ranks.

Women personnel of the force have also received gallantry awards, including Constable Kamlesh Kumari, who was posthumously awarded the Ashok Chakra for thwarting the 2001 terrorist attack on Parliament.

Constable Vimla Devi was awarded the Sena Medal, while Lance Naik Rajwanti Devi received the Chief of Army Staff Commendation Card for playing a “critical” operational role with the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) in Sri Lanka in 1988.

Constable Bindu Kumre received a gallantry medal for displaying “exemplary” bravery during the Srinagar Airport terrorist attack in 2001, according to official records.

The CRPF, with about 3.25 lakh personnel, is the country’s leading internal security force, it is primarily deployed for internal security duties, including anti-Naxal operations, counter-terrorism operations in Jammu and Kashmir and anti-insurgency operations in the northeastern states.

88.title: Nagaland: Assam Rifles says NSF delegation stopped at Avangkhu over lack of border pass
88.description: Assam Rifles says NSF delegation was stopped for lacking a valid Border Pass or permission to cross the India-Myanmar border.
88.text: Guwahati: The Free Movement Regime (FMR), now operating under a regulated movement framework, allows eligible residents of villages located within 10 km of the India-Myanmar border on either side to undertake cross-border travel subject to prescribed conditions, officials said on Monday. A defence spokesperson said the number of legitimate crossings facilitated under the FMR/Regulated Movement Regime (RMR) demonstrates that the mechanism is intended to regulate cross-border travel rather than prevent people-to-people contact. According to official records, 16,428 Border Passes have been issued so far, indicating that eligible residents who fulfil the required conditions continue to be permitted to cross the international boundary, the spokesperson said. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) announced in 2024 that the earlier FMR, which permitted residents living along the India-Myanmar border to travel up to 16 km into the neighbouring country without passports or visas, would be discontinued. It subsequently proposed a regulated system under which residents living within 10 km of the border on either side would be issued passes for cross-border movement. The decision to replace the FMR and the proposal to fence the India-Myanmar border have faced opposition from the governments of Nagaland and Mizoram, as well as political parties and civil society organisations in the two states. Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland and Mizoram collectively share a 1,643-km unfenced international border with Myanmar. The Centre has also proposed fencing the entire stretch, citing concerns including arms and narcotics smuggling, unauthorised cross-border movement and other forms of contraband trafficking. The estimated cost of the project has been put at Rs 31,000 crore. The clarification from the defence authorities came after reports alleged that the Assam Rifles had stopped a delegation of the Naga Students’ Federation (NSF) from travelling to Myanmar at Avangkhu in Nagaland’s Meluri district. The Assam Rifles rejected the suggestion that the delegation was stopped because of its identity or the stated purpose of its visit. According to its statement, the movement was halted because the group did not possess the required authorisation to cross the international border. The statement said eight people in three vehicles arrived at the designated crossing point on September 19 and informed officials that they intended to travel to Tsera in Myanmar. When asked to produce the documents required for authorised cross-border movement, the delegation allegedly failed to provide a valid Border Pass or permission issued by the competent authority, the statement said. The Assam Rifles maintained that the issue was one of compliance with border-movement regulations and not a restriction on cultural exchanges or people-to-people contact. It further said that cross-border travel under the prevailing regulated framework is permitted only through designated points and is subject to specified eligibility criteria and documentation. According to the statement, the NSF delegation had travelled from Kohima and therefore could not claim an automatic right to cross the international border solely on the basis of a proposed cultural-exchange programme or reference letters. The Assam Rifles also clarified that a recommendation or reference letter issued by a civil society organisation does not constitute official permission to cross an international boundary. 89.title: Six militants arrested in Manipur
89.description: Six militants belonging to various banned outfits have been arrested by security forces in Manipur's Imphal East and Tengnoupal districts, a police statement said on Tuesday.
89.text:
Representational Image

Imphal



Six militants belonging to various banned outfits have been arrested by security forces in Manipur's Imphal East and Tengnoupal districts, a police statement said on Tuesday.

A cadre of the proscribed Kangleipak Communist Party (MFL) was apprehended by a joint team of state police commandos and the Assam Rifles from the Andro area in Imphal East on Monday, it said.

He has been identified as 21-year-old Yumnam Ramos Singh.

In another joint operation by state police commandos and the Army, two active members of the banned KCP (Apunba) were arrested in the Lamlai area of the district on September 21.

They were identified as Ngangom Loijinghenba Meitei (22) and Ngangom Hemba Meitei (28), the statement said.

A combined team of the state police and the Assam Rifles apprehended three members of the outlawed People's Liberation Army from the vicinity of Border Pillar-87 along the India-Myanmar international boundary on Sunday, the police said.

Two of them were identified as Ningthoujam James Singh (21) and Kshetrimayum Rustan Singh (25), while another was a juvenile.

90.title: Six militants arrested, arms and ammunition recovered in Manipur operations
90.description: Imphal, Sep 22 (SocialNews.XYZ) Security forces in Manipur, in separate operations, arrested six militants from different districts bordering Myanmar and recovered a cache of arms and ammunition, officials said on Tuesday. A defence spokesman said... - Social News XYZ
90.text:
Imphal, Sep 22 (SocialNews.XYZ) Security forces in Manipur, in separate operations, arrested six militants from different districts bordering Myanmar and recovered a cache of arms and ammunition, officials said on Tuesday.

A defence spokesman said that in a major effort to maintain peace and safety, Assam Rifles, working alongside local police, successfully carried out two security operations in Manipur. The joint operations resulted in the detention of three individuals along the Myanmar border and the recovery of hidden arms and ammunition in the valley.

Acting on specific information regarding three individuals who had left their camp at Teijang in Chandel District and were attempting to cross the area, security personnel set up monitoring posts around Shaibol in Tengnoupal District, supported by teams in nearby Moriengthel and Yangoupokpi. During the continuous monitoring, teams spotted movement along a forest path near Border Pillar 87. The teams moved in promptly and detained the three individuals. All three were handed over to the police station for further legal steps and inquiry.

In a second operation, a combined team from Assam Rifles and Imphal West Police searched an area along the Akham–Lamdeng Road in Imphal West District. Following details obtained from previously detained individuals of the People's Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (PREPAK-PRO faction) group and verified by local inputs, the team located a collection of stored weapons. The items recovered include two bolt-action rifles, nine 9mm pistols, one Lathode gun, one 36-hand grenade without a safety lever, one stun grenade, one smoke grenade, two rubber anti-riot shells and one smoke anti-riot shell.

The seized materials were handed over to Lamsang Police Station under formal procedures for further investigation. These successful operations reflect the ongoing commitment and close coordination between Assam Rifles and Manipur Police in ensuring public safety, preventing illegal movements along the border and keeping local communities secure.

A police official said that a combined team of Tengnoupal District Police and Assam Rifles arrested three active cadres of the banned People's Liberation Army (PLA) from the Myanmar border areas. The arrested militants were identified as Ningthoujam James Singh alias Bibarel (21), Kshetrimayum Rustan Singh alias Thoihenba (25) and a juvenile.
