112.title: ‘Vande Mataram’ Voice of India’s National Consciousness, Unity and Pride: Gen Upendra Dwivedi
112.description: Guwahati, 25 September (HS): The 150th anniversary of the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ was commemorated in Guwahati on Friday with a special programme, ‘Namami Bharatam’, organised by Shishu Shiksha Samiti, Assam, affiliated with Vidya Bharati Akh
112.text:
Guwahati, 25 September (HS): The 150th anniversary of the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ was commemorated in Guwahati on Friday with a special programme, ‘Namami Bharatam’, organised by Shishu Shiksha Samiti, Assam, affiliated with Vidya Bharati Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Sansthan.

The programme was held at the Srimanta Sankardev International Auditorium, where ‘Vande Mataram’ was sung collectively along with people across the country.

Former Chief of the Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi attended the programme as the chief guest. Retired Air Vice Marshal Sanjeev Bordoloi, Vidya Bharati Purvottar Kshetra Organising Secretary Dr Pawan Tiwari, Secretary Dr Jagadindra Ray Choudhury, Shishu Shiksha Samiti, Assam president Kulendra Kumar Bhagawati, ‘Namami Bharatam’ coordinator Gourab Kalita and Assam Gaurav awardee Meenakshi Das were among those present.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Pawan Tiwari said ‘Vande Mataram’ was not merely a song but represented India’s national consciousness, cultural unity and pride. Referring to the cultural and spiritual heritage of Northeast India, he said the collective rendition from the land of Maa Kamakhya, inspired by the legacy of Srimanta Sankardev and the valour of Lachit Barphukan, reflected the spirit of national unity.

Gen Dwivedi said he attended the programme not as a former Army Chief but as a former student of Saraswati Shishu Mandir. He described the Northeast as a gateway to India and said the region had an important role in the country’s strength, leadership and unity.

Calling upon young people to actively participate in nation-building, Gen Dwivedi described ‘Vande Mataram’ as a call to the nation, with India as its identity and the goal of building a developed India by 2047.

He urged the youth to cultivate three qualities — Attitude, Adaptability and Ability — which he described as a positive mindset, the capacity to adjust to changing circumstances and competence. He also called upon them to move beyond being “problem finders” and become “problem fixers” through positive thinking, responsibility, courage and determination.

The former Army Chief advised youngsters to follow the principle of “Learn, Unlearn and Relearn” while preserving Indian cultural values and traditions and embracing modern technology.

Remembering the heroes of the Northeast, Gen Dwivedi highlighted the contributions of Lachit Barphukan and Kanaklata Barua. He also underlined the role of the Indian Army, NCC and Vidya Bharati in transforming India’s diversity into strength and urged alumni and civil society members to create opportunities and guide the younger generation.

He further encouraged youngsters to develop a daily “zero-ten” habit by spending 10 minutes every morning away from mobile phones to reflect on their goals, gratitude and resolve for the day. Addressing students, he asked them to consider what they could learn each day to make themselves and the country better.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Arup Buzarbarua, principal of Sankardev Shishu Niketan, Birubari, followed by the national anthem.------------

Hindusthan Samachar / Sriprakash

113.title: Meet Major Vivek Singh Bhandral: 21 Para SF Officer Who Killed Two Terrorists Despite Being Gravely Wounded
113.description: On 29 August 2002, deep inside the forests of the Machhal sector in Kupwara, a search party of 21 Para (Special Forces) was closing in on a militant hideout when the operation suddenly turned into ...
113.text:
On 29 August 2002, deep inside the forests of the Machhal sector in Kupwara, a search party of 21 Para (Special Forces) was closing in on a militant hideout when the operation suddenly turned into a close-quarter firefight. Two terrorists burst out of a house and opened fire on the troops. Within moments, the leading scout and the squad commander were wounded. Major Vivek Singh Bhandral took the fight forward. He killed one terrorist at close range, pursued the second into a nearby grove and continued the assault even after being struck by a burst of machine-gun fire. Bleeding heavily, he refused to disengage and pressed forward until the second terrorist was eliminated. Shortly afterwards, he succumbed to his injuries. He was just 32 years old.

For his courage and leadership in the operation, Major Bhandral was awarded the Sena Medal posthumously. His final action became a powerful example of the kind of leadership demanded in Special Forces operations, where carefully prepared plans can turn within seconds into brutal encounters fought at extremely short distances. With members of his team already wounded and the situation rapidly deteriorating, Major Bhandral chose to remain at the forefront of the engagement and ensure that the threat was neutralised.

Major Vivek Singh Bhandral was born on 16 June 1970 at a military hospital in Hyderabad. His family hailed from Kangra in Himachal Pradesh and had strong ties with the Armed Forces. His father, Colonel Pritam Singh Bhandral (Retired), had served in the Maratha Light Infantry, while his mother, Smt Rajkumari Bhandral, looked after the family as Army postings took them across the country. Vivek was the elder of two sons, with his younger brother Vikram Bhandral growing up alongside him in the military environment.

Because of his father's Army service, Vivek's childhood was spent in several parts of India. His schooling took him through Kangra, Belgaum, Jalandhar, Assam and Udhampur. He later completed a degree in Commerce, but rather than pursuing a civilian career, he chose to follow the military path. He cleared the Combined Defence Services Examination and joined the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun in July 1991.

On 19 December 1992, Vivek Bhandral passed out of the Indian Military Academy and was commissioned as a Lieutenant into 9 Maratha Light Infantry. The connection with the Maratha Light Infantry carried particular meaning because his father had served in the same regimental family. However, conventional infantry soldiering would not be the limit of his military career. He soon volunteered for the Special Forces.

After completing the demanding selection and training process, he joined 21 Para (Special Forces) in 1995. The move placed him among troops trained for some of the Army's most difficult missions, including counter-insurgency, reconnaissance and operations in hostile terrain. Over the following years, Major Bhandral developed into an accomplished Special Forces officer.

His professional qualifications reflected the range of skills required of such an officer. He completed the Commando Course, Young Officers' Course and Signals Course and also qualified as a combat free-faller. His abilities were recognised beyond operational deployments when he was selected to serve as an instructor at the All Arms Wing of the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering at Mhow. The appointment reflected confidence not only in his field experience but also in his ability to train other soldiers and officers.

Long before his final operation in Machhal, Major Bhandral had already served in areas where the Indian Army was actively engaged in combat and counter-insurgency operations. During his deployment in Assam, he participated in Operation Rhino against insurgent groups operating in the Northeast.

When the Kargil conflict erupted in 1999, he served during Operation Vijay and led Special Forces teams on demanding missions. His leadership and devotion to duty during the conflict earned him the Chief of the Army Staff Commendation Card. It was an important recognition of an officer whose operational career was already being shaped by difficult assignments.

By 2002, 21 Para (SF) was operating in Jammu and Kashmir during Operation Parakram. The period following the December 2001 terrorist attack on Parliament saw large-scale mobilisation along India's western frontier alongside intensified counter-infiltration and counter-terrorism operations in Jammu and Kashmir. Kupwara, particularly areas close to the Line of Control such as Machhal, remained challenging terrain for security forces because of its thick forests, steep slopes and infiltration routes.

It was in this environment that Major Bhandral and his men were tasked with a search-and-destroy operation on 29 August 2002. Intelligence had indicated the presence of heavily armed terrorists in the forests of the Machhal sector, and a team from 21 Para (SF) moved in to locate and neutralise them.

At around midday, as the troops closed in on the suspected hideout, two terrorists suddenly emerged from a house and opened intense fire in an apparent attempt to break the cordon. The leading scout and the squad commander were wounded in the initial exchange. Their injuries created an extremely dangerous situation, with casualties requiring attention while armed terrorists were still attempting to escape.

Major Bhandral immediately took control of the engagement. Rather than allowing the terrorists to exploit the confusion created by the first burst of fire, he moved against them. He engaged the first terrorist at very close range and killed him.

The second terrorist escaped towards a nearby grove and continued firing. Major Bhandral pursued him rather than allowing him to disappear into the forest. During the ensuing fight, he used a grenade and continued closing in on the militant's position. It was during this phase of the engagement that he was struck by machine-gun fire.

Despite suffering serious wounds and losing blood, Major Bhandral continued the pursuit. He refused to break contact and pressed the attack until the second terrorist was also killed. By the end of the encounter, both terrorists had been neutralised and the wounded members of the team could be evacuated. Major Bhandral, however, had sustained fatal injuries and succumbed shortly afterwards.

The sequence of events made his final action particularly significant. He had entered the engagement after members of his team were wounded, killed one terrorist at close quarters, pursued another into difficult terrain, suffered serious gunshot wounds and still continued fighting until the threat had been eliminated. His actions helped protect his men at the cost of his own life.

Major Vivek Singh Bhandral was subsequently awarded the Sena Medal posthumously for his gallantry. Accounts commemorating his sacrifice have highlighted his leadership, fieldcraft and determination to continue the operation despite being critically wounded. Army remembrance posts over the years have similarly recalled his courage and his role in ensuring that the terrorists were neutralised while his wounded comrades were extricated.

Among those who served with and remembered him, Major Bhandral also came to be associated with the informal name "Cheetah", a reflection of the speed, aggression and determination for which he was remembered. It was not an official military title, but the kind of nickname that can become closely associated with an officer within the fraternity in which he served.

His military career had lasted less than a decade, yet it had taken him from the Maratha Light Infantry to the Special Forces, from counter-insurgency operations in Assam to the Kargil conflict and finally to the forests of Kashmir. He had trained as a commando and combat free-faller, served as an instructor at Mhow and earned recognition for his service during Operation Vijay before receiving the Sena Medal for his final action.

Major Vivek Singh Bhandral's story ultimately rests on what happened during those few violent minutes in Machhal. With two soldiers wounded and two terrorists attempting to escape, he chose to take the fight forward. Even after being critically hit, he continued until the second terrorist had been eliminated.

The 32-year-old officer from a military family in Kangra had followed his father into the Army, earned his commission from the Indian Military Academy, served with 9 Maratha Light Infantry and then volunteered for the demanding life of a Special Forces operator. On 29 August 2002, that journey ended in the forests of Kupwara.

More than two decades later, Major Vivek Singh Bhandral, SM (Posthumous), is remembered not simply for the decoration that followed his death, but for the actions that earned it. In the final engagement of his life, he remained with his men, continued fighting despite his wounds and completed the mission. His Sena Medal recorded his gallantry; his story preserves the memory of the officer behind it.

114.title: Royal Global University signs MoU with Assam Rifles
114.text:
Guwahati, Sep 25: Strengthening its commitment to nation-building

through education and supporting the families of defence personnel, The Assam Royal

Global University (RGU) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Assam

Rifles at the Headquarters Directorate General Assam Rifles (HQ DGAR), Laitkor, Shillong.

The MoU was signed yesterday in the presence of senior officials from both organisations.

Representing RGU was Dr. D. N. Singh, Registrar Academics, while the Assam Rifles was

represented by Maj Gen J. S. Bainsla, SM, ADG Assam Rifles, along with Brig Sandip

Chatterjee, SM, Brig (Pers), Col. Harmeet Singh and other senior officials.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. D. N. Singh highlighted the significance of the collaboration

and outlined the benefits of RGU’s Royal Shaurya and Royal Suraksha scholarship schemes

for the dependents and wards of defence personnel.

Under the MoU, RGU will introduce two dedicated scholarship categories—Royal Shaurya

and Royal Suraksha—for the dependents and wards of defence personnel, covering serving

personnel, ex-servicemen, personnel with disabilities and personnel who have died in

harness.

The Royal Shaurya Scholarship will provide a 100 per cent tuition fee waiver to the families

of martyrs and gallantry awardees. The Royal Suraksha Scholarship will provide a 50 per

cent tuition fee concession to the wards of serving and retired defence personnel.

The Assam Royal Global University offers a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate and

doctoral programmes across diverse disciplines, including Science, Engineering,

Management and Commerce, Architecture, Paramedical and Allied Health Sciences,

Pharmacy, Law, Humanities and Social Sciences, Fine Arts and Design, Sports, and several

emerging fields.

115.title: NorthEast United FC vs Sreenidi Deccan Preview - Team news, lineups | IFA Shield 2026
115.description: Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to rise up against NorthEast United FC in their final group stage game in the IFA Shield 2026.
115.text:
Sreenidi Deccan, who got thrashed by the Kolkata outfit in the IFA Shield 2026 opener with a massive score of 6-0 are all set to battle it out in their final group game when they will face two-time Durand Cup champions NorthEast United FC, as the venue has not yet been confirmed by the Indian Football Association.

NorthEast United FC are ready to lock horns against the Indian Football League (IFL) side Sreenidi Deccan FC in their opening IFA Shield fixture on 26th September, 2026, at 14:30 IST, as the game between these two clubs will be a vital clash from a points table perspective after the IFL side got a defeat in their opening clash against Mohun Bagan.

NorthEast United FC

NorthEast United look to start the IFA Shield campaign with a win.

The opening clash is poised to happen for the Highlanders when they take on Sreenidi Deccan FC in their IFA Shield 2026 opener, after a premature elimination by Mohun Bagan during the Durand Cup 2026, this could be a good stage for Pedro Benali to test the squad he and the management recruited before the Indian Super League 2026-27 season.

Against Sreenidi Deccan, who has built by far the best squad to contest in the IFL 2026-27 season, this will be a stern test for NorthEast. With a good foreign core and a young team, they are lined up to square off against them and are looking to play attacking football with multiple transitions and also give more outings to their forwards.

Sreenidi Deccan FC

A must-win game for Sreenidi Deccan FC.

After a disappointing defeat away from home against Mohun Bagan, now the southern side are all in to take on NorthEast United FC, following the game, surely marking the final group stage fixture for them, and a win is what they needed the most to survive in the race.

They need to play calm and composed football against The Highlanders and also seek to adjust the defensive shape, which was wide open when they faced the Mariners and conceded six goals, not only in the defence but also in the attack; they lacked creativity.

Team News

Both sides will have most of their players who will be set to field for the opening game.

Head-to-Head

This game will be the first meeting between the two sides.

Predicted Lineups

Sreenidi Deccan FC (4-4-2):

Kamaljit Singh (GK), Pritam Kotal, Hadi Idrissou, Gurmukh Singh, Abhash Thapa, Pronay Halder, Pape Gassama, Adriano Castanheira, Jerry Mawihmingthanga, David Castañeda, Fabrice Kah

NorthEast United FC (4-2-3-1)

Gurmeet Singh (GK), Asheer Akhtar (C), Eneko, Rabeeh, Samte, Macarton, Maya, Moyano, Ajaraie, Ethyan, Jithin.

Alaaeddine Ajaraie (NEUFC)

Alaaeddine Ajaraie is the most influential player in the history of NorthEast United FC’s footballing history, as he led the team by example with his return from the short loan spell, guiding his side to the Durand Cup 2026 semi-finals is not an easy task. But for Alaaeddine, scoring goals in tough situations and bringing the result are key points, as he is lethal in front of goal and against a defensively feeble team like Sreenidi, this could be a great opportunity to bag the goals and also register an opening victory to gain momentum.

Apart from everyone, Eneko Satrustegui will be very important for NorthEast United FC heading into the clash against Sreenidi Deccan, with Eneko, Alaaeddine Ajaraie, having found his actual mirror form as he left the Durand Cup 2026 campaign with the Golden Boot award by scoring the most goals.

Pronay Halder (Sreenidi Deccan)

With immense experience in the bag, the former India international midfielder, who even featured 24 times for the Blue Tigers, Pronay Halder can make a big difference against NorthEast United FC. As he has the experience of playing Kolkata football all over his life, he can be vital for Antonio Rueda to dictate the middle of the park, as he also started against Mohun Bagan in the first game.

116.title: POWERGRID Appoints Dharambir Kumar as Head of North Eastern Region Transmission System
116.description: POWERGRID appoints Executive Director Dharambir Kumar as Head of NERTS from September 18, 2026, bringing over 32 years of power transmission experience.
116.text:
Indian Masterminds Stories

New Delhi: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID) has appointed Dharambir Kumar, Executive Director (ED), as the Head of North Eastern Region Transmission System (NERTS), effective September 18, 2026.

POWERGRID is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Kumar brings more than three decades of experience in the power transmission sector to his new leadership role.

Dharambir Kumar Appointed Head of NERTS

Dharambir Kumar joined POWERGRID in January 1994 and has completed more than 32 years of service in the power transmission sector.

He was promoted to the position of Executive Director in July 2026 and has now taken charge as Head of NERTS.

His new role involves overseeing POWERGRID’s transmission system operations and related activities in the North Eastern Region.

Read also: POWERGRID Acquires Barmer HVDC Transmission for ₹18.98 Crore, to Develop 6 GW Project in Rajasthan

Educational Qualification and Professional Experience

Kumar holds a B.Sc. Engineering degree in Electrical Engineering from B.R. Ambedkar Bihar University, Muzaffarpur.

During his long association with POWERGRID, he has worked in several capacities across different regions and offices.

His professional experience covers:

Substation maintenance and operation

Operation and maintenance activities

Consultancy assignments

Transmission line projects

Substation projects

Project execution

Corporate and regional office assignments

His diverse experience spans technical operations as well as project implementation within the power transmission sector.

Experience Across North Eastern and Eastern Regions

Kumar has served across the North Eastern and Eastern regions, along with assignments at POWERGRID’s corporate and regional offices.

His previous postings have included locations such as:

Jiribam

Seppa

Ranchi

Jamshedpur

Gurgaon

Rajasthan

Other regional and corporate locations

His experience in the North Eastern Region includes assignments at Jiribam and Seppa, providing him with exposure to the region’s transmission infrastructure and operational requirements.

New Leadership Role at POWERGRID

As Head of North Eastern Region Transmission System (NERTS), Dharambir Kumar will lead POWERGRID’s transmission-related operations and activities across the North Eastern Region.

His appointment follows his elevation to the Executive Director position in July 2026 and marks another senior leadership responsibility in his long career with POWERGRID.

The appointment brings extensive experience in transmission system operation, maintenance, consultancy and project execution to the leadership of NERTS.

Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID) is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. The company is primarily engaged in the transmission of electricity and operates one of the world’s largest electricity transmission networks. POWERGRID also provides consultancy, telecommunications and energy-related services and plays a key role in strengthening India’s power transmission infrastructure.

117.title: Arunachal Governor stresses stronger civil-military coordination, highlights state’s strategic significance
117.description: Itanagar, Sep 25 (SocialNews.XYZ) Arunachal Pradesh Governor Lt Gen K.T. Parnaik (Retd) on Friday underscored the strategic importance of the state and called for further strengthening civil-military coordination to enhance security and development in the... - Social News XYZ
117.text:
Itanagar, Sep 25 (SocialNews.XYZ) Arunachal Pradesh Governor Lt Gen K.T. Parnaik (Retd) on Friday underscored the strategic importance of the state and called for further strengthening civil-military coordination to enhance security and development in the frontier state.

The General Officer Commanding (GOC) 101 Area, Lt Gen Mohit Waghwa, called on the Governor at Lok Bhavan in Itanagar on Friday. A Lok Bhavan official said that during the interaction with Lt Gen Waghwa, the Governor said close coordination among the Armed Forces, state government, and civil administration was essential for effective disaster response and public welfare initiatives.

He also suggested enhancing transit routes, communication networks, and administrative infrastructure to support troop movement and border area logistics.

The meeting focused on logistics and administrative support, civil-military coordination, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) mechanisms in the Northeast, the official said.

The Governor commended the pivotal role of 101 Area, headquartered in Shillong, in ensuring seamless combat logistics and operational coordination across the region.

He appreciated the Command’s prompt and professional response during natural disasters, including floods and landslides, where timely rescue, relief, and rehabilitation efforts have brought invaluable support to affected communities.

The Governor urged the GOC to further strengthen welfare measures for ex-servicemen and Veer Naris, with particular emphasis on improving access to the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS), and empanelling of state healthcare institutions.

He also highlighted the importance of facilitating access to other welfare programmes, including resettlement and skill development initiatives, educational assistance for children of ex-servicemen, pension-related services, and reemployment of veterans, as provisions provided by the state government.

Lt Gen Parnaik (Retd) suggested regular awareness camps, medical outreach activities in remote areas, and closer coordination with the Rajya Sainik Board and Zila Sainik Boards to ensure that every eligible veteran and family member avails benefits and entitlements provided by the government.

The GOC assured the Governor about the Indian Army’s continued commitment to maintaining close coordination and extending all possible support for the security, development, and well-being of the people of Arunachal Pradesh.

119.title: Brahmaputra-Chao Phraya Dialogue explores new pathways for India-Thailand cooperation in Northeast
119.description: The Brahmaputra-Chao Phraya Dialogue, held across Guwahati and Shillong on September 22 and 23, brought together senior diplomats, policymakers and academics from India and Thailand to explore new avenues for bilateral cooperation with a focus on India's Northeast region. The two-day dialogue aimed to translate regional policy into actionable initiatives in bilateral trade, education and development, with participants emphasising the need to move beyond formal agreements and focus on implementation through institutional exchanges and on-ground cooperation. Organised by think tank Asian Confluence in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs, India, and Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the summit was co-hosted by Assam Royal Global University and the Meghalaya Institute of Governance. The first day of the dialogue in Guwahati focused on human capital, healthcare, education and youth entrepreneurship. Participants highlighted the importance of youth engagement, institutional partnerships and direct exchanges between educational institutions to support local economic growth. The opening sessions were chaired by former MEA Secretary Ambassador Riva Ganguly Das and attended by Urasa Mongkolnavin, Director-General, Department of South Asian, Middle East and African Affairs, Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Sabyasachi Dutta, Executive Director, Asian Confluence; former Minister of State for External Affairs and Education R K Ranjan Singh; Additional Secretary (South) in the Ministry of External Affairs Prashant Agrawal; Assam Higher Education Secretary Narayan Konwar; and representatives of academic institutions. We must move beyond MoUs to meaningful implementation through on-ground visits and institutional exchanges, participants noted during the opening sessions. The dialogue moved to Shillong on September 23, where discussions centred on strategic partnerships in the Bay of Bengal region and strengthening connectivity between India and Thailand. Key recommendations discussed during the second day included the development of direct air corridors and regional transit links, joint initiatives in clean energy, green manufacturing and disaster management, and city-to-city and province-level partnerships to promote trade and tourism. Participants also discussed aligning shared interests through regional platforms such as the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA). India's Northeast holds strategic importance for the country's Act East policy, owing to its geographic proximity to Southeast Asia. Enhanced connectivity and institutional cooperation with Thailand are expected to support regional trade, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties. Asian Confluence has been facilitating engagement between India and Thailand since 2018 through its Brahmaputra-Chao Phraya Initiative and the NADI platform. The think tank said it would continue working to strengthen cooperation in trade, culture and innovation between the two regions. The dialogue concluded with an emphasis on converting policy recommendations into concrete initiatives through sustained engagement among governments, institutions, businesses and civil society. (ANI)

121.title: AFSPA extended in parts of Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland for six months
121.description: Centre extends AFSPA in disturbed areas of Manipur, Nagaland, and Arunachal Pradesh for six months from Oct 1, 2026.
121.text:
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Friday extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) in parts of Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland for another six months.

AFSPA has been extended in the whole State of Manipur except the jurisdiction of 13 police stations in five valley districts. Manipur has been affected by ethnic violence since May 3, 2023.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has declared the entire state of Manipur, excluding areas under 13 specified police stations, as a "disturbed area" under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958.



The declaration will remain in effect for six months from October 1, 2026, unless… pic.twitter.com/sy1GbMDfTt — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) September 25, 2026

“Whereas the Central government after review of the law and order situation in Manipur, in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (28 of 1958) declares the entire State of Manipur, excluding the areas falling under the jurisdiction of the following 13 police stations of five districts, as ‘disturbed area’ for a period of six months with effect from 01.10.2026, unless withdrawn earlier,” the MHA notification said. The excluded police stations are Imphal, Lamphel, City, Singjamei, Patsoi, Wangoi, Porompat, Heingang, Irilbung, Thoubal, Bishnupur, Nambol and Kakching.

On November 14, 2024, out of 19 police stations in seven districts of Manipur, AFSPA was reimposed in the limits of six police stations in five districts, mostly valley, in the wake of the 2023 ethnic violence. President’s Rule was imposed in the State on February 13, 2025 and revoked on February 4 this year.

AFSPA was withdrawn from all valley police stations between April 1, 2022-April 1, 2023 by the Manipur government amid improved security situation and “large sense of security among general public.” The provisions of the Act were withdrawn from the Imphal Municipality area in 2004. The disturbed area notification for the hill districts in Manipur has been periodically extended for the past three decades, with the last notification issued on March 23, 2026.

In Nagaland, AFSPA was extended for another six months in nine districts — Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren and Meluri and 21 police stations in five other districts of Kohima, Mokokchung, Longleng, Wokha and Zunheboto, another MHA notification said.

In Arunachal Pradesh, Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts and the areas falling within the jurisdiction of Namsai, Mahadevpur and Chowkham police stations in Namsai district of Arunachal Pradesh, bordering Assam, were declared as ‘disturbed area’ for another six months.

The 1958 law gives power to the Army and the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) deployed in “disturbed areas” to kill anyone acting in contravention of law, arrest and search any premises without a warrant and protection from prosecution and legal suits without the Central government’s sanction. AFSPA is applicable in Manipur since 1981. Manipur, a former Union Territory attained Statehood in 1972.

New Delhi [India], September 25 (ANI): The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Friday extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (AFSPA) in nine districts of Nagaland and specified areas under 21 police stations in five other districts, declaring them as "disturbed areas", for another six months with effect from October 1, 2026.

The nine districts are Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren and Meluri, where AFSPA is extended.

The MHA made the announcement through a notification, considering the gravity of the situation in the state following an assessment of concerned security wing, an Intelligence Bureau report and a review of the law and order situation.

The AFSPA empowers the Central Government to declare an area as a 'disturbed area' under Section 3 of the Act where the use of armed forces in aid of civil power is considered necessary.

The latest declaration will remain in force for six months from October 1, 2026, unless withdrawn earlier.

124.title: Manipur Security Forces Destroy 3 IEDs In Ukhrul, Arrest 4 Militants With Arms & Ammunition
124.description: In separate operations, four militants belonging to different banned outfits were arrested from three districts of Manipur. Security forces also recovered arms and ammunition, including foreign-made weapons, from their possession.
124.text:
Manipur Security Forces Destroy 3 IEDs In Ukhrul, Arrest 4 Militants With Arms & Ammunition | X - Spearcorps

Imphal, Sep 25: Three Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) were safely destroyed in a joint operation by security forces in Manipur’s Ukhrul district, the Army said on Friday.

In separate operations, four hardcore militants of different banned outfits were arrested from three districts of Manipur. Arms and ammunition, including foreign-made weapons, were also recovered from the possession of the arrested militants.

IEDs destroyed in Ukhrul

Acting on specific intelligence inputs, troops of the Spear Corps, in coordination with the Assam Rifles and Manipur Police, detected the three IEDs in Ukhrul district.

Acting on specific intelligence, troops of #SpearCorps, in close coordination with #AssamRifles and #ManipurPolice, successfully neutralised three Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) in… pic.twitter.com/fUaxcUYsPD — SpearCorps.IndianArmy (@Spearcorps) September 25, 2026

According to the Army, the explosives had been laid with complex initiation mechanisms and posed a potential threat to civilian life and property. The security forces completely sanitised the area before carrying out a controlled in-situ demolition of the IEDs, thereby eliminating the threat, the Army said.

The successful operation highlighted the vigilance and operational readiness of the security forces, and the coordination among the Army, Assam Rifles and Manipur Police, it added.

Militants arrested in operations

The joint action is part of continuing efforts by the security forces and law enforcement agencies to prevent militant activities and maintain peace and stability in the region.

A Manipur police official said that four militants belonging to the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) and its political wing, the Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) and Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP) were arrested from Imphal West, Bishnupur and Kakching districts. Some arms and ammunition, including foreign-made, were recovered from the possession of the extremists.

The arms and ammunition include two Chinese hand grenades along with a detonator, one GLOCK 19 pistol with a magazine loaded with five rounds. One two-wheeler was also seized.

The arrested militants identified as Phandom Dinesh Singh (38) alias Thembung alias Wangba, Aheibam Silan Meitei (34), Okram Gobin Meitei (25) and Sanjenbam Abung Singh alias Krishna (49).

Also Watch:

Security measures continue

Meanwhile, the security forces comprising the Central and state units continue extensive crackdowns against militants, with search operations and area domination drives underway in fringe, mixed-populated and vulnerable areas across districts.

A total of 116 nakas/checkpoints have been set up across Manipur in both valley and hill districts, to curb the illegal movement of inimical elements and suspicious vehicles.

Security forces have also been providing escorts to vehicles, including trucks carrying essential commodities, along the Imphal-Jiribam National Highway (NH-37). Strict security arrangements and convoy protection continue in sensitive stretches to ensure the safe movement of vehicles.

127.title: Four Nagas killed in Kamjong amid fresh Manipur violence, AFSPA extended for six months
127.description: The killings near the Myanmar border came as Centre extended AFSPA in Manipur from 1 October, excluding 13 areas. 2 days ago, 41 Naga houses were set ablaze in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district.
127.text:
MHA has also reviewed and thereafter declared 9 districts and 21 police stations in 5 districts of Nagaland as “disturbed areas” for six months in effect from October 1.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Home Affairs Friday extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act 1958 in Manipur which will be in effect for six months from October 1, 2026, unless withdrawn earlier. The MHA notification observed Manipur as a “disturbed state”. However, AFSPA is not extended to 13 police stations including Imphal, Parompat, Thoubal, etc.

New Delhi: Four Nagas died in a cross-border attack in Manipur’s Kamjong district near the Indo-Myanmar border Thursday afternoon, the Working Committee of Tangkhul Naga Long (WC-TNL) has said in a statement. Two days ago, at least 41 Naga houses were set ablaze in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district.

A senior officer from the district of Kamjong confirmed the alleged killing of four Nagas in a cross border violence, however, he refused to divulge details.

The Naga organisation alleged that the members of the Kuki National Army Burma (NSA-B) and Kuki militants backed by the Myanmar-based People’s Defence Force (PDF) carried out the attack. “A Kuki terror group armed heavily with sophisticated weapons crossed the Namya River from Phailen Kuki village of Myanmar and launched a violent attack on Pilong civilians,” the WC-TNL alleged.

According to the statement, two residents were shot dead near the village, while two others were allegedly taken to adjoining Phailen and killed by the attackers. The organisation identified the deceased as Vareishim Jajo, Betterson Jajo, Phami Jajo and Ningthem Kashak.

Reacting to the incident, former chief minister of Manipur N. Biren Singh condemned the killing of four Tangkhul Naga civilians near Pilong village in Kamjong district and termed it “a matter of grave concern”.

“The victims, Phami Jajo, Ningthem Kashak, Betterson Jajo and Vareishim Jajo, were civilians who deserved to live without fear. It is especially heartbreaking as Phami and Vareishim Jajo were father and son. I also express my concern for Akhan Kaping of Ukhrul, who survived the attack,” he said.

“Such attacks and incidents of violence originating from across the border are not new. Border guarding must be professional, vigilant and strengthened, with security personnel stationed effectively along the actual border line, as is done in several stretches of the India-Bangladesh border in Assam, West Bengal and Tripura. The Government of India must accord greater attention to the Indo-Myanmar border, particularly in view of the ongoing conflict between the Myanmar military authorities and armed resistance groups,” his post on social media platform X read.

Condemning the acts of violence, Lun Kipgen, spokesperson of the Kuki Group Committee on Tribal Unity, said the Kukis in Manipur have no connection with the violence. “The cross-border violence might be perpetuated by Myanmar groups, which have no connection with us. This is a false narrative,” Kipgen told ThePrint.

Two days ago, in a 12-hour long spell of violence, at least 41 houses belonging to Naga residents and churches were burnt in Kangpokpi district’s Makui area in Manipur. Seventeen houses were razed in Makui Chamriupui, eight in Makui Thanamba, 16 in Makui Thebram and several other houses were also burnt in Naga villages Langka, Thanamba, Kapningching, Tajeikaiphun.

The Makui Village Authority condemned the incident, calling it a “direct attempt to wipe out Liangmai Nagas from the IT Road area” and grab ancestral land. It also further alleged that the latest violence was connected with the attack on 27 August, in which four villagers from the Makui area were reportedly killed in an ambush between Makui Ashang and Thanamba.

(Edited by Viny Mishra)

128.text:
News india Centre Extends ‘Disturbed Area’ Status Under AFSPA In Manipur For 6 Months Amid Renewed Violence

Centre Extends ‘Disturbed Area’ Status Under AFSPA In Manipur For 6 Months Amid Renewed Violence

Curated By :

,

Last Updated: September 25, 2026, 18:48 IST

The latest flare-up of violence in Manipur took place after suspected militants reportedly killed four people near the Myanmar border.

3 Quick Answers

Manipur is grappling with renewed violence as police struggle to rein in militancy. | File image credit: PTI

The Ministry of Home Affairs on Friday extended the “disturbed area" status under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958, in the entire state of Manipur, excluding areas under 13 specified police stations, amid renewed violence in the state.

The declaration will remain in effect for six months from October 1, 2026, unless withdrawn earlier. Notably, the Centre had designated Manipur as a “disturbed area" under AFSPA in 2023, which has been extended repeatedly.

Under Section 3 of the AFSPA, 1958, the Governor, Administrator or Central Government can declare any part or the whole of a state or Union Territory a ‘disturbed area’ if it is considered to be in a “disturbed or dangerous condition" requiring the use of armed forces in aid of civil power. The declaration is made through a notification published in the Official Gazette.

Why Has AFSPA Been Extended In Manipur?

The decision came as violence flared up in the strife-torn state, with four people allegedly shot dead by suspected militants in the Kamjong district on Friday. Their bodies, bearing bullet marks, were found at an isolated spot near the Myanmar border in remote Pilong village.

Locals alleged militants from neighbouring Myanmar crossed into India and ambushed a group of five villagers on Thursday. One of them managed to escape and alert local authorities.

Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh has condemned the killing, saying that “such acts of violence have no place in our society and will not be tolerated". He also conveyed his deepest condolences to the bereaved families.

At A Glance 1 . The government extended the "disturbed area" status under the AFSPA in the entire state of Manipur, excluding 13 regions. 2 . The declaration will remain in effect for six months from October 1, 2026, unless withdrawn earlier. 3 . More than 40 people have been killed since clashes broke out between Naga and Kuki communities in February

Manipur has been grappling with ethnic conflict that began in 2023 between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities. The latest cycle of violence began when armed attackers attacked three villages in Kangpokpi in retaliation for the killing of three Kuki civilians.

Four people, including a couple, were killed, and a six-year-old boy was injured in two separate attacks by armed assailants in Manipur’s Tamenglong district on September 13. A week later, a 17-year-old boy was shot dead in the Tamenglong district.

More than 40 people have been killed since clashes broke out between Naga and Kuki communities in February, according to officials.

129.title: Govt Extends AFSPA in Manipur for Six Months As Violence Continues
129.description: The extension comes amid continuing ethnic tensions, fresh clashes and renewed insurgent activity in the state.
129.text:
The extension comes amid continuing ethnic tensions, fresh clashes and renewed insurgent activity in the state.

The extension comes amid continuing ethnic tensions, fresh clashes and renewed insurgent activity in the state.

Representational image. Smoke erupts from the damaged remains of a house after suspected militants attacked a hill village, in Manipur's Kangpokpi district, Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. Photo: PTI

New Delhi: The Union government on Friday (September 25) extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) in Manipur for another six months, effective October 1, 2026. The Gazette notification of the decision cited the prevailing law and order situation in the state, reports PTI.

Manipur has been caught up in ethnic strife since 2023, when violence erupted in May 2023 between the Kuki and Meitei residents of the state. Around 43,000 people displaced in the violence continue to live in relief camps while several violent incidents have occurred over the last three years. There have been reports of over 700 deaths of residents of these camps as well.

The Manipur government stated in the state assembly in September 2026 that 306 people had been killed and 49 were still missing after the violence that contiued from May 2023 to August 31, 2026.

In recent months, a Naga-Kuki faultline has been emerging in the hill districts of the state. Human Rights Watch has reported that at least seven people were killed in clashes in late August this year, bringing deaths in such incidents to 34 since February. Armed groups have been reported as involved in shootings, hostage-taking, arson and highway blockades in parts of Manipur through 2026.

On September 24, suspected Kuki National Army-Burma militants reportedly attacked a village in Kamjong district near the Myanmar border, killing four Tangkhul Naga civilians, the Indian Express reported, citing police sources.

Advertisement

The latest AFSPA extension covers Manipur except areas under 13 police stations in five districts: Imphal West, Imphal East, Thoubal, Bishnupur and Kakching. The excluded police station areas are Imphal, Lamphel, City, Singjamei, Patsoi, Wangoi, Porompat, Heingang, Irilbung, Thoubal, Bishnupur, Nambol and Kakching.

The notification was issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs on September 24, under Section 3 of the AFSPA, 1958. The declaration will remain effective until March 2027.

Advertisement

Meanwhile on September 24, the proscribed Revolutionary People’s Front reiterated its demand for what it refers to as an independent Manipur, alleging the government of India has adopted military measures to suppress the armed movement in the state, reported Imphal Times.

Meanwhile, protests were held in Manipur by the opposition Congress party on the issue of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Friday.

131.title: Manipur: MHA declares majority of state as ‘disturbed area’ under AFSPA for 6 month from October 1: What does it mean?
131.description: The Ministry of Home Affairs has classified most of Manipur as a ‘disturbed area’ under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958. This notification, effective from October 1, 2026, will be valid for six months unless revoked by the Centre.
131.text:
The Ministry of Home Affairs on Friday extended the classification of most of Manipur as a “disturbed area” under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA), 1958, while keeping 13 police station areas outside its purview, according to the notification.

It will take effect from October 1, and remain valid for six months, unless the Centre revokes it before the period ends.

What is a ‘disturbed area’? Under Section 3 of the AFSPA, 1958, a “disturbed area” is an area officially declared through a notification in the Official Gazette where the situation is sufficiently disturbed or dangerous that the use of armed forces is considered necessary to assist the civil administration.

The law allows such a declaration when there are severe disturbances, violence or conflicts involving different religious, racial, linguistic, regional, caste or community groups.

Under AFSPA, armed forces personnel in a declared ‘disturbed area’ can:

Use force: After giving due warning, use force, including lethal force, against people violating orders prohibiting certain assemblies or possession of weapons/explosives.

Destroy armed facilities: Destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters or structures used for armed attacks, training or as hideouts.

Arrest without warrant: Arrest without a warrant anyone who has committed, or is reasonably suspected of committing or about to commit, a cognizable offence.

Also Read | Meet Bishworjit Konthoujam: Manipur pacer who removed Vaibhav in Duleep Trophy

Search without warrant: Enter and search premises without a warrant to make an arrest, rescue a person believed to be wrongfully confined, or recover suspected stolen property, weapons, ammunition or explosives.

The areas exempted from the “disturbed area” declaration cover 13 police station jurisdictions across five districts. These include Imphal, Lamphel, City, Singjamei, Patsoi and Wangoi in Imphal West; Porompat, Heingang and Irilbung in Imphal East; Thoubal in Thoubal district; Bishnupur and Nambol in Bishnupur district; and Kakching in Kakching district.

AFSPA extended in Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh In Nagaland, the Centre has extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) across nine districts — Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren and Meluri. The areas have been classified as “disturbed areas” under Section 3 of the Act, according to the notification.

The order also brings under AFSPA certain areas falling within the jurisdiction of 21 police stations across five other Nagaland districts — Kohima, Mokokchung, Longleng, Wokha and Zunheboto.

In Arunachal Pradesh, the extension covers the districts of Tirap, Changlang and Longding.

Also Read | NSCN denies role in ambush that killed two Assam Rifles personnel in Manipur

The notification further includes areas under Namsai, Mahadevpur and Chowkham police stations in Namsai district, which borders Assam.

The Centre said the extensions were made following a “further review of the law and order situation” in the three states.

NIA arrests in Aizawl Meanwhile, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested two Kuki student leaders from Aizawl in Mizoram, an official said on Friday, as per PTI.

According to the official, the duo were taken into custody from a hotel in the Khatla area of Aizawl on Thursday.

Their arrests came shortly after NIA personnel, with assistance from the Assam Rifles, detained United Kuki National Army (UKNA) chief Thangkhomang Haokip and his driver on the outskirts of the Mizoram capital, the official said.

Haokip, his driver and the two student leaders are currently being held by the NIA, the official added.

Haokip is wanted in connection with several cases in Manipur, while the specific allegations against the two student leaders were not immediately known.

132.title: Arunachal Governor stresses stronger civil-military coordination, highlights state’s strategic significance
132.description: Arunachal Pradesh Governor emphasizes strategic importance, calls for strengthening civil-military coordination to enhance security and development in the frontier state.
132.text:
Itanagar, Sep 25 (IANS) Arunachal Pradesh Governor Lt Gen K.T. Parnaik (Retd) on Friday underscored the strategic importance of the state and called for further strengthening civil-military coordination to enhance security and development in the frontier state.

The General Officer Commanding (GOC) 101 Area, Lt Gen Mohit Waghwa, called on the Governor at Lok Bhavan in Itanagar on Friday. A Lok Bhavan official said that during the interaction with Lt Gen Waghwa, the Governor said close coordination among the Armed Forces, state government, and civil administration was essential for effective disaster response and public welfare initiatives.

He also suggested enhancing transit routes, communication networks, and administrative infrastructure to support troop movement and border area logistics.

The meeting focused on logistics and administrative support, civil-military coordination, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) mechanisms in the Northeast, the official said.

The Governor commended the pivotal role of 101 Area, headquartered in Shillong, in ensuring seamless combat logistics and operational coordination across the region.

He appreciated the Command’s prompt and professional response during natural disasters, including floods and landslides, where timely rescue, relief, and rehabilitation efforts have brought invaluable support to affected communities.

The Governor urged the GOC to further strengthen welfare measures for ex-servicemen and Veer Naris, with particular emphasis on improving access to the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS), and empanelling of state healthcare institutions.

He also highlighted the importance of facilitating access to other welfare programmes, including resettlement and skill development initiatives, educational assistance for children of ex-servicemen, pension-related services, and reemployment of veterans, as provisions provided by the state government.

Lt Gen Parnaik (Retd) suggested regular awareness camps, medical outreach activities in remote areas, and closer coordination with the Rajya Sainik Board and Zila Sainik Boards to ensure that every eligible veteran and family member avails benefits and entitlements provided by the government.

The GOC assured the Governor about the Indian Army’s continued commitment to maintaining close coordination and extending all possible support for the security, development, and well-being of the people of Arunachal Pradesh.

--IANS
