156.title: Colin Gonsalves
156.text:
Awarded 2017

Colin Gonsalves

“For his tireless and innovative use of public interest litigation over three decades to secure fundamental human rights for India’s most marginalised and vulnerable citizens.”

Colin Gonsalves is amongst the most versatile and innovative human rights lawyers of his generation, fighting for the rights and well-being of India’s most vulnerable populations. He is a Senior Advocate at the Supreme Court of India and the founder of the Human Rights Law Network (HRLN), an Indian national network of public interest lawyers. Over three decades, HRLN’s lawyers have engaged in public interest litigation to hold the government to account and secure a broad spectrum of human rights.

Gonsalves’ work has focused on securing rights for India’s most vulnerable people, such as bonded labourers, ethnic and religious minorities, refugees, slum dwellers, women and the poor. His most significant victories in the courtroom include the 2001 “Right to Food” case, which saw India’s Supreme Court issue far-reaching orders enforcing a free midday meal for all schoolchildren. It also granted access to subsidised grain for over 400 million Indians living below the poverty line.

In 2016 and 2017, Gonsalves obtained landmark judgments from the Supreme Court that ended the longstanding immunity of the Indian Armed Forces from criminal prosecution. This has had a significant impact in reducing the number of extrajudicial executions occurring in India’s Northeast.

157.title: Foreign Nationals: A New Security Question for India
157.description: Sergio Gor visits Manipur during BRICS Just when the high visibility BRICS Summit was taking place in New Delhi, the US Ambassador Sergio Gor was touring India’s North-Eastern state of Manipur between 11-12 September 2026. He was perhaps visiting the region to familiarize himself with the State and see how the North-Eastern region could have better linkages with the US. But for security observers, his visit has importance. Here is a state that has been racked by violence and narco-terrorism and yet the US Ambassador chooses to visit and do some sightseeing? Things do not add up. The Chief Minister
157.text:
The challenge before India in Manipur is manifold; there is a weapons smuggling racket, high ethnic tensions and freely narcotics available. The usual route for narco-traffickers is China-Myanmar and then to India’s North-East. Myanmar is also the provider of substantial quantities of arms and ammunition, which is being smuggled into India. In September 2026, the police in Manipur recovered a haul of 328 illegal arms including AK-47s, and INSAS rifles with substantial amounts of ammunition. However, a different security challenge has emerged in recent years: the growing presence of foreign nationals allegedly involved in the movement and smuggling of drones into Myanmar and Bangladesh, posing a new concern for Indian security planners. Some of them are private military contractors with an American background, while many act on behalf of criminal groups, which engage in transnational narco-terrorism. While such cases remain scattered for now, the presence of foreign nationals involved in these activities warrants close attention, given the strategic sensitivity of India’s Northeast, and the US is known to be familiar with creating instability. The region’s complex ethnic, political and geographical fault lines make it particularly vulnerable to external pressures and instability. It is against this backdrop that the recent visit of Sergio Gor, the U.S. ambassador to India, to Manipur assumes particular significance—a state that has been gripped by violence and ethnic conflict for several years. The focus of this article is on the role and presence of foreign nationals in the north-east and the likely threat this poses to India.

Sergio Gor visits Manipur during BRICS

Just when the high visibility BRICS Summit was taking place in New Delhi, the US Ambassador Sergio Gor was touring India’s North-Eastern state of Manipur between 11-12 September 2026. He was perhaps visiting the region to familiarize himself with the State and see how the North-Eastern region could have better linkages with the US. But for security observers, his visit has importance. Here is a state that has been racked by violence and narco-terrorism and yet the US Ambassador chooses to visit and do some sightseeing? Things do not add up. The Chief Minister of Manipur Y.K. Singh subsequently tweeted: “We had the opportunity to discuss relations between the United States and Manipur. I am confident that the engagement between the United States and Manipur (India) will strengthen in the years to come.” The US is an interested party in the region, because of its interests in Myanmar and Bangladesh.

Sergio Gor’s visit to Manipur comes at a time when the state is caught in a wave of ethnic strife between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities. This has only escalated in the past few months with episodes of violence between Kukis and Nagas. The State Government estimates that at least 306 people have been killed, and 49 are still missing in Manipur, where ethnic violence had first flared up in May 2023, in the aftermath of a ‘Tribal Solidarity March’ organised in the hill districts, to protest the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribes status. From an American perspective, India’s North-East is important for US’s plans for Myanmar and Bangladesh, that is why Gor visited Manipur.

US interests in the North-East, Bangladesh & Myanmar

US interests in the region centre around support to the Bangladesh government under the BNP, with possibility of securing a military base. But more practically, it serves US interest if private military contractors, usually working for the State Department or the Pentagon to train, Bangladesh law enforcement and military officers. The other strategic objective is to train insurgent forces in Myanmar to fight the military-led government. Last year, the US established a military logistic base close to Bangladesh’s border with Myanmar. They also met representatives of the Chin National Front and the Arakan Army.

Individual Cases of US Nationals Analysed

The US is channelling arms and weapons to anti-government forces in Myanmar, including the Arakan National Army. There have been stray cases of US nationals involved in such activity. In August 2025, Nepal’s Immigration Authority arrested Daniel Stephen Courney, a former US Army veteran, on charges of unlawful activities for preaching Christianity and attempting to convert the locals. Of far greater concern was his alleged missionary work in Manipur in 2023, wherein he also was involved in supplying arms to insurgent groups. Social media posts surfaced online and revealed that Courney under the guise of humanitarian aid, had been distributing military-grade protective gear, including long-range surveillance drones (capable of operations beyond five kilometres), bulletproof jackets, combat helmets, boots, sleeping bags, and other military equipment to Kuki militants in Manipur.

The other more recent case is that of Matthew Aaron Van Dyke, who along with six Ukrainian nationals had been arrested by law officials, while they were transiting through Mizoram. Van Dyke and his associates were alleged to have been involved in the supply of drones and other equipment to insurgents fighting the Myanmar government. This must have been the Arakan Army. The firm run by Van Dyke, Sons of Liberty International, had been operational in Ukraine since 2022 and involved in training, which is also something they were doing in Myanmar, the new angle being Ukrainian nationals being his partners. After all, Ukraine has the expertise in drone warfare against Russia today. February 2026, a drone strike at Myiktina airfield on a Myanmar airlines ATR-72, passenger aircraft is suspected to have been carried out by insurgents using a drone supplied by Van Dyke and party.

Another case of a retired US Special Forces officer, Colonel Terence Averelle Jackson, Van Dyke, was involved in training and providing logistics in Bangladesh. Jackson had served with the 1st US Special Forces Command. Jackson, when he arrived in Dhaka stayed under the cover of Chief Risk Officer at Lee and Jackson Management LLC, with some reports claiming that he was a serving US Army officer. In fact, Jackson was in touch with another American national, Richard Daniel Roman, working with Makwa Global, who was also involved in training of Bangladesh Military officers at Rajshahi. Roman left Bangladesh abruptly a few days after Jackson’s death in Singapore. The reasons for Jackson’s death in Dhaka at the Westin hotel last year are still unexplained, but the fact that US officials took over his body and sent it back to the US shows the ability of Washington DC to pull strings when required.

This ability was again demonstrated in the reported meetings between US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Indian officials, including with the NSA, and Home Minister and according to tweets by Van Dyke’s family, it was this which eventually led to Van Dyke’s bail.

Jordan Brown, is another instance of a US citizen (later proved to be a UK national) who was arrested along the UP-Nepal border in July 2026, while trying to cross over into Nepal by the SSB. Strangely, Brown was carrying a Chinese passport, when arrested. At that time, he gave contradictory statements, claiming he had lost his passport in Thailand, entered India by sea and lived in Goa without any documents since November 2025. He claimed that he was going to Nepal to meet a contact. For a US citizen to be arrested on the border with Nepal, with no documentation and being bare chested seems highly unusual. The other twist came a little later, which showed that Brown was actually a British citizen and this was reportedly confirmed by the UK Embassy in Delhi.

The narrative that was spun by Brown, probably not his real name, was that he had worked with the US Green Berets and then married an Indian Yoga instructor in Italy in 2024. A UK national with a Chinese passport trying to enter Nepal and having lived freely in India since November 2025? What on earth is going on? It is probable that he lost his US/UK passport in Thailand and obtained a fake Chinese passport to travel to India. However, that needs to be proved. He could have got another passport from the US Consulate in Thailand. It also became apparent when Brown was sent to Tohar Jail on 19th September, that he had two other aliases, namely, Jordan Joseph Peter Fitzpatrick and Logan Miller. He allegedly escaped Indian immigration authorities in October 2025.

Airport Immigration FIR revealed his UK nationality

This fact is revealed by the FIR filed by the airport police, based on a complaint filed by an Immigration Officer, after Air India claimed the passenger had ‘disappeared’. Really? How on earth did that happen? Jordan Brown was a deportee who had been in custody in Thailand. Around 7.30 am on 28 October 2025, when he was waiting in the international transit area for an onward flight to the UK. That’s when he escaped. Why are officials in Air India not being held accountable? What was the CISF doing? Too many questions and too few answers? Here is a known criminal who is wanted in the UK for assault on a minor child and is alleged to have committed a crime in Thailand also. Petty criminal, but one who manages to evade law officers at IGI Airport. Quite unbelievable!

Worrisome signs

There have been several instances of foreign nationals becoming involved in illegal activities in India, including cases with links to the Northeast and Nepal. The case of Jordan Brown may, on the face of it, appear to be one of ordinary criminality. Yet the ease with which such individuals can move within India raises broader questions about gaps in surveillance, immigration controls and the country’s internal security architecture.

That most were apprehended thanks to alert police and paramilitary staff indicates that all is not lost. Intelligence officials say that in most of such cases, the US Central Intelligence Agency sends an individual under cover with a specific mission. Even the companies registered by these individuals could be a cover. After all the CIA established fake company in the 1960s just to obtain a sunken Russian nuclear submarine.

Therefore, India’s intelligence agencies would do well to do a thorough and detailed analysis of foreigners living or transiting through India. This will be useful in ascertaining the antecedents and whereabouts of all such foreigners living and working in India.

158.title: 60 Tourists Evacuated from Lachen After Five Days of Severe Weather
158.description: Around 60 tourists stranded in Lachen since September 23 were safely evacuated on September 28 after heavy rain, snowfall and landslides disrupted connectivity.
158.text:
GANGTOK- Approximately 60 tourists who had been stranded in Lachen, North Sikkim, since September 23 due to continuous heavy rainfall, snowfall and a series of landslides were successfully evacuated on September 28 in a coordinated rescue operation.

HINDI TUTION

The evacuation was carried out under the supervision of Mangan SP Rinzing Chopel Rai and Chungthang SDPO Chandan Chhetri, with the participation of the Indian Army, Sikkim government, Mangan district administration, disaster management personnel, police, local residents and social organisations.

Connectivity to Lachen was severely affected after a massive landslide at Chapten in Mangan blocked the main road leading to the mountain town.

With the principal route cut off, authorities also examined the possibility of using an alternative route through Lachung and Zero Point via Dongkya La. However, the route was itself obstructed by a thick layer of snow extending for approximately eight kilometres before Dongkya La.

Watch Video

The situation prompted the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and General Reserve Engineer Force (GREF) to begin clearing snow and landslide debris to facilitate movement and restore connectivity.

A coordinated mechanism was put in place to manage the evacuation and road-clearance efforts.

The operation involved the district administration, police, Indian Army, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), BRO/GREF and local institutions, including the Lachen Dzumsa.

The Station House Officer of Lachen Police Station and his team continuously monitored the situation and worked to ensure the safety of the stranded tourists.

Watch Video

District authorities also inspected affected areas to assess the condition of roads and identify possible routes for evacuation and restoration of connectivity.

Local residents and organisations played a significant role during the prolonged road blockade.

The Lachen Dzumsa and Pipon arranged machinery, fuel and other logistical support required for road-clearing operations.

Volunteers from the Lachen Hotel Association, Drivers’ Association, Lachen Tourism Development Committee and Lachen Youth Development Committee also assisted in the rescue effort.

Hotel owners and leasing companies in Lachen provided free accommodation and meals to tourists who remained stranded during the disruption.

Read More- Gurudongmar Lake: The most amazing place in Sikkim

Tea and meals were also arranged for tourists as well as personnel involved in the rescue operation.

One of the evacuated tourists, Nirmal Srivastava, expressed gratitude to the local residents and hotel owners for providing shelter and food during the crisis.

He said the support extended by the people of Lachen gave the stranded tourists confidence during the difficult period.

Following the successful evacuation, all the stranded tourists were transported safely to Gangtok.

Vehicles arranged by their respective travel agencies were used to take the tourists onward to their destinations from Gangtok.

Meanwhile, BRO and GREF personnel continued working to clear landslide debris and snow from the road leading towards Lachen.

Authorities expect connectivity to improve as restoration work progresses. However, travellers planning to visit North Sikkim have been advised to check the latest weather and road conditions with the district administration or relevant authorities before undertaking the journey.

The evacuation operation also highlighted the role of coordination between government agencies, security forces and local communities in responding to emergencies in the difficult terrain of North Sikkim.

The incident took place at around 6.30am near Nampong Nallah under Nampong circle, when personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles were patrolling an area where border fencing work is under way.

162.title: ‘Strong camaraderie’: Rohit Sharma opens up on Virat Kohli bond ahead of Guwahati ODI
162.description: Rohit Sharma spoke about his long-standing bond with Virat Kohli before the second ODI in Guwahati. His remarks underlined their continued exchange of batting inputs as Kohli arrives after a record-breaking hundred.
162.text:
Former India captain Rohit Sharma has opened up on his long-standing relationship with Virat Kohli, saying the two have shared a close bond since the early years of their international careers and continue to exchange inputs to improve their game.

Speaking ahead of India's second ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati, Rohit recalled how his camaraderie with Kohli developed during India's tour of Australia and has remained strong over the years.

The two made their international debuts within a year of each other, with Rohit making his debut in 2007 and Kohli following in 2008. According to Rohit, their shared journey at the highest level has helped build a mutual understanding of the demands of international cricket.

"Both of us, we've almost started playing at the same time. I made my debut in 2007; he made his debut in 2008. And since then, we've been trying to give our best for the team," Rohit said.

He added that the pair share a strong camaraderie and understand what it takes to maintain high standards in international cricket.

Rohit also dismissed the idea that Kohli's approach has changed significantly with their roles evolving over the years. He said the former India captain continues to be driven by the same desire to prepare well, score runs and win matches for the team.

"When he was captain, pretty much the same. When I was captain, pretty much the same. And I don't see any reason why anything needs to change," Rohit said.

The former captain also spoke about the mutual appreciation between the two and their regular cricketing conversations. He said they often discuss aspects of their batting and offer each other suggestions when they notice something that could be improved.

"At the same time, there has been a lot of discussion about how both of us as individuals can improve our own game. So, sometimes if something is happening with my batting, he comes and mentions it, sometimes I mention it," Rohit said.

While their conversations were once a regular part of life on tour, Rohit said the two now meet less frequently as they spend more time at home.

"Until a year ago, every 5-7 days we were on tour, so we didn't get much time at home. Now both of us are spending more time at home, which is always nice," he said.

Kohli, meanwhile, enters the second ODI in Guwahati after a record-breaking performance in the series opener. Chasing 296, he smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, hitting 10 fours and nine sixes as India secured a convincing victory over the West Indies.

The innings took Kohli past 15,000 ODI runs and brought up his 86th international century. His nine sixes were also his most in a single ODI innings.

The second ODI will be played at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati on Wednesday, September 30.

166.title: Assam Rifles NCO killed, four personnel injured in militant ambush in Arunachal Pradesh
166.description: A police official in Itanagar said that the patrolling party of the 21 Assam Rifles came under attack by suspected militants in Changlang district, which shares an unfenced border with Myanmar.
166.text:
Itanagar: An Assam Rifles havildar was killed, and four other personnel injured after heavily armed suspected militants ambushed a patrol party along the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district on Tuesday, officials said.

A police official in Itanagar said that the patrolling party of the 21 Assam Rifles came under attack by suspected militants in Changlang district, which shares an unfenced border with Myanmar.

The incident took place near Nampong Nallah under Nampong circle when the Assam Rifles personnel were patrolling the area where border fencing work is underway.

According to the Assam Rifles, the slain havildar was identified as Jangkhokai Kuki, 42.

The police official, quoting preliminary reports, said that the suspected militants opened fire on the patrol team, killing the NCO on the spot and injuring four others.

The injured personnel were shifted to a hospital for medical treatment, while details regarding their condition were awaited.

In the wake of the incident, additional security forces were rushed to the area, and a massive operation was launched to nab the fleeing militants.

There were reports suggesting that militants belonging to the NSCN-K-YA were involved in the attack but no official confirmation. Further details of the incident are awaited.

Changlang District Superintendent of Police Kirli Padu said that he had asked the officer-in-charge of Changlang police station to gather further details about the incident.

The India-Myanmar border in Changlang district has remained sensitive due to the movement of various banned insurgent groups operating in the region and across the international boundary.

Assam Rifles Director General Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera condemned the incident and condoled the death of the havildar.

"Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera, AVSM, SM, Director General Assam Rifles & All Ranks of Assam Rifles pay solemn tribute to Hav Jangkhokai Kuki who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty at Changlang, Arunachal Pradesh on 29 Sep 2026 and offer deep condolences to the family of our Brave Soldier. DG Assam Rifles & All Ranks of Assam Rifles stand firmly with the bereaved family," a post on the paramilitary force's X handle said.

168.title: India’s Himalayan Shield against China: Strategic Connectivity, tech & air power, civilian fusion to fortify security
168.description: India is calibrating multifront strategy to secure the Himalayas against China. This includes military, civilian & infrastructure fusion
168.text:
India stands amidst a volatile geopolitical latitude, with aggressive theatrics and unprecedented military postures being exhibited by the neighbouring players. Adopting heightened and utmost strategic prudence & operational readiness is thus a pivotal pillar of India’s national security playbook. As geopolitical gravity shifts to Indo-Pacific and the littoral actors emerge as increasingly assertive, it is fundamental to New Delhi’s foreign policy and military discourses to explicitly articulate an integrated and multidimensional strategic lexicon to fortify national security and territorial integrity.

As the grammar of contemporary great power politics rapidly oscillates with sheer unpredictability and the geopolitical basket of risks escalates, India is impounding its strategic propositions with significant salience, underscoring a realist approach for strategic deterrence, especially across the Himalayas to counter China’s aggressive military manoeuvres. India has adopted a multifaceted tactic to etch national security in the northern front, given the rugged and difficult mountainous terrain. From Doklam & Galwan in Ladakh to Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh, New Delhi is calibrating a comprehensive strategy as the shield against Beijing’s muscle flexing.

1. Swift connectivity, stronger logistics and strategic tunnels

India is calibrating a stronger connectivity fortress to seal national security across the strategic frontier of the Himalayas. All weather roads have been rapidly constructed to ensure critical supplies throughout the year, despite the wild conditions of the Himalayas. Helipads and landing zones are built at high-altitude regions, to ensure critical supply during unforeseen or combat circumstances.

For example, budget allocation to the Border Road Organisation(BRO) has multiplied drastically from Rs. 3,782cr in 2013-14 to Rs. 14,387cr in 2024. This will help scale up the road construction to the remotest regions and ensure last mile connectivity, upto Line of Actual Control(LAC). In this direction, road construction along the China border has doubled from 3,610kms to 6,806kms.

Apart from roads, India is also building railway lines to the border areas. This includes, Bilaspur-Manali-Leh line, which also has a dedicated military corridor. Not just Ladakh, even in Arunachal Pradesh, railway lines are drawn to the remote parts, to ensure security, sovereignty and integrate the people into the mainstream & empower them with economic opportunities.

Similarly, strategic tunnels are erected deep in the Himalayas to ensure swift connectivity throughout the year and integrate the units which were seemingly impossible previously. For example, the 13.15-km-long Himalayan tunnel promises all-weather connectivity to Ladakh while fortifying movement of military logistics and troops along the China border. This is the world’s longest single tube, bi-directional tunnel. This helps to keep operations and connectivity to Ladakh open, even during the harsh winters.

The Zojila Tunnel project is part of a mega infrastructure push by the Union government comprising 31 tunnels, 20 in J&K and 11 in Ladakh. This is aimed at boosting connectivity to the region and enhancing strategic preparedness. Once fully operational, it promises 365day connectivity between Srinagar and Ladakh while improving access to Drass, Kargil, Leh and the surrounding regions. Similarly, Atal tunnel, a high-altitude route provides year-round swift military logistics connectivity to Ladakh, by reducing transportation time by 4-5 hours.

2. High-altitude airbases and state-of-the-art landing ground

India is crafting a network of high-altitude airbases and advanced landing zones in the vicinity of Line of Actual Control(LAC). This helps in rapid deployment of troops, weapons systems and other critical supplies, even to the tricky landscapes. For example, Nyoma in Ladakh is upgraded into a high-altitude airbase at 13,700 feet. The airbase is capable of handling the advanced aircrafts such as the Rafale. Similarly, the Daulat Beg Oldi in eastern Ladakh is capable of handling Sukhoi-30 MKI, which is the world’s highest airstrip near Aksai Chin.

On the other hand, in Arunachal Pradesh, Pasighat, Walong, Ziro and even in the remotest regions such as Tuting state-of-the-art airbases are developed, which are strategically vital for national security and acts as India’s shield against China’s offensive military postures. It helps in rapid airlift of infantry, artillery and other critical supplies. They are indeed a boon to the long military logistical bottlenecks suffered by India in the dangerous terrains, but which were crucial from the security perspective.

3. Superior surveillance yields expertise in mountain warfare

India also has articulated a multi-layered, advanced, cutting-edge technology based surveillance system across the China border. This aids for real-time information, timely contact with the ground station, thus swift action and refuelling, to fortify national security. For example, the Indian Army has deployed 140-145 A-based surveillance systems to accelerate border security. These automated systems gain data from radars, thermal images and high-resolution cameras, which helps for early warning, detection and action in the strategic frontiers of Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh.

India also uses indigenous satellites of ISRO that aids precise surveillance. ISRO has deployed a multi-layered satellite ecosystem as the watchdog of rugged Himalayan terrain and sensitive borders. This includes CARTOSAT-2 and 3, EOS-05, GSAT-7, NavIC etc. which are popularly called the “eyes in the sky”. It helps to track infrastructure development, real-time positioning and troop buildup or any other activities on the Chinese side and if they are violating India’s territorial integrity.

Similarly, India has deployed many indigenous Unmanned Aerial vehicles(UAVs) or drones for real-time border mapping, monitoring and to ensure aerial supplies. India also has developed integrated command centres and frontline communication systems in the high-altitude tactical battlefields. As a state-of-the-art effort, India is also geo-tagging the critical infrastructure and regions in the high-altitude Himalayas to harness territorial integrity and national security.

Geotagging yields positional clarity and clearly defines the Indian territories boundary and keeps a vigilance over it through satellite communication systems and tech-based surveillance mechanisms. Such state-of-the-art tech aids strategic edge in high-altitude, mountain warfare amid emerging forms of non-conventional warfare.

4. Vibrant villages, civilian fusion & a holistic approach against Chinese threat

Yet another striking feature and key pillar of India’s strategy against China, is the development of the border & remote villages, which were previously ignored, isolated and remained detached from the mainstream. As the government repeatedly asserts, border villages are not the last part of India, but they are the first villages of India and a gateway to the country. Today, border villages even in the deep Himalayas and high-altitude provinces have better road connectivity, adequate supply of essentials round the year and other critical resources.

Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, the remote and frontier villages are developed as model villages to bolster national security. It is a strategic initiative to harness the border areas as a frontier community to seek national security against any threat. The villages are developed with all the amenities and critical infrastructure. This civilian fusion, coupled with military strength acts as a strategic impetus against external threats. The local residents act as “eyes and ears” of the intelligence, help in early warning and act as the first line of moral defence.

New Delhi has thus harnessed a multi-layered, integrated and holistic strategy against the geopolitical aggression of China. Swift connectivity, solid air and tech power, strong manpower who are expertised in mountain warfare, state-of-the-art infrastructure and the civil-military integration is redefining India’s strategic capabilities to seal national security and territorial integrity.

170.title: Assam Rifles havildar killed in Arunachal Pradesh near International Border
170.description: Assam Rifles havildar killed, four injured in an attack by NSCN factions near India-Myanmar border fencings in Arunachal Pradesh.
170.text:
Suspected extremists attacked Assam Rifles personnel patrolling the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), killing a havildar and injuring four others.

Officials said the incident occurred around 6.30 a.m. near Nampong Nallah, where personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles were deployed for patrolling amid the ongoing border fencing work.

Havildar Jankhokai Kuki, 42, was killed when suspected members of the National Socialist Council of Nagaland (Khaplang-Yung Aung) fired at the patrolling team. Four other Assam Rifles personnel were injured in the attack.

Assam Rifles captures two men from Bihar possessing firearms in Agartala

Attackers identities

Security agencies said they were trying to ascertain the identities of the attackers. Security forces launched an operation after the incident to secure the border stretch.

“We received information about the incident that took place along the India-Myanmar border and asked the officer in-charge of Changlang police station to collect information related to it,” the district’s Superintendent of Police, Kirli Padu, said.

“All ranks of Assam Rifles pay solemn tribute to Havildar Jangkhokai Kuki, who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty...and offer deep condolences to the family of our brave soldier,” said Director General Assam Rifles, Lt. Gen. Vikas Lakhera.

Several factions of the National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN) have been active in Changlang and two other Arunachal Pradesh districts — Longding and Tirap — for over three decades. These include the NSCN (Isak-Muivah) and the Myanmar-based NSCN (Khaplang), which later spawned the Yung Aung faction.

172.title: Assam Rifles patrol team attacked along Indo-Myanmar border, one jawan martyred
172.description: An Assam Rifles patrol team came under attack along the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district early Tuesday, September 29 morning, resulting in the death of a personnel, officials said.
172.text:
An Assam Rifles patrol team came under attack along the India-Myanmar border in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district early Tuesday, September 29 morning, resulting in the death of a personnel, officials said.

The incident took place at around 6.30 am when the Assam Rifles personnel were conducting a patrol near an area where fencing work is underway along the India-Myanmar border. The incident was reported near Nampong Nallah, under Nampong Circle of Changlang district in Arunachal Pradesh, along the India–Myanmar border.

The attack is suspected to have been carried out by cadres of the NSCN-K-YA (Yung Aung faction), according to preliminary information.

The deceased personnel has been identified as Havildar Jankhokai Kuki, 42.

Following the attack, security forces launched operations in the area to track down those responsible and secure the border region. Further details about the exact location of the incident and the circumstances surrounding the attack are awaited.

The incident comes amid heightened security along the India-Myanmar border, where fencing work is being carried out as part of efforts to strengthen border surveillance and security.

Security agencies are maintaining a heightened alert in the area following the attack.

173.title: SWACHH BHARAT CAMPAIGN OBSERVED IN AGARTALA MILITARY STATION
173.description: September 29, Agartala: Demonstrating its steadfast commitment towards cleanliness, environmental su
173.text:
Ministry of Defence

SWACHH BHARAT CAMPAIGN OBSERVED IN AGARTALA MILITARY STATION

September 29, Agartala: Demonstrating its steadfast commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and operational health readiness, the Indian Army's Spear Corps organized a comprehensive educational and awareness drive for troops stationed in Agartala on 29 September 2026 as part of the nationwide Swachh Bharat Campaign.

The day-long initiative aimed to reinforce the core values of cleanliness, personal hygiene and ecological mindfulness among service personnel, integrating environmental stewardship into daily military routine and garrison management.

The event commenced with a keynote address detailing the vision, spirit and national significance of the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026'. The talk emphasized that cleanliness is an integral component of military discipline, national pride and operational efficiency.

Dedicated interactive sessions were conducted on environmental conservation. Troops were encouraged to remain actively mindful of their daily actions and habits, highlighting how individual choices directly impact the surrounding ecology. Personnel were urged to adopt energy-efficient habits, reduce resource wastage and preserve local ecosystems.

Recognizing that healthy personnel are fundamental to military readiness, a clinical awareness session on Swachhta was also delivered by the Army's Medical Officer focusing on core operational pillars of Personal Hygiene, Sanitation & Cleanliness among soldiers.

Soldiers were also educated on modern waste management protocols centered around the core principles of Reduce, Reuse, Recycle and Recharge. Special emphasis was laid on reducing plastic waste, recycling organic materials and recharging groundwater reserves through rainwater harvesting units within military stations. An Army Official when contacted said, "Cleanliness and environmental responsibility are force multipliers that directly contribute to troop morale, health and operational readiness. Through initiatives under Swachh Bharat Campaign, the Spear Corps remains committed to leading by example in preserving our ecosystems and ensuring the highest standards of sanitation across all garrisons."

Spear Corps of the Indian Army is tasked with maintaining operational readiness and security across the North-Eastern frontier. Beyond its tactical duties, Spear Corps actively engages in nation-building, disaster relief, community development and ecological protection across the region.

174.title: Yung Aung-led NSCN/GPRN claims joint attack on Assam Rifles
174.description: NSCN/GPRN Yung Aung group claims joint attack with RPF on 21 Assam Rifles near Nampong in Arunachal Pradesh
174.text:
DIMAPUR — The NSCN/GPRN (Yung Aung group) has claimed that its combined tactical team with the Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) carried out a joint military operation against the 21 Assam Rifles near Nampong in Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh on Tuesday morning.





In a statement issued, the group said that the operation was conducted at around 6.30 am and claimed that one Assam Rifles soldier was killed and several others critically injured during the engagement.





It also claimed that its joint team recovered an AK assault rifle from the site.





The group described the operation as being in line with the groups’ “previously established understanding and commitment” to unite against what they termed foreign occupational forces and to defend their sovereignty.

175.title: 21 Assam Rifles Patrol Attacked Near Nampong During Fencing Work; 1 Jawan Killed, 4 Injured
175.description: One Assam Rifles jawan was killed and 4 injured after suspected militants fired at a 21 Assam Rifles patrol near Nampong Nallah in Changlang district along the India-Myanmar border during fencing work.
175.text:
Changlang: An Assam Rifles patrol came under suspected terrorist fire in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district early on Tuesday, claiming the life of one jawan and leaving4 others seriously injured. The security officials confirmed the incident, saying that the firing occurred on Tuesday morning, following which a massive search operation was initiated to hunt down the terrorists.

According to officials, the firing took place at about 6.30 am in the vicinity of Nampong Nallah, which falls under Nampong circle, along the sensitive India-Myanmar frontier. The security personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles were out on routine patrolling duties in the area when they were ambushed.

The officials stated that the patrol had been deployed in the border stretch where fencing work is currently in progress, making the timing of the attack particularly important for security agencies monitoring the frontier.

Search Operation Launched To Trace Attackers

Following the deadly attack, the security forces initiated extensive operations across the area to track down the assailants and to secure the vulnerable border segment.

Advertisement

The officials stated that the exact circumstances leading to the ambush and the precise sequence of events are still being pieced together. They noted that a clearer picture would emerge only after the ongoing ground assessment is completed.

The initial inputs received by the security establishment suggested the involvement of cadres belonging to the NSCN-K-YA, the Yung Aung faction. However, the agencies are continuing to verify and ascertain the identities of those who carried out the firing before drawing any firm conclusion.

Advertisement

Heightened Vigil Along Myanmar Frontier

The incident has led to intensified security measures and heightened vigilance along the India-Myanmar border in the region, especially in and around Nampong. The security forces are particularly alert given that efforts to strengthen border surveillance through the erection of fencing are presently underway.

The personnel have been placed on high alert and additional checks have been ordered to prevent any further attempts to destabilise the area. The focus remains on ensuring the safety of troops engaged in border management duties.

176.title: Lt Gen PC Nair addresses changing security paradigms in Northeast India at HDMC-22
176.description: In a significant address at the Higher Defence Management Course (HDMC-22) hosted by the College of Defence Management, Integrated Defence Staff (CDM-IDS), Lt
176.text:
In a significant address at the Higher Defence Management Course (HDMC-22) hosted by the College of Defence Management, Integrated Defence Staff (CDM-IDS), Lt Gen PC Nair (Retd), the former Director General of Assam Rifles, focused on the evolving security paradigms in India’s Northeast region. His insights highlighted the complexities of the region’s security landscape, particularly along the borders with Bangladesh and Myanmar.

Lt Gen Nair detailed the changing dynamics of the security situation in these border areas, emphasizing the historical underpinnings that have shaped the present environment. By delving into the rich historical context of the Northeast, he aimed to clarify the contemporary security challenges that these areas face today. His analysis not only addressed the immediate threats but also the broader geopolitical factors that influence the stability and security of the region.

During his presentation, he discussed the multifaceted interactions along India’s eastern frontiers, emphasizing the significance of understanding both the historical and geopolitical narratives at play. This perspective is particularly crucial given the intricate relationships and crises that manifest in border regions, which can have far-reaching implications for national security.

The address served as a critical resource for participants of HDMC-22, providing them with a nuanced view of the various factors that shape the security environment in the Northeast. Lt Gen Nair outlined potential strategic responses that could be adopted in light of these evolving threats and opportunities, underscoring the importance of adaptive planning and readiness within India’s security apparatus.

His call to action focused on the necessity for policymakers and military leaders to comprehend the shifting security paradigms, thereby facilitating proactive measures to address and mitigate emerging risks. By fostering a deeper understanding of these dynamics, Lt Gen Nair aimed to equip the next generation of military leaders with the tools necessary for effective strategic decision-making.

The interaction at CDM-IDS highlighted the value of experienced military leadership in shaping contemporary defense education and strategy. Lt Gen Nair’s forward-looking insights were a reminder of the strategic importance of the Northeast as India navigates its security challenges in an increasingly complex regional landscape. As these discussions continue, the emphasis on the historical and geopolitical contexts remains critical for understanding the future trajectory of India’s defense and security policies in the region.

177.text:
Guwahati: The Insurgent outfits NSCN (K-YA) and the Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) have claimed responsibility for an ambush on an Assam Rifles patrol team in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district that left one jawan dead and four others injured.

The attack took place at around 6.30 am on 29th September, along the India-Myanmar border, when the patrol team was moving through an area where border fencing work is currently underway.

The deceased personnel was identified as 42-year-old Havildar Jankhokai Kuki. The four injured crew members were taken to a hospital for treatment. Their current condition was not immediately known.

Changlang Superintendent of Police Kirli Padu confirmed on 29th September that security operations had been stepped up following the incident.

The India-Myanmar border in Changlang district remains a sensitive area, with officials citing the movement of insurgent groups operating in the region and across the international boundary.

Further details are awaited.

178.title: ACA Extends Support to Bordoloi Trophy; Nasir, Premananda Join APL Apex Council
178.source: The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People
178.description: Our Sports ReporterGUWAHATI: The Assam Cricket Association (ACA) has decided to promote football in the State by extending financial assistance to the Guwahati
178.text:
Our Sports Reporter

GUWAHATI: The Assam Cricket Association (ACA) has decided to promote football in the State by extending financial assistance to the Guwahati Sports Association (GSA) for organising the next edition of the Bordoloi Trophy.

The decision was taken at the ACA’s Annual General Meeting held at the 91 Yards Club at the ACA Stadium complex on Monday. The meeting was chaired by ACA president Taranga Gogoi.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Gogoi said the ACA would promote sports other than cricket as part of its broader initiative to contribute to the development of sports in Assam.

“Along with cricket, the ACA will promote a few other games in the state. Football is a very popular sport, and as part of our initiative to promote football, the ACA has decided to provide financial assistance for hosting the Bordoloi Trophy,” Gogoi said.

The meeting also deliberated on various aspects of cricket development in Assam, including player performances, ongoing projects, infrastructure development, player welfare and future plans to strengthen the state’s cricketing ecosystem.

Special emphasis was placed on grassroots cricket, strengthening coaching and youth development programmes, and creating greater opportunities for players at different levels.

The ACA also decided to establish six new academies across six zones of the association. Construction work is already underway, with the academies at Barpeta and Naharkatia reportedly nearing completion.

Meanwhile, the ACA constituted a new APL Governing Council for the 2026-27 term. Premananda Saikia and Nasir Gul Khan were inducted as members for a one-year term.

The meeting was attended by BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia as the Special Invitee, along with ACA secretary Sanatan Das, vice-president Romen Dutta, joint secretary Rajendra Singh, treasurer Anupam Deka and Apex Council member Mukutananda Bhattacharjya. The appointment of the auditor for the new financial year was also confirmed. Justice Manojit Bhuyan, retired Judge of the Gauhati High Court, was appointed Ombudsman-cum-Ethics Officer of the association.

Also Read: Mohit Sharma Set to Join CSK as Bowling Coach Ahead of IPL 2027

179.title: East Bengal loses to Punjab FC, will face NorthEast United in IFA Shield semifinal

Diego Raposo’s stunning strike from outside the box proved to be the difference as Punjab FC beat Indian Super League champion, East Bengal, 1-0 in their IFA Shield match in Kolkata on Wednesday.

The Red-and-Gold Brigade, which fans turn up in numbers at the East Bengal Ground, started with a team mostly comprised of first-time regulars, including new signings Chris Ikonomidis and Diego Živulić. However, Punjab, which entered the match after a 7-0 win over Calcutta Customs, continued its red-hot form with a narrow win in its final group-stage match.

The Indian Navy will bring 18 warships into service this year. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the news that these warships will be commissioned in 2026. At the Navy's Commanders Conference in New Delhi the defence minister said “this is a year for the Indian Navy”.

The India Meteorological Department says parts of Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and some northeastern states will face heavy rainfall. It also says there are expectations of thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds in areas.

The ministries will focus on making places cleaner, fixing pending work and making the work faster.

The United States has finally ended its military mission in Iraq, after a 23-year long US military presence since 2003. However, the concerns remain over the security and the potential influence of armed groups in the region.

The 81st session of the UN General Assembly is going to be in New York, with the general debate continuing through October 2. Topics such as Nuclear disarmament and international security will be the main topics of discussions.

Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep won women's team gold after defeating China.

182.title: Arunachal ambush: Forces step up hunt as NSCN/GPRN (YA), RPF claim responsibility
182.description: Security forces intensify surveillance after deadly Assam Rifles patrol attack along India-Myanmar border
182.text:
Imphal/Guwahati, Sep 30: Security has been intensified and search operations launched in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district following an ambush that killed an Assam Rifles havildar and injured four other personnel, officials said.

Additional security forces have been deployed in the area, while surveillance and area-domination operations have been stepped up along the India-Myanmar border.

The ambush took place around 6.30 am on September 29 near Nampong Nallah under Nampong Circle, when a patrol party of the 21 Assam Rifles came under suspected insurgent fire, officials said.

The personnel were patrolling an area where border-fencing work was underway when the attackers opened fire.

The deceased was identified as Havildar Jangkhokai Kuki, 42, a native of Maphou Kuki village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district.

He later settled in Nagaland and had served in the Assam Rifles for more than two decades.

Kuki was posted in the Changlang sector of Arunachal Pradesh when the attack took place.

Four other Assam Rifles personnel were injured in the firing and evacuated for medical treatment. Their condition was not immediately available.

Changlang Superintendent of Police Kirli Padu had previously said that police had received information about the incident and directed the officer-in-charge of Changlang police station to collect details related to the attack.

Meanwhile, in a significant development, the NSCN/GPRN (YA Group) and the Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) jointly claimed responsibility for the attack in a statement issued on September 29.

According to the statement, a combined tactical team of the two outfits carried out what they described as a “joint military action” against the 21 Assam Rifles near Nampong around 6.30 am.

The groups claimed that one Assam Rifles personnel was killed, several others were critically injured and an AK assault rifle was recovered from the site.

The claim could not be independently verified by The Assam Tribune.

The statement came after officials had initially indicated the possible involvement of the NSCN-K (YA) faction, although there was no official confirmation of the identity of the attackers in the immediate aftermath of the ambush.

Meanwhile, Assam Rifles Director General Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera, AVSM, SM, and personnel of the force paid tribute to Kuki, who was killed in the line of duty.

The attack comes amid heightened security along the India-Myanmar border, where forces have been conducting patrols and area-domination operations alongside ongoing border-fencing work.

183.title: NIA arrests two more over 2024 armed ambush on former Manipur CM’s convoy
183.description: In separate case, the central agency arrested Churachandpur man over IED attack that killed two minor children in Tronglaobi Awang Leikai
183.text:
Imphal, Sept 30: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested two more accused in connection with the armed ambush on the convoy of the former Manipur Chief Minister in June 2024.

The accused have been identified as Jangminlun Singson, alias Franky, 44, of Bethel in Churachandpur district, and Thangjoel Haokip, alias Thangboi, 21, of Gamphajang Tuibong in Churachandpur, the NIA said in a statement on Tuesday.

The agency said both men had previously been arrested in another case and were subsequently arrested in the present case based on evidence gathered during the investigation.

“Investigation of the case has established the involvement of the two accused, in association with other accused persons, in the planning and facilitation of the ambush and their linkages with others involved in the conspiracy,” the NIA said.

The arrests were made in connection with FIR No. 133(6)2024, registered at New Keithelmanbi Police Station in July 2024.

The two accused were produced before the Special Court, Manipur (for NIA Cases), Thoubal, which remanded them to eight days of police custody.

The two arrested persons are the third and fourth accused arrested in the case.

The ambush took place on June 10, 2024, near K Sinam village in Kangpokpi district when armed assailants targeted the convoy of the then Chief Minister.

Two security personnel sustained grievous injuries and government vehicles were damaged in the attack.

Manipur IED attack case

In a separate development, the NIA arrested a 48-year-old man from Churachandpur in connection with an IED attack on a residential house at Tronglaobi Awang Leikai on April 7, in which two minor children were killed and their mother injured.

The accused, identified as Thangmang Haokip, was arrested on September 25 and is the second person to be arrested in the case, the agency said.

The NIA had earlier arrested S Palal on August 12. Palal is currently in judicial custody.

The case was initially registered at Moirang Police Station before the NIA took over the investigation on April 23. The agency said Haokip’s involvement emerged during the course of the investigation.

Haokip was produced before the Special NIA Court-II in Imphal, which remanded him to 12 days of police custody.

The NIA said further investigation was underway to identify and arrest other persons allegedly involved in the attack.

184.title: Assam Flood: Indian Army launches ‘Operation Jal Rahat’
184.text:
The Indian Army has launched ‘Operation Jal Rahat’ to assist the Assam government in large-scale rescue and relief operations as worsening floods continue to affect several parts of eastern Assam, impacting thousands of people across seven districts, officials said on Monday.

Army and Assam Rifles columns have been deployed in the worst-hit districts of Charaideo, Sivasagar and Jorhat, where floodwaters have submerged vast areas, cut off villages and disrupted normal life, a senior official said.

The Indian Air Force (IAF) has been kept on standby to provide aerial assistance if the flood situation worsens.

Officials said Army personnel, working in coordination with the civil administration and disaster response agencies, have rescued several stranded residents from inundated areas and are continuing evacuation and relief operations.

The floods have also disrupted transport infrastructure, with railway services affected after floodwaters damaged and washed away portions of railway embankments. At least two breaches have been reported. Road connectivity has also been affected in several low-lying areas, while numerous villages remain submerged.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has deputed state ministers Bimal Bora and Susanta Borgohain to the affected districts to oversee rescue operations and assess the ground situation.

The state government has directed senior ministers and officials to remain in constant contact with district administrations to ensure the timely distribution of relief materials and rehabilitation assistance.

According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation deteriorated significantly on Sunday, with one death reported in Sivasagar district.

ASDMA data showed that more than 57,100 people have been affected across Charaideo, Dhemaji, Dibrugarh, Jorhat, Sivasagar, Tinsukia and Udalguri districts, up sharply from around 24,000 a day earlier.

Charaideo remains the worst-affected district, with nearly 24,000 people impacted, followed by Dhemaji with over 22,000 affected residents. More than 4,000 people have been affected in Dibrugarh, while flooding has also impacted parts of Jorhat, Sivasagar, Tinsukia and Udalguri.

Rescue teams continue evacuation and relief operations as authorities monitor the evolving flood situation amid forecasts of further rainfall across the region.

(With IANS inputs)

186.title: Army, BSF Hold Synergy Seminar in Shillong to Boost Border Coordination
186.source: The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People
186.description: SHILLONG:  A crucial seminar between the Army and the Border Security Force (BSF) was held in Shillong for better operational coordination.The "Army-BSF Sy
186.text:
SHILLONG: A crucial seminar between the Army and the Border Security Force (BSF) was held in Shillong for better operational coordination.

The "Army-BSF Synergy Seminar 2026" was hosted by the 101 Area of the Army's Eastern Command. Participants included senior officers from the BSF's Meghalaya, Guwahati, Mizoram, and Cachar and Tripura Frontiers.

The BSF is in charge of managing the 4,096 km border with Bangladesh. Of this, 856 km lies in Tripura, 443 km in Meghalaya, 318 km in Mizoram, and 262 km in Assam. The remaining 2,217 km of the border is managed by the South Bengal and North Bengal Frontiers of West Bengal.

The terrain through which the border runs makes management difficult. It comprises riverine, forested, and hilly stretches, where fencing is difficult.

According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, about 3,232.2 km, or approximately 78 per cent of the border, is fenced. There is little possibility of fencing the 174.5 km that has water bodies, marshes and dense forests.

Apart from intensive patrolling, the BSF now uses advanced surveillance equipment to keep a check on criminal activities and illegal immigration.

While the Army is not directly involved in management of the India-Bangladesh border, some of its vital installations and assets along the northeastern states lie close, requiring greater coordination with the BSF. (IANS)

187.title: India’s Strategic Fort for Siliguri: Underground military, rail & highway web—7 layered security amid external shocks
187.description: India is articulating a multilayered strategic architecture across Siliguri to fortify national security against geopolitical upheavals
187.text:
India is articulating a multilayered mega strategic architecture to fortify the vital Siliguri Corridor that bridges Northeastern India to the other regions of the country. Amid escalating geopolitical uncertainity and multi-directional threat, New Delhi is crafting the region into a more resilient strategic zone. Underground military infrastructure, additional railway capacity, alternative highways, border roads and new military installations, encompass the integrated approach to seal national security in the strategic chokepoint.

The emerging architecture is designed to ensure that disruption to any single route does not create gridlocks to the Northeast’s connection with the rest of the country. The state-of-the-art and critical infrastructure across Siliguri also aims to consolidate India’s territorial integrity against any external threats, particularlu from China and Bangladesh. The growing anti-India sentiments & security crisis in Bangladesh and China’s aggressive military manoeuvres raises apprehension, thus India is mapping a masterplan for Siliguri corridor, to contain security contingencies.

The strategic Siliguri corridor, critical for national security

The Siliguri Corridor is a narrow land link connecting mainland India with the Northeast. At its narrowest, the corridor is around 22 km wide and lies close to the borders of Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan, while China’s Chumbi Valley also lies nearby.

Its vulnerable & sensitive geography, bordering many countries, has made the corridor a longstanding strategic concern. The concentration of railway lines, highways, military facilities and logistical routes in a relatively confined area creates a potential vulnerability if any individual route is disrupted. India’s emerging response is therefore centred on alternative approach for critical circumstances. Instead of relying on a single road, railway or installation, the government is developing multiple parallel routes and protected facilities.

The result is an emerging seven-layer security and strategic architecture around the corridor.

1. Underground shield for ammunition and military assets

One of the most significant elements is the planned expansion of underground military infrastructure. According to details cited in various reports on the emerging plans, the Army infrastructure package at the cost of Rs. 297 crore includes

12 underground Army Air Defence ammunition storage facilities

One underground Long Range Vector ammunition storage facility

21 overground Long Range Vector emplacements

12 bomb shelters

Two critical storage spaces

Critical ammunition stocks housed underground are less exposed to threats, thus safe vulnerable surface installations. Such secret military infrastructures aids during unforesenn circumstances to thwart the atrocities of the adverseries.

The proposed infrastructure is also particularly relevant in a geographically constrained corridor where the loss of a small number of critical installations could have disproportionate consequences. The small passage also has limited space on the land for all critical installations and they are easily vulnerable. Thus, underground facilities are protective and space-economical.

2. Protected command-and-control network

The second layer focuses on keeping military decision-making and communications functioning during a crisis. Plans cited in reports include

Five underground command-and-control centres

Six underground communication centres

Three underground Long Range Vector ammunition storage facilities

The strategic purpose is not simply to protect physical assets but to preserve operational continuity. Protected command, communication and storage infrastructure could provide greater resilience if surface facilities face disruption from aerial attacks, drones, electronic warfare or other forms of conflict-related damage.

The underground component represents a shift from conventional surface-based military infrastructure towards a more distributed and survivable architecture.

3. Six line underground railway: A second lifeline beneath the corridor

Perhaps the most visible component of the multi-layered Siliguri strategy is the proposed underground railway. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced in February 2026 that special planning was underway for the strategic corridor, including underground railway tracks and expansion of the existing railway infrastructure.

The proposed underground alignment runs from Tin Mile Haat in West Bengal to Rangapani and onwards towards Bagdogra, thus connecting the entire stretch of Siliguri. Railway officials said that the underground tracks would be around 20–24 metres below ground. The project has subsequently been notified as a Special Railway Project. A July 2026 notification covers the Dumdangi (Tin Mile Hat)-Rangapani-Bagdogra stretch of 35.76 km.

This is not merely a replacement for the existing railway. The plan envisages expanding the existing double-line section into a four-line system while adding two underground lines. Once implemented, the strategic corridor would therefore have six railway lines — four overground and two underground.

The railway network aids both civilian connectivity and movement of defence logistics. If an above-ground section is disrupted by congestion, natural disasters or a security contingency, an alternative protected railway route would provide channel.

4. Highway web to reduce dependence on a single route

The railway push is being complemented by an expanding road network. The proposed Gorakhpur-Siliguri Expressway is another important component. The Union government confirmed in Parliament in November 2024 that the Detailed Project Report, including preliminary survey and alignment studies, was in progress.

More recently, the government has also announced a major highway push connecting Siliguri with Guwahati and Shillong, alongside work on the Gorakhpur-Siliguri connection. The broader road strategy is intended to improve connectivity into the Northeast while creating additional approaches to the strategically important region.

The strategic value of such projects lies in avoiding a confinment or being locked at single-point failure. Instead of concentrating movement through one road artery, multiple highways and bridges can distribute civilian traffic, logistics and emergency movement and also transportation of military assets.

5. NH-10 and lateral routes strengthen access towards Sikkim

Another component is the strengthening of routes leading from the corridor towards Sikkim. The planned upgrades to NH-10 between Sevoke and Rangpo, along with additional lateral links between major highways, are intended to provide alternative approaches for movement towards the Sikkim sector.

This becomes particularly important because the Siliguri region is not merely the gateway to the Northeast. It is also an important logistical base for movement towards India’s northern and northeastern border areas. Additional heavy-load-capable routes therefore provide greater flexibility for the movement of military equipment and supplies.

6. Border roads expand the security grid

India’s strategy also extends beyond the immediate Siliguri urban zone. The Fatehpur-Galgalia road forms part of the Indo-Nepal Border Road programme. Government records have documented the 79.5-km stretch and its implementation under the border-road scheme. Further proposals for Indo-Nepal border roads would expand connectivity and patrol access along the frontier.

This has a dual purpose. Better roads allow security forces to reach remote border areas more rapidly while improving the ability to monitor and respond to cross-border security challenges. The proposed connectivity along the Bhutan frontier also implies security and logistics concern, where improved roads can support swift movement towards strategically sensitive areas.

7. Strategic connectivity across India-Bhutan-China tri-junction

The final layer involves strengthening the broader military and logistical network around the strategic siliguri corridor. Plans for additional military establishments are aimed at improving access and response capabilities around strategically sensitive approaches towards Sikkim and the Bhutan frontier.

The Siliguri Corridor sits in proximity to the Sikkim-Bhutan-China tri-junction region, while the Chumbi Valley is located close to the Indian and Bhutanese frontiers. Consequently, resilience around Siliguri cannot be neglected or treated as an isolated infrastructure exercise. Connectivity towards Sikkim, Bhutan and the wider eastern Himalayan region forms part of the same strategic and security dynamics of India

Siliguri Corridor: Crafting a chokepoint into a strong security grid of India

The larger significance of the emerging architecture is that India is not attempting to protect the Siliguri Corridor through a single defensive measure. Instead, the approach combines underground infrastructure, multiple railway tracks, alternative highways, lateral roads, border connectivity, protected command facilities and dispersed military assets. The broader objective is therefore resilience and strategic deterrence.

If one highway is blocked, another route can carry traffic. If an above-ground railway section is disrupted, underground capacity provides an alternative. If surface military facilities are threatened, protected underground command, communication and ammunition infrastructure can preserve critical functions.

Rather than treating Siliguri simply as a narrow geographical vulnerability, India is developing it as a multi-modal strategic network to seal national security. The emerging Siliguri fortress architecture is therefore less about building one giant fortification and more about ensuring that no single road, railway line, bridge or military installation becomes vulnerable to external threats. India’s message is clear: a chokepoint becomes far harder to choke when it has multiple layers of protection and multiple ways through!

188.title: Imphal getting congested, Manipur CM wants sports complexes in rural areas
188.description: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on October 1 said the government wants to establish sports complexes in rural areas as Imphal becomes increasingly congested.
188.text:
Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on October 1 said the government wants to establish sports complexes in rural areas as Imphal becomes increasingly congested.

Singh made the remarks while felicitating weightlifter Saikhom Mirabai Chanu and Wushu player Naorem Roshibina Devi for winning silver medals at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

The chief minister said developing sports infrastructure outside the state capital would make proper facilities more accessible to sportspersons in rural areas.

He also said that if the law and order situation improves, the government could consider increasing financial assistance for sportspersons who bring laurels to Manipur.

Manipur already has provisions for sports infrastructure development in its 2026-27 budget, including allocations for sports infrastructure and the construction of astro-turf facilities in districts.

The proposal to expand sports facilities into rural areas comes as Manipur seeks to strengthen its sporting ecosystem beyond Imphal, which has traditionally remained the state's main hub for sports infrastructure and training.

OUR CORRESPONDENT

ITANAGAR: Insurgent outfits NSCN (K-YA) and the Revolutionary People's Front (RPF) have claimed responsibility for the ambush on an Assam Rifles patrol team in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district, which left one jawan dead and four others injured.

The incident took place around 6.30 am on Tuesday along the India-Myanmar border, when the team was patrolling an area where fencing work is underway, officials said. In a joint statement, the outfits said they executed the operation against personnel of the 21 Assam Rifles stationed near Nampong.

191.title: Havildar Jangkhokai Kuki Laid to Rest with Full Military Honours in Nagaland
191.description: Havildar Jangkhokai Kuki, a brave soldier who lost his life in the line of duty while serving in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district, received a heartfelt
191.text:
Havildar Jangkhokai Kuki, a brave soldier who lost his life in the line of duty while serving in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang district, received a heartfelt send-off during a solemn ceremony that took place in Medziphema, Nagaland. The event was marked by full military honours, highlighting the profound respect and gratitude the armed forces hold for their fallen comrades.

Senior military figures, including the General Officer Commanding of Spear Corps and the Director General of Assam Rifles, led the tributes, laying wreaths in honour of Havildar Kuki. These gestures underscored the soldier’s exceptional courage and dedication to his service, particularly in the challenging operational terrains found in the northeastern region of India, which has long been the focal point of security operations.

As family members, fellow soldiers, and well-wishers gathered to pay their final respects, memories of Havildar Kuki’s unwavering commitment to duty filled the atmosphere. His bravery in the face of adversity served as a poignant reminder of the sacrifices made by Indian soldiers who stand guard over the nation’s security.

The ceremony was a reflection of the wider appreciation for Havildar Kuki’s professionalism and selflessness. The armed forces acknowledged that his actions would not only be cherished but would also serve to inspire future generations of soldiers who take up the mantle of protecting the country.

As the final rites were conducted, the somber yet proud recognition of his service was palpable. The tribute marked not just the end of Havildar Kuki’s journey but also his lasting impact on those who serve. His name now joins the esteemed and noble list of Indian soldiers who have made the ultimate sacrifice for their nation. The memory of his dedication will continue to resonate within the hearts of his family, comrades, and the larger Indian society, ensuring that his legacy endures well beyond this day.

193.title: Two ULFA(I) cadres held in Arunachal after alleged plot to ambush security forces, plant IED
193.description: Assam Rifles, in coordination with Changlang and Tinsukia police, apprehended two suspected ULFA(I) cadres allegedly planning an ambush and IED attack along the Miao-Vijaynagar road in Arunachal Pradesh, officials said.
193.text:
Assam Rifles, in coordination with Changlang and Tinsukia police, apprehended two suspected ULFA(I) cadres allegedly planning an ambush and IED attack along the Miao-Vijaynagar road in Arunachal Pradesh, officials said.

The operation was launched on September 29 based on intelligence inputs regarding a possible attack in the area.

The two apprehended cadres were identified as SS Lance Corporal Sahdev Rai alias Bappi Akhom and SS Private Siraju Alam alias Shiraj Asom, according to the security forces.

An AK-series rifle, three magazines and 90 live rounds were recovered during the operation.

According to the security forces, the two men were intercepted before they could allegedly execute the planned attack. During questioning, they reportedly revealed that they were part of a larger group of around 20 armed cadres.

Security forces said the operation prevented a potential attack targeting security personnel and civilians and could provide leads about the group's network, operational methods and future plans.

Search and combing operations are continuing in the area to locate the other suspected insurgents, officials said.

The Miao-Vijaynagar road runs through the remote Changlang district and the Namdapha landscape. The route is strategically significant and forms part of the proposed Kharsang-Miao-Vijaynagar Frontier Highway (NH-913).

The Assam Rifles said the operation reflected the forces' intelligence-based approach and continued efforts to maintain security in the region.

196.title: Manipur CM discusses security, border fencing with Assam Rifles officials
196.description: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Thursday reviewed the state’s security situation and the progress of fencing along the
196.text:
Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Thursday reviewed the state’s security situation and the progress of fencing along the India-Myanmar border during a meeting with senior Assam Rifles officials.

Major General Gaurav Sharma, SC, SM, Inspector General of Assam Rifles (South), and Brigadier Pranav Prasoon, Deputy Inspector General of 28 Sector Assam Rifles, met the Chief Minister at the Secretariat in Mantripukhri.

The discussions focused on regional security and the ongoing construction of the border fence, according to details shared by the Chief Minister on his official social media account.

The meeting took place amid continuing security concerns in Manipur’s border districts, including Kamjong, Chandel and Tengnoupal, which share the international boundary with Myanmar.

In a post on X, Khemchand Singh said, “Major General Shri Gaurav Sharma, SC, SM, Inspector General, Assam Rifles (South), and Brigadier Shri Pranav Prasoon, DIG, 28 Sector Assam Rifles, called on me at my Secretariat, Mantripukhri, Imphal, today. We discussed matters pertaining to general security and the status of border fencing along the Indo-Myanmar border.”

Major General Shri Gaurav Sharma, SC, SM, Inspector General, Assam Rifles (South), and Brigadier Shri Pranav Prasoon, DIG, 28 Sector Assam Rifles, called on me at my Secretariat, Mantripukhri, Imphal, today. We discussed matters pertaining to general security and the status of… pic.twitter.com/gXeJ5w3Yr4 — Khemchand Yumnam (@YKhemchandSingh) October 1, 2026

Security forces have been maintaining surveillance along the frontier and strengthening their presence through additional forward operating locations.

Also Read: Manipur: Militant, student leader arrested in Imphal East over alleged kidnapping, extortion

The border areas also face challenges linked to the movement of people across the frontier, as well as concerns over arms and narcotics smuggling.

Last month, Manipur Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam informed the Legislative Assembly that around 55 km Indo-Myanmar border fencing out of 398 km has been completed. He also said that the state government is aiming to complete fencing of the entire border by 2028.

The minister said border fencing had become essential from a security perspective and that work is being undertaken to cover the remaining stretches.

197.title: Army backs youth through sports, skills
197.description: Army backs youth through sports, skills

Kohima/Pasighat, Oct 1: Assam Rifles, under the aegis of Spear Corps, continued its community outreach initiatives by supporting youth through sports, skill development and career-oriented programmes in Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh.
